department: Hawaiʻi Institute of Geophysics and Planetology
description: Professor Bin Chen conducts Earth and planetary science research at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa involving mineral physics, geophysics, high-pressure experiments, planetary interiors, and the physical properties of materials under extreme conditions. Chen's official opportunities information includes a dedicated section for high-school students and welcomes motivated local high-school researchers interested in laboratory experience. Students interested in high-pressure devices, diamond-anvil cells, large-volume presses, and related experimental techniques are encouraged to contact Professor Chen directly regarding research opportunities.

name: RAHI Research — Rural Alaska Honors Institute
title: Molecular Biology, Biotechnology and Biomedical Research Program
department: Biomedical Learning and Student Training Program
description: RAHI Research at the University of Alaska Fairbanks provides Alaska high-school students with an intensive residential research experience involving molecular biology, biotechnology, biomedical science, and university laboratory research. Participants complete research-focused training and gain experience working within UAF research laboratories while developing laboratory and scientific research skills. The six-week experience can also provide substantial college credit, combining academic coursework with exposure to active university research. The program offers a structured pathway for eligible Alaska high-school students seeking advanced STEM and biomedical research experience.

name: YuYe Tong — Tong Lab
title: Chemistry, Environmental Chemistry and Analytical Chemistry Research Prospect
description: Professor YuYe Tong leads chemistry research at Georgetown University involving analytical chemistry, environmental chemistry, electrochemistry, surface chemistry, spectroscopy, and related areas of experimental chemical science. The Tong Lab's official research opportunities information contains a dedicated section for high-school students and explicitly instructs interested students to contact Professor Tong directly regarding possible volunteer research internships. Prospective high-school researchers can submit information about their interests and academic background as part of the process. The laboratory also documents a history of high-school researchers participating across summers and academic semesters, providing strong precedent for sustained pre-college laboratory research.

name: Liang Tong — Tong Lab
title: Structural Biology, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Research Prospect
description: Professor Liang Tong leads structural biology and biochemistry research at Columbia University involving protein structure, molecular mechanisms, biochemistry, molecular biology, and biomedical science. The Tong Lab's official personnel roster includes a dedicated High School Students section and documents current pre-college research participation, providing recent evidence that high-school students can become members of the laboratory research environment. Interested students should inquire directly regarding current projects and mentorship availability.

name: Darren Rapp — Rapp Lab
title: Chemistry, Biochemistry and Chemical Biology Research Prospect
description: The Rapp Lab at the University of Oregon conducts interdisciplinary research spanning chemistry, biochemistry, chemical biology, bioengineering, and biomolecular science. The laboratory's official recruitment information explicitly identifies high-school students seeking research experience as prospective researchers and provides a dedicated High School Students Research Interest Form. The laboratory emphasizes research mentorship and supports trainees in developing scientific skills and pursuing their own research ideas. This provides an unusually direct and accessible pathway for motivated high-school students seeking substantive experience within an active university research laboratory.

name: O'Malley Pre-College Research Program
title: Business Research and Analytics Pre-College Program
description: Manhattan University's O'Malley Pre-College Research Program gives high school students the opportunity to conduct original business research directly with a university professor. Research areas can include finance, economics, marketing, management, accounting, and business analytics, with students working with real cases or data and developing a research project for presentation at a concluding symposium. The six-week program combines an in-person week in New York City with five weeks of online research and provides three college credits. This is a confirmed structured high-school research pathway rather than an unverified faculty cold-email prospect.

name: Research and Mentoring Program (RAMP)
title: Long-Term High School Biomedical Research and Mentoring Program
department: University of Maryland School of Medicine
tags: University of Maryland School of Medicine
description: The Research and Mentoring Program at the University of Maryland, Baltimore provides eligible Baltimore City high school students with a sustained biomedical research pathway spanning approximately two years. Participants begin with an intensive five-week summer research and skills experience, continue through research-related activities and rotations during the academic year, and can progress to an applied research experience during the following summer. The program is designed for participating 11th- and 12th-grade students and combines scientific training, laboratory exposure, research mentorship, and long-term engagement with university researchers. Geographic and school eligibility are restricted, so applicants should verify current Baltimore City requirements and application dates.

name: ENLACE Summer Research Program
title: High School Multidisciplinary STEM Laboratory Research Program
description: UC San Diego's ENLACE Summer Research Program provides participating high school and university students with direct experience in active STEM research environments. Eligible 11th-grade high school students are matched with UC San Diego research laboratories according to their scientific and engineering interests and work alongside university researchers on laboratory projects. Research areas vary with participating laboratories and can span engineering and other STEM disciplines. The program represents a confirmed high-school laboratory research pathway rather than general pre-college coursework. Students should verify current eligibility, geographic or partnership requirements, dates, funding, and application procedures for the applicable program cycle.

name: Melanie Morrison — Neuromodulation Imaging Lab
title: Neuroscience, Neuroimaging and Neuromodulation Research Prospect
description: Melanie Morrison's Neuromodulation Imaging Lab at UCSF conducts neuroscience research involving neuroimaging, neuromodulation, brain function, and related biomedical imaging approaches. The laboratory explicitly provides information for high school students and directs prospective high school researchers toward established UCSF research pathways including RISE, SEP, CURE, BAYS, and UCSF-SFUSD opportunities. This provides direct evidence that the laboratory is prepared to work with high school researchers through structured programs. Placement is not guaranteed through independent outreach, so students should apply through an appropriate current UCSF high-school research pathway and verify individual program eligibility.

name: Miriam Goodman — Goodman Lab
title: Neuroscience, Sensory Biology and Molecular Research Prospect
department: Department of Molecular and Cellular Physiology
tags: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program
description: Professor Miriam Goodman's Stanford laboratory studies sensory neuroscience and the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which nervous systems detect and respond to physical stimuli. Research includes mechanosensation, ion-channel function, sensory neurons, neurobiology, and related molecular and physiological questions. The Goodman Lab explicitly states that it primarily hosts high school researchers during the summer and directs interested high school students toward Stanford's SIMR program. This provides documented high-school research precedent within the specific laboratory, although students should pursue the structured Stanford program rather than assume independent placement through direct outreach.

name: Karatsoreos Lab Research Intensive
title: High School Circadian Neuroscience and Stress Biology Research Intensive
department: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
description: The Karatsoreos Lab Research Intensive at UMass Amherst gives rising high school juniors and seniors six weeks of full-time experience in an active neuroscience and behavioral research environment. Research focuses on circadian rhythms, biological timing, stress systems, neural communication, metabolism, immune function, and relationships between physiology and behavior. Participants assist faculty and graduate researchers with ongoing work and develop a final research poster. The laboratory hosts only a very small number of high school researchers, making the experience unusually focused, although the substantial tuition and residential costs reduce accessibility compared with funded research internships.

name: Karlstrom Lab Research Intensive
title: High School Developmental Neuroscience and Zebrafish Research Intensive
description: The Karlstrom Lab Research Intensive at UMass Amherst places high school students into an active developmental neuroscience laboratory studying brain development and neural stem cells using zebrafish as a model organism. Participants can gain experience with techniques including brain dissection, confocal microscopy, fluorescent transgenic zebrafish, genetics, imaging, and experimental manipulation. Students contribute to ongoing laboratory research and may help develop research questions or projects under university mentorship. The program hosts only a small cohort of high school researchers and culminates in scientific presentation of the students' work.

name: You Lab Research Intensive
title: High School Nucleic Acid Chemistry and Bioengineering Research Intensive
department: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: The You Lab Research Intensive at UMass Amherst gives a very small number of high school students the opportunity to contribute to ongoing research in nucleic acid chemistry, chemical biology, and molecular bioengineering. Research topics can include fluorescent RNA sensors, DNA nanostructures, nucleic-acid-based engineering, targeted delivery to cancer cells, and interactions involving membrane proteins. Students work in an active university research environment alongside faculty and graduate researchers and complete a scientific poster describing their work. The laboratory hosts up to approximately two high school researchers through the structured UMass Research Intensives pathway.

name: Zhou Lin Group Quantum Chemistry Research Intensive
title: High School Computational and Quantum Chemistry Research Intensive
description: The Zhou Lin Group Quantum Chemistry Research Intensive at UMass Amherst provides an exceptionally small high school research placement in computational and theoretical chemistry. The participating student assists university researchers with ongoing work involving quantum chemistry, electronic structure, quantum dynamics, photochemistry, photocatalysis, materials, and related molecular problems. The experience introduces the student to how computational and quantum-mechanical methods are used to investigate chemical systems and culminates in a research poster. The listed intensive hosts approximately one high school student, making it a highly individualized research environment.

name: Fusarium Genomics Lab Research Intensive — Ma Lab
title: High School Fungal Genomics and Plant Biology Research Intensive
department: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: The Fusarium Genomics Lab Research Intensive at UMass Amherst gives high school students hands-on experience investigating interactions between fungal pathogens and plants. Research uses systems including Fusarium and Arabidopsis and can incorporate genomics, bioinformatics, microbiology, plant experiments, microfluidics, automated phenotyping, and quantitative analysis. Participants contribute to ongoing laboratory research alongside university researchers and develop a scientific poster describing their work. The structured intensive hosts a small cohort of high school researchers and provides direct exposure to both experimental and computational approaches in modern genomics and plant biology.

name: ResearcHStart
title: Multi-Institutional High School Cancer Research Internship
university: University of Chicago / University of Illinois Chicago / Northwestern University / Rush University / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
department: Cancer Research Centers and Affiliated Research Laboratories
description: ResearcHStart is a multi-institutional high-school cancer research program involving the University of Chicago, University of Illinois Cancer Center at UIC, Northwestern University, Rush University, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Students gain hands-on cancer research experience in faculty laboratories and complete independent research projects while also participating in workshops, lectures, and professional-development activities. At the UIC Cancer Center site, the 2026 program lasted eight weeks from June 15 through August 7, with students working approximately 35 to 40 hours per week. Participants conclude their research experience by presenting their work at a student research symposium. Research exposure can include biophysics, biochemistry, immunology, pharmacology, molecular biology, and related areas of cancer science.

name: Cancer Health Engagement Summer Scholars (CHESS)
title: High School Cancer Research and Health Professions Summer Program
department: University of Illinois Cancer Center / Urban Health Program
description: The Cancer Health Engagement Summer Scholars program is an eight-week summer program operated through the University of Illinois Cancer Center and UIC Urban Health Program. CHESS trains and mentors high-school students interested in cancer research and other health professions. The program provides structured exposure to biomedical and cancer research while developing students' research, academic, and professional skills. CHESS and ResearcHStart share a summer curriculum and schedule at the Cancer Center but are distinct programs with different eligibility criteria and administrative structures.

name: Summer Program for Research Interns (SPRI)
title: Six-Week High School Faculty-Mentored Research Internship
department: Clemson University Honors College / South Carolina Governor's School for Science and Mathematics
description: Clemson University's Summer Program for Research Interns is a six-week intensive research experience operated in partnership with the South Carolina Governor's School for Science and Mathematics. The program is specifically for GSSM students, who join university or corporate research groups during the summer between their junior and senior years. Participants work closely with research mentors and later analyze their findings, prepare formal research papers, and present at the GSSM Annual Research Colloquium and South Carolina Junior Academy of Science meeting. Clemson projects have included bioengineering, plant and environmental science, electrical and computer engineering, robotics, and other fields. This is a highly substantive research pathway but is restricted to students participating through GSSM.

name: CTAHR Summer Research Institute (SRI)
title: Eight-Week Faculty-Mentored High School and Undergraduate Research Program
department: College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resilience
description: The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resilience Summer Research Institute is an eight-week research program for high-school and undergraduate students from Hawaiʻi. Each student is assigned a faculty mentor and conducts original scientific research addressing real-world problems in areas such as food systems, agriculture, environmental sustainability, resilience, invasive species, and related fields. Students spend approximately 25 hours per week conducting laboratory, field, and/or library-based research while learning how to formulate research questions, gather and analyze data, evaluate research ethics, and communicate scientific findings. The program concludes with student research posters and presentations.

name: MasterScholar UCSB Summer Research Program
title: Interdisciplinary High School Sustainability and Engineering Research Program
description: The MasterScholar UCSB Summer Research Program is a three-week pre-college research experience for high-school students interested in sustainability, engineering, and environmental science. Students conduct research in a university setting under expert guidance and select concentrations that can intersect with data science, economics, humanities, and social sciences. Participants work in teams to develop research questions, investigate their topics from multiple disciplinary perspectives, and build specialized knowledge through the research process. Students conclude the program by formally presenting their findings and scholarly contributions.

name: Project NePTWNE Regional Summer School of Excellence (RiSSE)
title: Free High School Environmental Science and Freshwater Research Program
department: Project NePTWNE / Center for Environmental Research and Education
description: Gannon University's Project NePTWNE Regional Summer School of Excellence is a free weeklong residential environmental science program for students entering grades 9 through 12. Participants work alongside Gannon faculty, staff, and student mentors while investigating the Lake Erie watershed through authentic field and laboratory research. Activities include collecting macroinvertebrates, fish, and water-quality samples, conducting laboratory analyses, investigating coastal erosion, analyzing environmental data, and studying freshwater ecosystems. Students develop scientific findings and environmental recommendations and conclude the program by presenting their research. The program emphasizes field methods, data collection, water-quality monitoring, ecological research, and scientific communication.

name: Explore Engineering Summer Program
title: High School Sustainable Engineering Research Experience
university: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry
description: SUNY ESF's Explore Engineering Summer Program is a residential experience for rising high-school seniors focused on engineering, sustainability, and research. Students engage directly with ESF faculty and graduate students and collaborate on hands-on research projects addressing real-world challenges. Program topics include renewable resources, materials innovation, environmental protection, waste reduction, sustainability, and related engineering fields. The inaugural 2026 program brought 35 students to the SUNY ESF campus for an immersive week of engineering research, university life, and exploration of engineering careers.

name: Online Research Academy
title: Virtual Faculty-Mentored High School Research Program
university: North Carolina State University / University of North Carolina Wilmington
description: NC State's Online Research Academy is a four-week virtual interdisciplinary research program for high-school students in grade 10 or above. Participants learn fundamental research methodologies and apply them to a dedicated research project while receiving mentorship from faculty associated with North Carolina State University and the University of North Carolina Wilmington. Students meet online with a faculty mentor twice each week throughout the program. Upon successful completion, participants receive a graduation certificate and a performance evaluation letter from their professor. The online format makes the program accessible to students beyond North Carolina while still providing direct faculty research mentorship.

name: Summer High-School Internships in Research Experiences (SHIRE)
title: Paid High School Pharmacology and Sustainable Engineering Research Internship
department: Collaborative for STEM Education and Outreach
description: Vanderbilt University's Summer High-School Internships in Research Experiences program is a paid research internship for rising juniors and seniors participating in Vanderbilt's Interdisciplinary Science and Research program at eligible partner high schools. Students work with scientists from Vanderbilt's Collaborative for STEM Education and Outreach and educators from their ISR schools on authentic research questions. In 2026, rising juniors investigated pharmacology and sustainable engineering through work involving areas such as cell culture and water quality, while rising seniors developed individual research projects designed to continue during the fall semester. Participants work approximately 28 hours per week and can receive academic credit in addition to compensation through the POWER Youth partnership. This is a substantive research opportunity but is restricted to students already participating in Vanderbilt's ISR pathway.

name: Brown Cancer Center High School Summer Research Program
title: High School Cancer Biology and Drug Discovery Research Program
description: The Brown Cancer Center High School Summer Research Program at the University of Louisville provides high school students with intensive hands-on experience in cancer research. The 2026 program began with approximately two weeks of laboratory and drug-discovery training before students transitioned into seven-week individual research placements mentored by Brown Cancer Center faculty. Participants commit at least 30 hours per week and work directly within active research environments rather than completing only classroom-based enrichment. The program provides exposure to experimental cancer biology, biomedical laboratory methods, drug discovery, scientific investigation, and faculty mentorship.

name: School of Engineering & Computing Summer Research Residency
title: Faculty-Mentored Engineering, Computing and AI Summer Research Residency
description: Fairfield University's School of Engineering and Computing Summer Research Residency brings high school, undergraduate, and graduate students into faculty-mentored engineering and computing research. The 2026 residency ran for eight weeks and included more than 30 research projects spanning areas such as artificial intelligence, quantum circuits, autonomous-vehicle LiDAR, biomedical engineering, advanced manufacturing, computing, and other engineering disciplines. Participants work within university research teams and communicate their findings through a concluding research poster symposium. Fairfield has explicitly documented high school students participating alongside university researchers, making this a confirmed high-school research pathway rather than a speculative faculty prospect.

name: You Zhou — Quantum Materials & Nanophotonics Research Group
title: Quantum Materials, Nanophotonics and Condensed Matter Research Prospect
department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Professor You Zhou's research group at the University of Maryland studies quantum materials, nanophotonics, condensed-matter physics, and related materials phenomena using approaches that can include materials synthesis, nanofabrication, electronic measurements, cryogenic optical experiments, and programming. The group's official roster documents former high school researchers, providing direct evidence that high school students have previously participated in the laboratory. The group also advertises opportunities for students, but it does not guarantee a currently available high-school position. This listing is therefore a direct-inquiry professor prospect with documented high-school research precedent rather than a formal high-school program.

name: Goldman Group / LEEDAR Summer Research Program
title: High School Chemistry, Catalysis and Energy Research Program
department: Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology
description: The Goldman Group / LEEDAR Summer Research Program at Rutgers University's Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology provides high school juniors and seniors with direct experience in an active university chemistry research environment. Participants typically spend approximately six to eight weeks working closely with Rutgers faculty members and graduate researchers and become involved in a specific laboratory research project. The Goldman Group's research includes catalysis, organometallic chemistry, energy-related chemical transformations, and fundamental molecular chemistry. Rutgers explicitly identifies high school juniors and seniors as participants in the summer research program, making this a confirmed laboratory-based high-school research opportunity.

name: YES in THE HEIGHTS
title: Eight-Week High School Cancer Research and Mentorship Program
description: YES in THE HEIGHTS is a high school cancer research and mentorship program at Columbia University's Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center. High school participants commit to an eight-week summer experience working with a cancer research group and receive hands-on exposure to biomedical and cancer research with personalized mentorship. The 2026 high school program ran from June 29 through August 21. Columbia announced in August 2026 that YES in THE HEIGHTS joined the NYC Science Research Mentoring Consortium, further establishing the program as a structured New York City high-school research pathway.

name: You Chen — OHPEN Lab
title: Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Informatics and Health Data Research Prospect
description: Professor You Chen's OHPEN Lab at Vanderbilt University Medical Center conducts computational biomedical research involving artificial intelligence for healthcare, graph-based AI, electronic health record data, drug safety, therapeutic discovery, clinical informatics, and biomedical data science. The laboratory's official recruiting materials document mentorship of high school researchers and note that some student researchers have produced first-author publications. The group's current and historical rosters also document high-school participation, providing unusually strong evidence of genuine pre-college research involvement. This is not a guaranteed formal high-school internship, so interested students should directly inquire about current projects, preparation requirements, remote or in-person possibilities, and mentor availability.

name: Joseph Henry Project
title: High School Physics, Engineering and Computational Modeling Research Prospect
description: Princeton University's Joseph Henry Project provides a research environment centered on physics, engineering, electromagnetic systems, computational modeling, simulation, and related experimental work. Princeton's official project page documents multiple high school interns in recent cohorts, including several high school participants in 2026 and additional high school researchers in previous years. Student projects have involved areas such as electromagnetic devices, engineering experimentation, computational simulation, and COMSOL modeling. Because the project page demonstrates substantial high-school participation but does not advertise a universal high-school application process, this listing should be treated as an open-inquiry research prospect with documented high-school precedent rather than a guaranteed formal internship.

name: Research Internships in Materials Science (RIMS)
title: Paid High School Artificial Intelligence and Materials Science Research Internship
description: Research Internships in Materials Science is an eight-week paid internship for New York City high school students associated with Cornell University's Artificial Intelligence Materials Institute. The NSF-supported institute integrates artificial intelligence with materials science and materials discovery, creating research at the intersection of machine learning, chemistry, physics, computation, and materials engineering. Cornell explicitly identifies RIMS as a paid high-school internship and part of the institute's education and workforce-development efforts. The program is particularly distinctive for students interested in applying artificial intelligence and computational approaches to experimental and theoretical materials research.

name: Jinglin Fu — Bio-Mimetic Design & Nanoscience Lab
title: DNA Nanotechnology, Biosensing and Bionanotechnology Research Prospect
description: Professor Jinglin Fu's Bio-Mimetic Design & Nanoscience Lab at Rutgers University–Camden studies DNA nanotechnology, molecular sensing, biomolecular self-assembly, biosensing, nanomedicine, and related chemical and biological nanotechnology. The laboratory's official group roster documents current and former high school researchers, including a 2026 high school student conducting virtual research as well as previous students participating through programs such as HSAP and REAP. Rutgers has also documented Fu mentoring high school research involving DNA nanotechnology and biosensing. These records provide strong evidence of genuine high-school participation, but independent placement is not guaranteed; students should directly inquire about current research projects, mentorship capacity, and possible in-person or virtual participation.

name: Avian Physiology Research Intensive — Gerson Lab
title: High School Avian Physiology, Migration and Ecophysiology Research Intensive
description: The Avian Physiology Research Intensive in the Gerson Lab at UMass Amherst gives a very small number of high school students six weeks of experience in an active animal physiology and ecophysiology laboratory. The Gerson Lab investigates how birds cope physiologically with demanding environmental conditions and long-distance migration, connecting cellular and physiological mechanisms with whole-animal biology and ecology. Participants contribute to ongoing university research alongside laboratory researchers and develop a scientific poster describing their work. The intensive hosts up to approximately two high school students, creating a highly focused research environment.

name: Yale Neuroscience Summer Scholars (YNSS)
title: Eight-Week High School Neuroscience Research Program
department: Yale School of Medicine / Department of Pathology
description: The Yale Neuroscience Summer Scholars Program provides students from New Haven Public Schools with an eight-week research experience in neuroscience, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation. Scholars receive didactic neuroscience education and hands-on laboratory training before completing a supervised research project. Participants gain experience reviewing scientific literature, conducting laboratory research, writing research summaries, and presenting scientific findings while interacting with Yale undergraduate, graduate, medical, and research trainees. Four New Haven public high school students completed the competitive 2026 program. Eligibility is geographically restricted to students from New Haven Public Schools.

name: Boston University Lab Apprenticeship in Science & Technology (BLAST)
title: Paid High School Biomedical Research Training and Laboratory Apprenticeship
description: Boston University Lab Apprenticeship in Science & Technology is a paid two-summer biomedical research pathway for eligible high school students. The first summer emphasizes problem-based learning, laboratory practicums, scientific literacy, and preparation for college-level science while connecting students with undergraduate, graduate, and medical student mentors. Students who progress through the pathway engage in immersive research projects within Boston University Medical Campus laboratories during the second summer under investigators committed to research mentorship. The inaugural 2026 first-summer session ran for six weeks from July 6 through August 14, Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. The program is associated with BU's BEAMS initiative and is supported by an NIH grant.

name: Chemical Engineering Experience in Research (ChEER) for Youth Interns
title: High School Chemical Engineering Laboratory Research Internship
description: The Chemical Engineering Experience in Research for Youth Interns at the University of Kansas gives high school students ages 15 to 18 direct experience conducting non-hazardous research in university chemical engineering laboratories. Youth interns work under graduate-student or postdoctoral mentorship, participate in research-team meetings, analyze and present their own data, and receive laboratory safety and professional-development training. The 2026 program ran for four weeks at 20 hours per week, with projects including sustainable polymers and membrane technologies for refrigerant separation. The internship is unpaid and intended for students who can commute locally because housing and travel support are not provided.

name: High School Student Research Program
title: Faculty-Mentored High School Authentic Research Program
description: St. Bonaventure University's High School Student Research Program pairs high school students with university faculty to work on authentic research projects. Participants receive close faculty mentorship on a cutting-edge topic and conclude the experience by presenting their own research poster. Recent research areas span biochemistry, bioinformatics, biopsychology, computational chemistry, developmental biology, digital humanities, mathematics and computer-aided design, engineering, mental health and media, human-computer interaction, molecular genetics, and theology. The program has operated since 2015, and the 2026 session lasted two weeks. Current eligibility and research areas should be checked for each summer cycle.

name: High School Summer Research — Department of Chemistry
title: High School Faculty-Mentored Chemistry Laboratory Research Program
description: Saint Louis University's Department of Chemistry offers a summer research program in which current high school students work in active research groups directed by SLU chemistry faculty. Research projects are available across chemistry subdisciplines, and applicants identify three chemistry faculty members whose research most interests them as part of the application process. The 2026 program operated from June through August. Current high school students who had completed a high school chemistry course were eligible for consideration, subject to citizenship or permanent-residency requirements. The structure provides genuine faculty-laboratory placement rather than classroom-only enrichment.

name: 4-H STEM Research Internship Program
title: Paid Yearlong High School Faculty-Mentored STEM Research Internship
description: The University of Maryland Eastern Shore Extension 4-H STEM Research Internship Program is a paid yearlong research experience for eligible Lower Shore high school students. Interns work with UMES mentors, develop a research project, acquire the technical skills needed to conduct it, and continue visiting campus during the academic year. Research opportunities have included genomics, horticulture, physics, biomedical science, and related STEM areas. Participants must complete a substantial final product such as a formal research report, journal-article draft, conference poster, or another appropriate presentation of their findings. The 2026-27 cohort runs from September 2026 through August 2027 and offers selected interns a $3,000 stipend plus mileage reimbursement.

name: ITMAT FIRST
title: Invitation-Only High School Translational Biomedical Research Experience
department: Institute for Translational Medicine and Therapeutics / FitzGerald Lab
description: ITMAT FIRST is a three-week mentored translational research experience based in the FitzGerald Lab at the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine. Students work approximately 40 hours per week with experienced postdoctoral mentors, learn experimental tools such as PCR, and become immersed in their mentor's research project. The curriculum also introduces pharmacology, genetics, bioinformatics, clinical research, data collection, analysis, and interpretation. Students present their projects at a concluding symposium. Access is highly restricted: the 2026 program accepted students by invitation from designated partner schools in Philadelphia and Dublin, and applicants must come through a participating institution.

name: PERI Institute STEM Education Research Program
title: High School STEM Education and Social Science Research Program
description: The PERI Institute STEM Education Research Program at UC Irvine gives rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors six weeks of authentic research experience focused on teaching, learning, student success, and STEM education. Scholars begin with an in-person research bootcamp at UCI, meet their research mentors, and learn the research process before spending several weeks conducting collaborative hands-on research with UCI faculty and staff. The 2026 program used a hybrid structure with an in-person first week and largely virtual collaborative research during weeks two through five. Participants conclude by presenting their work at a UCI research poster symposium.

name: Larkin University Summer Research Program (LUSRP)
title: High School Biomedical, Pharmaceutical and Clinical Research Program
department: University Research Program / Colleges of Biomedical Sciences and Pharmacy
description: The Larkin University Summer Research Program gives high school juniors and seniors and undergraduate students opportunities to conduct hands-on research in pharmaceutical, clinical, and biomedical sciences under Larkin University faculty mentors. Applicants review available research projects and identify projects aligned with their interests before selected students are matched with supervisors. Participants commit at least 20 hours per week to research, attend professional-development sessions, and present their findings through oral and poster presentations at a concluding Mini-Symposium. The 2026 cohort included 28 researchers, including five high school students, providing direct confirmation of high-school participation in faculty-mentored biomedical, pharmaceutical, and clinical research.

name: Summer Science Institute III — Student Research Internship
title: Eight-Week High School Independent Biomedical Research Internship
description: The University of Alabama at Birmingham CORD Summer Science Institute III is an intensive eight-week high school research internship. Students complete biomedical laboratory-technique training before being assigned to UAB faculty research mentors and developing independent projects related to their mentors' active research. Participants work approximately 40 hours per week and also attend scientific seminars, workshops, and related research activities before presenting original results through professional research posters. Participating research areas can include biochemistry and molecular genetics, biology, biomedical engineering, cardiovascular medicine, pediatrics, psychiatry and behavioral neurobiology, and other biomedical or engineering disciplines. SSI III is the advanced research stage of UAB CORD's sequential Summer Science Institute pathway, so applicants should verify prerequisite participation and current eligibility requirements.

name: Syracuse University Summer High School Internship Program (SU-SHIP)
title: Six-Week High School Physics Research Internship
description: The Syracuse University Summer High School Internship Program gives eligible Syracuse City School District students six weeks of college-level physics research experience. Participants work alongside Syracuse University physics faculty, graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers on active research while developing scientific and technical skills. The program culminates in a research poster session in which students communicate their work to members of the university research community. Syracuse documented 12 local high school students participating in the fifth cohort of the program in summer 2026, confirming sustained high-school access to the research experience.

name: MCC & EIPM Summer Internship Program
title: High School Cancer Biology and Precision Medicine Research Internship
department: Sandra and Edward Meyer Cancer Center / Englander Institute for Precision Medicine
description: The MCC & EIPM Summer Internship Program is a seven-week research experience jointly organized by Weill Cornell Medicine's Meyer Cancer Center and Englander Institute for Precision Medicine. High school and undergraduate interns receive hands-on mentored research experience while learning about cancer biology, precision medicine, computational biomedicine, epidemiology, and related biomedical fields. Approximately 20 hours per week are devoted to laboratory research and meetings with research mentors, with additional educational and professional-development programming supplementing the research experience. The program provides a structured pathway for high school students to participate directly in the Weill Cornell biomedical research environment.

name: Department of Pediatrics Summer Internship
title: High School Pediatrics, Public Health and Biomedical Research Internship
description: The Weill Cornell Medicine Department of Pediatrics Summer Internship provides high school and undergraduate students with mentored summer experiences in pediatric medicine, biomedical research, public health, health policy, and related areas. Current high school juniors and seniors are explicitly eligible to apply. Internship projects may run for approximately six or ten weeks depending on placement, with participants working full-time under the supervision of faculty or staff mentors. Students gain exposure to academic medicine and research while completing substantive projects, and participants who successfully complete the program receive a modest stipend.

name: Kirill Akopov — Akopov Lab
title: Solid-State Chemistry, Nanomaterials and Materials Research Prospect
description: Professor Kirill Akopov's laboratory at Rutgers University–Newark conducts research in solid-state and materials chemistry, including the synthesis and characterization of advanced materials and nanomaterials. The laboratory's official group news documents direct high-school participation: a high school student joined the group for a ten-week summer research internship in 2026. This provides current evidence that the laboratory has hosted a high school researcher in a sustained research role. However, the lab does not advertise a continuously open general high-school application, so prospective students should directly contact Professor Akopov or the laboratory to ask about current research projects, mentorship capacity, and possible high-school placements.

name: Collaborative Laboratory Internships and Mentorship Blueprint (CLIMB)
title: Paid High School Faculty-Laboratory Research Internship
department: University of Missouri–St. Louis Research Laboratories
description: The Collaborative Laboratory Internships and Mentorship Blueprint at the University of Missouri–St. Louis provides eligible local high school students with paid hands-on research experience in active university laboratories. Students work directly with UMSL researchers and mentors on authentic scientific projects rather than completing classroom-only enrichment. The program has operated for more than a decade, and seven local high school students participated in its 2026 cohort. Documented student research has included stem-cell differentiation work in UMSL faculty laboratories, demonstrating direct participation in ongoing university research. Eligibility is geographically and institutionally restricted, so students should verify current partner-school and local requirements.

name: Young Scientist Internship
title: High School Faculty-Mentored Biomedical and Health Sciences Research Internship
university: Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences
description: The Young Scientist Internship at Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences gives high school students an opportunity to contribute directly to faculty-mentored scientific research. Interns participate in a research project under the guidance of university investigators, gaining experience with the scientific process, research methods, data collection or analysis, and scientific communication. Participants conclude the experience by presenting their research at the Young Scientist Program Symposium. The program therefore provides substantive mentored research rather than observational shadowing or classroom-only science enrichment.

name: USU Summer Scholars Program
title: Paid Eight-Week High School Biomedical and Behavioral Research Internship
description: The Uniformed Services University Summer Scholars Program provides high school students with an intensive eight-week full-time research experience in the university's biomedical, clinical, and behavioral research environment. Participants join research teams working in areas that may include medicine, pathology, psychiatry, pharmacology, microbiology, immunology, and social or behavioral science. Scholars gain hands-on experience with the research process and conclude the program by preparing and presenting a scientific abstract at the Summer Scholars symposium. The program provides a stipend, with the published high-school award listed at approximately $3,500 for the eight-week experience. Admission is competitive and applicants should verify current eligibility requirements for each cycle.

name: Industrial and Systems Engineering High School Research Internship
title: High School Industrial Engineering and Data Science Research Internship
department: H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering
description: The Georgia Tech H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering has hosted high school students in a structured research internship combining industrial-engineering instruction with data-science research. Documented participants completed curated instructional material and worked on two research projects using quantitative and data-driven methods to investigate educational factors. Georgia Tech reports that the featured high school researchers ultimately published studies resulting from their work, demonstrating unusually substantive scholarly output for a pre-college research experience. The internship is particularly valuable for students interested in industrial engineering, statistics, data science, operations research, and quantitative social-science applications.

name: Computer Science, Biology, and Biomedical Informatics (CoSBBI) Summer Academy
title: High School AI, Programming and Biomedical Informatics Research Academy
description: The Computer Science, Biology, and Biomedical Informatics Summer Academy at the University of Pittsburgh introduces high school students to research at the intersection of computing, biology, artificial intelligence, and biomedical informatics. Participants receive programming and biomedical-informatics training and collaborate with mentors on active research projects. The broader Pitt biomedical informatics environment includes research in machine learning, generative artificial intelligence, causal inference, bioinformatics, imaging informatics, health data, and related computational approaches. CoSBBI therefore provides a structured high-school pathway into genuine computational biomedical research rather than a general coding camp.

name: USDA-ARS Sugarcane Phenotyping High School Research Internship
title: Paid High School Plant Science and Agricultural Phenotyping Research Internship
description: The USDA Agricultural Research Service Sugarcane Phenotyping High School Research Internship provides a high school student with sustained research experience at the USDA-ARS Sugarcane Research Unit in Houma, Louisiana. The intern contributes to field, greenhouse, and laboratory research investigating sugarcane traits including yield, biomass production, sucrose content, disease resistance, and environmental adaptation. Training can include laboratory and analytical techniques such as pipetting, spectrophotometry, centrifugation, and high-performance liquid chromatography. The initial appointment is approximately one year, with full-time participation during the summer and a stipend provided through the ORISE research-participation framework. This is a genuine federal agricultural research placement rather than a short-term enrichment program.

name: Discover Psychology — Summer Research Intensive
title: Psychology and Behavioral Science Summer Research Intensive
description: Clark University's Discover Psychology Summer Research Intensive is a two-week pre-college research experience designed specifically for high-school students interested in psychology and behavioral science. Participants learn psychological research methods and develop an original research study, collecting and analyzing data and preparing their findings for professional presentation. The program introduces students to experimental and participatory-action research while providing experience with the process of turning a research question into a completed study.

name: ATR Lab Summer Internship Program
title: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics High School Research Internship
description: Kent State University's ATR Lab offers a summer research internship specifically for high-school students interested in artificial intelligence, robotics, physical AI agents, and intelligent systems. Interns are assigned to research projects within the laboratory and gain exposure to the process of developing, testing, analyzing, and presenting research ideas. The program provides unusually direct access to an active university computer-science research laboratory for pre-college students.

name: Tyson Environmental Research Apprenticeship (TERA)
title: Paid Environmental Biology and Ecology Research Apprenticeship
description: The Tyson Environmental Research Apprenticeship is a six-week paid research experience at Washington University in St. Louis's Tyson Research Center. High-school participants become members of active environmental research teams and work alongside university scientists, postdoctoral researchers, graduate students, and undergraduate researchers on authentic ecology and environmental-biology projects. TERA provides substantial field and research experience rather than classroom-only enrichment. Participation is tied to the Tyson Research Center's SIFT pathway, so students should review current prerequisite and eligibility requirements before applying.

name: EBSCO Scholars Program
title: Paid High School Faculty-Mentored STEM Research Internship
description: The UAB EBSCO Scholars Program provides eligible high-school students with eight weeks of full-time research under the mentorship of a University of Alabama at Birmingham faculty researcher. Potential research areas span biology, cancer, computer science, chemistry, engineering, genetics, microbiology, molecular biology, pharmacology, physics, psychology, and related STEM fields. Participants conduct research in an active university environment, develop a scientific poster, and receive a $2,500 stipend. Eligibility is restricted to students from designated Birmingham-area schools, so applicants should verify the current participating-school requirements.

name: PROPEL — Professional Research Opportunities to Prepare for Engineering and Life Sciences
title: High School Engineering and Life Sciences Research Internship
description: UMass Lowell's Professional Research Opportunities to Prepare for Engineering and Life Sciences program provides eligible high-school students with summer research internships in engineering, life sciences, and related STEM disciplines. The 2026 program accepts students age 16 or older who meet specified Massachusetts school and geographic eligibility criteria, including qualifying vocational schools, Gateway City schools, and certain public schools. Participants gain experience in active university research environments while working with research mentors on scientific or engineering projects.

name: FPAC Lab — High School Plasma Research Prospect
title: Plasma Physics, Nuclear Engineering and Diagnostics Research Prospect
description: NC State's FPAC research environment conducts experimental work involving plasma science, nuclear engineering, diagnostics, electronics, and related technologies. NC State documented a high-school junior completing a six-week summer research internship with FPAC in 2026 and contributing to plasma-diagnostic development for the AMAROK RF ion-source experiment, including work involving electronics, circuit-board design, instrumentation, and experimental diagnostics. This provides strong recent evidence of substantive high-school research participation. However, FPAC does not advertise a continuously available high-school position, so students should treat this as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry prospect rather than a guaranteed opening.

name: NextGen FinTech Scholars: Data Science, AI & Digital Finance
title: Finance, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science High School Research Program
department: Schar School of Policy and Government — Young Scholars Research Program
description: George Mason University's NextGen FinTech Scholars program gives high-school students research experience at the intersection of finance, data science, artificial intelligence, and digital finance. Participants learn to work with analytical tools including Python, R, SAS, and Stata and may analyze professional financial datasets such as CRSP, Compustat, and SEC EDGAR data. The program emphasizes quantitative research and scholarly writing, with students developing a research paper that may be considered for publication. It is a particularly valuable pre-college research pathway for students interested in finance, economics, FinTech, quantitative analysis, or applied data science.

name: ACS Project SEED — University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee
title: Paid High School Chemistry and Biochemistry Research Program
description: The University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee serves as an ACS Project SEED research site where eligible high-school students participate in authentic chemistry research with university faculty and graduate researchers. Recent UWM projects have included computational chemistry, biochemistry and drug discovery, environmental and water chemistry, and molecular biophysics. The program provides an extended summer research experience in an active university research environment and follows ACS Project SEED eligibility and application requirements.

name: Visiting Student Intern Program for NYC Local Area Students (VSI-Local)
title: Faculty-Sponsored High School Research Internship Pathway
description: Columbia University's Visiting Student Intern framework includes a pathway for eligible students from the New York City local area, including high-school students, to participate in research and training under the supervision of a Columbia faculty member. VSI-Local provides institutional infrastructure for students who establish a research relationship with a Columbia principal investigator or faculty sponsor and can support research experiences lasting up to one year. This is not a centralized research-placement program: high-school students generally need to identify and secure a willing Columbia faculty sponsor before the visiting-intern appointment can be established, making direct PI or laboratory inquiry the appropriate access route.

name: GeoAI and Natural Hazards Lab
title: Geospatial Artificial Intelligence and Natural Hazards Research Prospect
description: The GeoAI and Natural Hazards Lab at the University at Buffalo conducts interdisciplinary research combining geospatial artificial intelligence, machine learning, GIS, spatial data science, natural hazards, human mobility, sustainability, and disaster resilience. The laboratory's official personnel history documents a New York high-school student completing two summer research internships with the group before attending Cornell University, providing concrete evidence of repeated pre-college participation. The lab does not advertise a continuously available high-school position, so students should treat it as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry prospect and contact the research group regarding possible current projects.

name: Boston University RISE Internship/Practicum
title: Research in Science & Engineering High School Research Program
description: Boston University's Research in Science & Engineering program is a six-week research experience for rising high-school seniors. Internship-track students spend approximately 40 hours per week conducting university laboratory research under the mentorship of BU faculty members, postdoctoral researchers, or graduate students and conclude by presenting their work at a research poster symposium. Research areas span biology, biomedical engineering, chemistry, computer science, Earth and environmental science, engineering, mathematics, medical laboratory research, neuroscience, physics, psychology, public health, and related fields. The Practicum track provides structured computational research in areas such as computational neurobiology and data science.

name: Nancy Padilla-Coreano — Padilla-Coreano Lab
title: Social and Computational Neuroscience Research Prospect
description: Professor Nancy Padilla-Coreano leads a University of Florida neuroscience laboratory investigating the neural mechanisms underlying social behavior and decision-making. The group combines behavioral neuroscience, neural-circuit approaches, quantitative analysis, and computational methods to study the social brain. The laboratory has documented high-school research participation, establishing concrete precedent for pre-college students contributing to its research environment. Because the lab does not advertise a continuously available high-school position, prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry opportunity and contact the laboratory regarding current projects and mentorship capacity.

name: Robert Lee — Lee Lab
title: Molecular Biology and Genetics Research Prospect
description: The Lee Lab at the University of Pennsylvania provides a strong direct-inquiry prospect for students interested in molecular biology, genetics, and experimental biomedical research. The laboratory has repeatedly hosted high-school researchers. Its official personnel history documents high-school students participating during multiple recent summers, including high-school researchers in summer 2026, while another researcher originally worked in the lab during high school before later returning as a Penn undergraduate. This repeated participation provides strong evidence that pre-college researchers can contribute to the lab, although current openings depend on project and mentor availability.

name: Tim Johnstone — Johnstone Laboratory
title: Bioinorganic and Organometallic Chemistry Research Prospect
description: Professor Tim Johnstone's laboratory at UC Santa Cruz studies medicinal and fundamental inorganic chemistry, including biologically relevant inorganic compounds, main-group chemistry, chemical bonding, and metal complexes. The group has exceptionally strong documented high-school research precedent. A local high-school researcher began an NSF-funded summer research project in the laboratory in 2025, and in April 2026 the lab reported that her first-author paper on alkali-metal complexation by phosphine and arsine oxides had been accepted by the Journal of Organometallic Chemistry. The current laboratory roster also documents high-school research participation. No standing high-school application is advertised, so students should inquire directly regarding current availability.

name: Micro-Precision Lab — Young Dawgs Research Prospect
title: Microfluidics, Bioengineering and Single-Cell Research Prospect
description: The Micro-Precision Lab at the University of Georgia conducts interdisciplinary bioengineering research involving microfluidics, exosome analysis, single-cell and bacterial phenotyping, multimodal cell analysis, three-dimensional printing, and related biomedical technologies. The laboratory's official team roster explicitly documents a high-school researcher who has participated in the group since 2024 through UGA's Young Dawgs program. This provides concrete evidence that high-school students can gain substantive laboratory research experience within the group. Access for high-school students is associated with the Young Dawgs pathway, so applicants should verify current program eligibility and laboratory placement options.

name: WINLAB Summer Internship Program
title: Wireless Systems, Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering Research Internship
description: Rutgers University's Wireless Information Network Laboratory operates a long-running summer research internship involving wireless systems, networking, artificial intelligence, smart cities, autonomous systems, edge computing, and related electrical and computer engineering research. Rutgers documented New Jersey high-school students participating alongside undergraduate and graduate researchers in the 2026 cohort, working for roughly ten weeks in faculty-mentored research teams. The 2026 showcase included more than 70 interns presenting 32 projects. WINLAB's standard published application instructions are primarily written for college students even though the center documents high-school participation, so high-school students should verify the appropriate current access route directly with WINLAB rather than assuming the undergraduate application applies to them.

name: UT Dallas Computer Science High School Research Program — Intensive Research Internship
title: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Research Internship
department: Department of Computer Science — K-12 Outreach
description: The University of Texas at Dallas Computer Science High School Research Program offers an intensive research-internship pathway for advanced and highly motivated high-school students. Students selected for the internship join active UT Dallas computer-science laboratories and generally commit approximately 20 to 40 hours per week. Work varies by research group and can include reading scientific papers, conducting simulations, developing software, analyzing data, and contributing to lab-specific research tasks. Individual laboratories manage intern selection, and UT Dallas describes admission to the research-lab pathway as highly selective.

name: Wolfram High School Summer Research Program
title: Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence Research Program
description: The Wolfram High School Summer Research Program is an intensive project-based research experience focused on computational thinking, artificial intelligence, scientific computing, mathematics, and interdisciplinary STEM research. Students build proficiency with Wolfram Language and then develop individual computational research projects under expert mentorship. Projects are selected in collaboration with the Wolfram team and can span mathematics, physics, biology, engineering, computer science, economics, social science, and other computational fields. The 2026 program was held at Bentley University in Waltham, Massachusetts, and participants completed original projects ranging from mathematical and physical modeling to AI, biology, economics, robotics, and quantum computation.

name: DiSC Lab
title: Data Science and Computer Science Research Prospect
description: Boston University's DiSC Lab conducts computer-science and data-oriented research in an active university research environment. The laboratory has unusually extensive documented high-school participation: its official team roster contains a dedicated High-School Researchers section listing numerous former high-school research interns alongside undergraduate, master's, doctoral, and other researchers. This repeated history provides strong evidence that the group has successfully incorporated pre-college students into its research environment. The lab does not advertise a continuously available high-school application, so prospective students should inquire directly regarding current projects and mentorship availability.

name: Synthetic Regeneration & Systems Physiology Laboratory
title: Synthetic Biology and Regenerative Biology Research Prospect
description: Columbia University's Synthetic Regeneration & Systems Physiology Laboratory conducts interdisciplinary research involving synthetic biology, regenerative biology, systems physiology, wound biology, genomics, and related biomedical science. The laboratory's current official team roster explicitly documents a high-school research intern working in synthetic biology at Columbia, providing direct recent evidence that a pre-college student has participated in the group's research environment. Because the laboratory does not advertise a standing high-school application process, prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry prospect and contact the group regarding current research opportunities.

name: Houston Methodist Summer High School Research Internship
title: Eight-Week High School Translational Biomedical Research Internship
description: Houston Methodist's Summer High School Research Internship is an eight-week full-time research experience for eligible current high-school juniors and seniors age 16 or older. Students conduct translational biomedical research under the guidance of Houston Methodist faculty and research mentors, gain experience with laboratory and scientific research techniques, and contribute to an active research project. Participants also develop scientific communication skills and conclude the experience by presenting their work at a summer research symposium. Houston Methodist currently advertises future program cycles, confirming that this is an active structured high-school research pathway.

name: CoMM Lab — High School Research Prospect
title: Cognitive Psychology, Memory and Communication Science Research Prospect
department: Department of Communicative Sciences and Disorders
description: NYU's CoMM Lab conducts research involving cognition, memory, language and communication, cognitive psychology, and related behavioral and communication-science questions. The laboratory's official team roster currently identifies a Class of 2027 student as a high school research intern whose interests include cognitive psychology, memory, language processing, and neurodegenerative disease. This provides direct current evidence that a pre-college student can participate in the laboratory's research environment. The lab does not advertise a continuously available high-school position, so prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry research prospect.

name: Nathan C. Walker — AI Ethics Lab
title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics, Human Rights and Technology Research Prospect
description: The Rutgers University–Camden AI Ethics Lab conducts interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, ethics, philosophy, human rights, technology, and society. The laboratory's official personnel information documents high-school research-assistant participation in its AI and human-rights research environment, including work connected with Project Insight. This provides concrete evidence that a pre-college researcher has contributed to the lab. Because the group does not advertise a continuously available high-school application, interested students should contact Professor Nathan C. Walker or the laboratory directly to ask about current research projects and mentorship availability.

name: Antonios Marsellos — High School Research Mentorship
title: Data Science, Earth Science and Biomedical Data Research Mentorship
description: Antonios Marsellos has documented extensive mentorship of high-school researchers using data science and computational methods across earth, environmental, and biomedical research. His official research record lists approximately 55 high-school researchers between 2021 and 2026, including seven students during summer 2026. Projects have analyzed real datasets involving EEG and Alzheimer's disease, anesthesia signals, arrhythmia screening, earthquakes, solar cycles, GPS measurements, coastal flooding, and satellite-based shoreline change. Students receive training in R and quantitative data analysis, and documented projects have progressed to science fairs and scholarly dissemination, including a peer-reviewed IEEE conference publication. Current opportunities should be verified directly because individual mentorship capacity can vary.

name: Shishir Chundawat — Chundawat Research Group
title: Biochemical Engineering, Biotechnology and Biomolecular Research Prospect
department: Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering
description: Professor Shishir Chundawat's Rutgers research group conducts biochemical and biomolecular engineering research involving biotechnology, protein engineering, biochemistry, biocatalysis, and related areas. The laboratory has documented repeated high-school research participation. Rutgers reports that two ACS Project SEED high-school interns completed six-week research experiences in the group and presented their findings at the ACS Project SEED poster competition, while the laboratory separately notes that it has hosted several high-school visiting research interns. This establishes strong precedent for substantive pre-college laboratory participation, although students should inquire directly about current availability and possible access pathways.

name: STEM Pathways for Aspiring Researchers & Knowledgeable Scientists (SPARKS)
title: Faculty-Matched High School STEM Research Mentorship Program
tags: Sacramento Regional Science and Engineering Fair
description: Chico State's STEM Pathways for Aspiring Researchers & Knowledgeable Scientists program creates faculty-led research mentorship teams for local high-school researchers. The 2026 program recruited principal investigators and university-student mentors specifically to train and guide a high-school student through a research project. Students are matched with research mentors and work toward sustained scientific research, with projects designed to progress toward presentation at the Sacramento Regional Science and Engineering Fair. This provides a structured pathway into authentic faculty-supported research rather than a short classroom enrichment experience. Students should verify current geographic eligibility, research fields, matching procedures, and application dates.

name: Rouge Research Group
title: Nucleic Acid Chemistry and Nanobiotechnology Research Prospect
description: The Rouge Research Group at the University of Connecticut conducts chemical-biology research involving nucleic-acid chemistry, nanobiotechnology, nanotechnology, biomolecular delivery, and related applications of DNA and RNA chemistry. The laboratory's official information documents current high-school participation through an Advanced Research Mentorship student from Glastonbury High School working within the group. This establishes direct precedent for school-year pre-college laboratory research. The laboratory does not advertise a continuously available general high-school application, so prospective students should inquire directly regarding current projects, mentorship capacity, and possible access pathways.

name: Christy Haynes — Haynes Research Group
title: Analytical Chemistry, Nanomaterials and Nanotoxicology Research Prospect
description: Professor Christy Haynes's research group at the University of Minnesota conducts analytical and bioanalytical chemistry research involving nanomaterials, nanotoxicology, environmental chemistry, and biological applications of advanced chemical techniques. The laboratory's official alumni roster documents a Summer High School Researcher who participated in the group during summer 2025, providing recent concrete precedent for pre-college laboratory involvement. The group does not advertise a continuously open high-school position, so interested students should contact the laboratory directly to determine whether suitable projects and mentorship are currently available.

name: Institute for Mathematics and Democracy — High School Summer Research
title: Mathematics, Economics and Public Policy High School Research Program
description: The Institute for Mathematics and Democracy's high-school summer research program supports students conducting interdisciplinary quantitative research connecting mathematics with economics, data science, game theory, public policy, democracy, and social issues. The institute publicly documented a 2026 high-school summer research cohort, confirming active pre-college participation. The program is particularly valuable for students seeking research outside traditional wet-lab STEM because projects apply mathematical and quantitative tools to social-science and policy questions. Prospective students should review the institute's current materials for future cohort dates, eligibility requirements, project areas, mentorship structure, and application procedures.

name: Adam Braunschweig — CUNY ASRC Nanoscience Initiative
title: Nanoscience, Environmental Chemistry and Materials Research Prospect
university: The Graduate Center, City University of New York
department: Advanced Science Research Center — Nanoscience Initiative
description: Professor Adam Braunschweig conducts nanoscience and materials-chemistry research within the CUNY Advanced Science Research Center's Nanoscience Initiative. CUNY documented exceptional high-school research participation in the group through a student who worked in an ASRC mentorship program and contributed to development of a low-cost arsenic-removal system using cellulose, eggshell-derived material, and magnetic nanoparticles. The work resulted in a 2026 ACS Omega publication on which the high-school researcher was a co-corresponding author, demonstrating unusually substantive pre-college involvement in publishable research. The laboratory does not advertise a continuously available general high-school position, so future participation should be treated as an availability-dependent direct-inquiry prospect.

name: Scientific Clinical Research Internship Program (SCRIP)
title: Faculty-Sponsored High School Clinical Research Internship
department: UCI School of Medicine / Office of Research
description: The Scientific Clinical Research Internship Program at the University of California, Irvine School of Medicine provides an institutional pathway for students to participate in clinical research under a UCI faculty sponsor. High school students age 16 or older are explicitly eligible and may participate for periods ranging from approximately one month to one year. Students must first identify and secure a faculty research sponsor rather than being automatically matched with a laboratory, making direct outreach to UCI investigators an important part of the process. Research experiences can provide exposure to clinical and biomedical research methods within an academic medical-school environment.

name: Thomas Folland — Quantum Nanophotonic Materials Lab
title: Quantum Materials, Nanophotonics and Two-Dimensional Materials Research Prospect
description: Professor Thomas Folland leads a University of Iowa research group studying quantum nanophotonic materials, polaritons, two-dimensional materials, graphene, semiconductors, infrared photonics, optical sensing, and related areas of experimental condensed-matter physics. The laboratory's official personnel information documents current high-school research participation, including high-school research intern Sophia Beers, whose work involves exfoliation of two-dimensional materials. This provides direct evidence that high-school students can participate in the group's research environment. Because a continuously available high-school position is not guaranteed, prospective students should contact Professor Folland or the laboratory regarding current opportunities.

name: Xiaoyu Shi — Shi Lab
title: Super-Resolution Bioimaging, Spatial Multiomics and Cell Biology Research Prospect
department: Department of Developmental and Cell Biology
description: Professor Xiaoyu Shi's laboratory at UC Irvine develops and applies advanced imaging technologies to investigate the molecular organization of cells. Research includes super-resolution microscopy, spatial multiomics, proteins, RNA, DNA, organelle biology, cellular structures, disease mechanisms, and computational image analysis. The laboratory's official materials document high-school research participation, including a project in which high-school students worked with lab researchers to program an automated robotic imaging system and perform organelle segmentation. This establishes precedent for substantive high-school involvement, although a continuously open independent position is not advertised. Interested students should inquire directly regarding current project and mentorship availability.

name: Trevor Sorrells — Sorrells Lab
title: Genetics, Neuroscience and Mosquito Behavior Research Prospect
description: Professor Trevor Sorrells leads a Yale Genetics laboratory investigating the genetic and neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, with a particular focus on the evolution and neural circuitry of mosquito blood-feeding behavior. The group uses approaches including behavioral experiments, genetics, gene editing, optogenetics, transcriptomics, and transgenic methods. The laboratory's official team roster explicitly includes a current High School Researcher, providing direct evidence of high-school participation in the research group. Because the laboratory does not advertise a continuously open high-school position, prospective students should contact the group regarding current research and mentorship availability.

name: Schmidt Lab — Cornell University
title: Environmental Microbiology and Marine Microbial Ecology Research Prospect
description: The Schmidt Lab at Cornell University conducts research in environmental microbiology and microbial ecology, including studies of microbial communities and their roles in environmental and biogeochemical processes. The laboratory's official personnel information documents high-school research participation through the TST-BOCES New Visions program. A documented high-school researcher has investigated how oyster farming influences marine-sediment microbial communities and their capacity for denitrification.
