This is strong evidence of authentic high-school participation in environmental microbiology research, although access is connected to the New Visions partner pathway rather than an unrestricted laboratory application.

name: Mohamed Abdelfattah — Abdelfattah Research Group
title: Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning Systems and AI Hardware Research Prospect
department: Cornell Tech / Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Professor Mohamed Abdelfattah leads a Cornell Tech and Cornell Electrical and Computer Engineering research group working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computer architecture, and hardware systems. Research includes deep-learning systems, AI accelerators, neural-network compression, automated machine learning, FPGA and reconfigurable computing, and hardware-software codesign. The group's official personnel history documents former high-school research participation, including a researcher explicitly identified as a High School Researcher. This establishes precedent for high-school involvement, although no continuously available high-school position is advertised. Interested students should contact the group regarding current opportunities.

name: Kelly Ruggles — Ruggles Lab
title: Computational Biology, Genomics and Precision Medicine Research Prospect
description: Professor Kelly Ruggles leads a computational biology research laboratory at NYU Grossman School of Medicine working across genomics, proteomics, single-cell sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, biomedical data science, machine learning, and precision medicine. The laboratory's official alumni information documents repeated high-school research participation, including multiple former high-school researchers. Recent high-school research associated with the group has also received recognition at a regional science and engineering fair. This repeated history provides strong evidence that high-school students have contributed to substantive computational biomedical research in the laboratory. Current openings are not guaranteed, so prospective students should inquire directly about availability.

name: Sicheng Kevin Li — Rotorcraft Aerodynamics and Aeroacoustics Lab
title: Rotorcraft Aerodynamics, Aeroacoustics and Advanced Air Mobility Research Prospect
department: School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
description: Professor Sicheng Kevin Li leads the Rotorcraft Aerodynamics and Aeroacoustics Laboratory at Oklahoma State University. The group studies rotorcraft aerodynamics, aeroacoustics, vortex interactions, advanced air mobility, computational and experimental fluid dynamics, particle image velocimetry, and related aerospace systems. The laboratory's official prospective-student information explicitly provides instructions for students interested in joining as high-school researchers. High-school applicants are directed to email their research interests and provide a teacher recommendation. This explicit recruitment pathway makes the laboratory an unusually strong direct-access aerospace research prospect for high-school students.

name: Pengjie Wang — Quantum Matter and Devices Lab
title: Quantum Matter, Condensed Matter Physics and Quantum Devices Research Prospect
department: Department of Physics / Materials Research Laboratory
description: Professor Pengjie Wang leads the Quantum Matter and Devices research group at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, with research spanning quantum matter, condensed-matter physics, quantum devices, electronic materials, and experimental materials physics. The laboratory's official personnel roster documents repeated high-school research participation, including multiple WYSE high-school researchers in recent summer cohorts. This repeated participation provides strong evidence that high-school students can contribute to the group's research through established university pathways. Students should verify the current WYSE or associated high-school research application process for future participation.

name: Daniel Kronauer — Laboratory of Social Evolution and Behavior
title: Social Evolution, Genetics and Animal Behavior Research Prospect
department: Laboratory of Social Evolution and Behavior
description: Professor Daniel Kronauer leads Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Social Evolution and Behavior, which investigates the biological mechanisms and evolution of social behavior using approaches spanning genetics, genomics, neuroscience, behavioral biology, and evolutionary biology. The laboratory's official recruitment information specifically addresses high-school students interested in working in the lab during the summer and directs them to apply through Rockefeller University's Science Research Program. This provides a structured high-school pathway into advanced research on social evolution and animal behavior rather than relying solely on unsolicited laboratory outreach.

name: HEROES Project
title: Honesty and Ethics on Everyday Schooling High School Research Internship
description: The HEROES Project at UC San Diego investigates Honesty and Ethics on Everyday Schooling, examining academic integrity, student behavior, ethics, and social influences within educational environments. The project explicitly recruits high-school students, particularly students in San Diego County, to participate in authentic social-science research. High-school researchers can contribute to activities including observations and interviews with students and teachers, providing experience with qualitative research and educational psychology methods. The program is particularly notable as a substantive high-school research opportunity outside the traditional laboratory STEM fields.

name: CELL Scholars
title: UCLA Bioscience Laboratory Research Mentorship Program
description: CELL Scholars is a UCLA Brain Research Institute initiative that provides eligible 11th- and 12th-grade students from University High School in Los Angeles with sustained bioscience research experience. Participants are paired with UCLA graduate-student mentors and conduct research within UCLA bioscience laboratories, with projects potentially involving bench-based or computational approaches. Students develop research skills throughout the academic year and present their work at an annual poster symposium. Eligibility is geographically and school restricted, but the program provides unusually substantial access to active university research laboratories for participating high-school students.

name: Matthew Niepielko — NJ-RAISE / Niepielko Lab
title: Evolutionary and Developmental Biology High School Research Pathway
description: Professor Matthew Niepielko's laboratory at Kean University participates in NJ-RAISE, an initiative connecting local high-school students with sustained research training through Kean University and collaborating institutions including Princeton University. High-school students can enter research through Kean's Group Summer Scholars Research Program and select an Evolution and Developmental Biology research stream associated with the Niepielko Lab. The pathway provides authentic laboratory experience in areas including developmental biology, evolutionary biology, genetics, and molecular biology. NJ-RAISE support can cover program tuition and provide a stipend for eligible participants, making this a particularly strong structured New Jersey research pathway.

name: High School Student Pathway to Scientist
title: Biomedical Research, Medicine and Data Science Mentorship Program
department: New Jersey Medical School / Institute for Infectious and Inflammatory Diseases
description: The High School Student Pathway to Scientist at Rutgers New Jersey Medical School provides Newark-area high-school students with mentored exposure to biomedical research, medicine, and data science. Participants can be matched with Rutgers research mentors and contribute to authentic scientific projects within an academic medical research environment. Rutgers has documented participants conducting hands-on immune-system research, producing substantial scientific papers, and continuing into additional university laboratory experiences. The combination of faculty mentorship, authentic biomedical investigation, scientific communication, and a structured pathway for local high-school students makes this a strong research opportunity.

description: The Sarazen Research Group at Princeton University conducts chemical engineering research involving sustainable chemistry, chemical reactions, and approaches to improving chemical processes. The laboratory explicitly invites interested high-school students to contact Professor Sarazen about opportunities to participate in hands-on research. Students are encouraged to introduce themselves and describe their scientific interests, relevant background, and availability. This is a particularly strong direct-inquiry prospect because the laboratory provides explicit guidance for high-school applicants rather than merely documenting past participation. Research placement remains dependent on available projects and mentorship capacity.

name: Chiel Lab
title: Neuroscience, Neural Control and Biological Systems Research Prospect
description: The Chiel Lab at Case Western Reserve University investigates neural control, motor behavior, biomechanics, and the relationships between nervous systems and movement. Its research combines experimental biology with quantitative and computational approaches to understanding how biological systems generate coordinated behavior. The laboratory explicitly encourages interested high-school students to inquire about volunteering in research and provides contact instructions on its official website. This makes the Chiel Lab a strong prospect for students interested in neuroscience, biology, animal behavior, and interdisciplinary research. Available positions depend on current projects, preparation, and mentorship capacity.

name: Hematian Research Group
title: Inorganic Chemistry, Catalysis and Molecular Research Prospect
university: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
description: The Hematian Research Group at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro conducts experimental chemistry research involving inorganic chemistry, coordination chemistry, catalysis, and molecular systems. The laboratory explicitly welcomes research inquiries from high-school students and community-college students, providing a direct pathway for prospective young researchers to express interest. Students are encouraged to contact the research group with information about their chemistry background, scientific interests, and research goals. This is a strong direct-inquiry opportunity because high-school eligibility is explicitly stated on the laboratory's recruitment page. Participation depends on project availability and laboratory capacity.

name: Vidal-Gadea Lab
title: Neurobiology, Animal Behavior and Muscular Dystrophy Research Prospect
description: The Vidal-Gadea Lab at Illinois State University conducts biological research involving neurobiology, animal behavior, neuromuscular function, and experimental studies using C. elegans as a model organism. The laboratory explicitly welcomes inquiries from high-school students interested in research. Its official opportunities page documents more than a dozen previous high-school researchers who investigated muscular dystrophy using microscopy, behavioral experiments, and statistical analysis. This extensive history provides unusually strong evidence of meaningful high-school participation in active laboratory research. Interested students should contact the research group to discuss current projects, research expectations, and available mentorship.

name: Sheel Dodani — Dodani Lab
title: Chemical Biology and Molecular Imaging Summer Research Prospect
description: Professor Sheel Dodani leads a chemical biology laboratory at the University of Texas at Dallas investigating molecular imaging, chemical probes, fluorescence-based methods, and the development of chemical tools for studying biological systems. The laboratory documents hosting high-school researchers through the Welch Summer Scholars Program, a structured five-week summer research experience. Its official recruitment information specifies that independent high-school applications are not accepted directly by the laboratory, so interested students must pursue the relevant program pathway. This provides a documented route to university-level chemical biology research under laboratory mentorship, subject to program eligibility and selection.

name: Krishnan Lab
title: Biomedical Science and Molecular Research Summer Internship Prospect
description: The Krishnan Lab at UT Southwestern Medical Center provides a biomedical research environment for students interested in molecular and experimental biological science. The laboratory's official recruitment information explicitly documents high-school research placements through UT Southwestern's STARS Summer Research Program. Participating high-school students can undertake approximately eight weeks of research within a university medical research laboratory under scientific mentorship. This represents a structured high-school research pathway rather than an unrestricted direct laboratory application. Interested students should review the current STARS program eligibility requirements, application deadlines, and available laboratory placements.

name: COSMIC Lab
title: Electrical Engineering, Intelligent Systems and Computational Research Prospect
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: The COSMIC Lab at the University of Cincinnati conducts electrical and computer engineering research involving intelligent systems, computational methods, and engineering applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning. The laboratory's official personnel roster documents a summer 2026 high-school researcher working on a project involving early detection of plant diseases. This provides recent evidence of high-school students contributing to applied engineering and computing research alongside university researchers. Prospective students should inquire directly about current project opportunities, expected technical preparation, and mentorship availability, as a continuously open high-school position is not guaranteed.

name: High School Chemistry Research Experience
title: Summer Chemistry Laboratory Research Program
description: Chicago State University's High School Chemistry Research Experience is a structured four-week summer program introducing high-school students to university-level chemistry research and experimental laboratory techniques. Participants receive training in laboratory instrumentation and engage in research projects involving topics such as polymer synthesis, natural-product extraction, and chemical recycling. The program's official description also identifies a participation stipend, providing financial support for student involvement. This opportunity is particularly suitable for high-school students seeking an organized introduction to experimental chemistry and hands-on research. Applicants should consult the university's current program information to confirm eligibility, stipend availability, dates, and application procedures.

name: WCS Project TRUE — Teens Researching Urban Ecology
title: Paid Urban Ecology and Wildlife Conservation Research Internship
department: Wildlife Conservation Society Education / Fordham University
description: Project TRUE (Teens Researching Urban Ecology) is a paid, mentored research internship operated by the Wildlife Conservation Society at the Bronx Zoo in collaboration with Fordham University. The program provides eligible Bronx high-school students with opportunities to investigate urban ecosystems, biodiversity, wildlife conservation, and ecological questions through authentic scientific research. Participants work alongside scientific mentors to develop research questions, collect field data, analyze findings, and communicate results. Research activities can include wildlife surveys, camera trapping, ecological sampling, and laboratory techniques depending on the projects offered during a particular year. Students also gain experience preparing scientific posters and presenting research findings at events, including scientific research symposia associated with the American Museum of Natural History. Project TRUE offers summer research experiences and opportunities for continued engagement during the academic year. Applicants should consult the official website for current Bronx residency requirements, grade eligibility, application dates, and compensation details.

name: Penn Research Experience for High School Students (PREHSS)
title: University Faculty-Mentored Summer Research Experience
description: The Penn Research Experience for High School Students (PREHSS) is a summer research program at the University of Pennsylvania that connects high-school students with faculty-mentored research opportunities. The program provides an approximately five-week, in-person experience in which participants contribute to ongoing university research projects. Potential research areas span multiple scientific disciplines, including biology, chemistry, physics, astronomy, psychology, and related fields, depending on available mentors and placements. Students gain exposure to scientific methodology, research techniques, data analysis, and the process of communicating research findings. The experience includes opportunities to present research work and engage with the university's academic research community. Interested applicants should review the official program page for current eligibility requirements, available research areas, application deadlines, and participation costs or financial assistance.

name: Jackson Laboratory Academic Year Fellowships
title: Academic-Year Genetics and Biomedical Research Fellowship
description: The Jackson Laboratory Academic Year Fellowships provide high-school students with opportunities to participate in authentic biomedical research under the guidance of experienced scientific mentors. Eligible high-school juniors and seniors may join active research groups and develop research projects related to genetics, genomics, molecular biology, biomedical science, and other areas represented by participating laboratories. Fellows gain exposure to scientific investigation, research methodology, data collection, and the process of conducting research within a professional laboratory environment. The program offers academic-year research experiences at participating Jackson Laboratory locations, which may include Farmington, Connecticut, and other institutional research sites depending on the application cycle. Students should review the official fellowship page for current location availability, eligibility requirements, research commitments, and deadlines.

name: Rockefeller University LAB Jumpstart
title: High School Biomedical Science Research and Mentorship Program
description: LAB Jumpstart is a science education and research mentorship initiative at Rockefeller University designed to expand access to biomedical science opportunities for high-school students, particularly students from backgrounds that have historically faced barriers to participation in scientific research. The program introduces participants to laboratory research, scientific methodology, and the work of professional researchers at Rockefeller University. Students receive scientific training and mentorship while developing skills relevant to experimental biology and biomedical research. The program emphasizes preparation, access, and engagement with a university research environment. Interested students should consult the official LAB Jumpstart website to confirm current eligibility criteria, program structure, application procedures, and whether a particular cycle includes independent laboratory research placements.

name: UChicago PME Youth Lab Internship
title: Molecular Engineering and University Laboratory Research Internship
description: The University of Chicago's Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering has supported high-school research experiences through youth internship partnerships, including opportunities associated with After School Matters. Participating students gain exposure to university-level molecular engineering research and may work alongside scientific mentors in active research environments. Depending on the available projects, research can involve materials science, chemical engineering, molecular systems, or other interdisciplinary engineering topics. These experiences provide opportunities to develop laboratory skills, understand scientific methodology, and explore engineering research careers. Because the documented pathway operates through a partner organization, interested students should investigate the relevant After School Matters program offerings and confirm whether molecular engineering research placements are available in the current cycle.

name: AMNH Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
title: Museum-Based Scientific Research Mentorship Program
description: The Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP) at the American Museum of Natural History connects New York City high-school students with scientific mentors and opportunities to participate in authentic research. Students work with researchers on projects connected to the museum's scientific disciplines, which can include biological sciences, ecology, evolution, paleontology, earth science, astronomy, and related fields depending on mentor availability. Participants develop skills in scientific investigation, research methodology, data interpretation, and communication while gaining experience in a professional museum research environment. The program emphasizes sustained mentorship and engagement with real scientific questions rather than classroom-only instruction. Interested students should consult the official SRMP application page for current New York City eligibility requirements, program dates, research commitments, and application deadlines.

name: Subree Lab
title: Biology and Experimental Laboratory Summer Research Prospect
description: The Subree Lab at the University of Minnesota provides opportunities for students interested in participating in experimental biological research within an active university laboratory. The laboratory's official recruitment page explicitly welcomes inquiries from high-school students interested in summer research experiences and provides instructions for contacting the research group. Students may gain exposure to scientific investigation, laboratory methods, research questions, and the process of contributing to ongoing research under university mentorship. This is a promising direct-inquiry opportunity because high-school participation is specifically addressed in the laboratory's recruitment information. Interested students should review the group's current research and contact instructions to determine whether summer placements are available.

name: Stathopoulos Lab
title: Developmental Biology, Gene Regulation and Embryonic Development Research Prospect
department: Division of Biology and Biological Engineering
description: The Stathopoulos Lab at the California Institute of Technology investigates developmental biology, embryonic development, gene regulation, and the molecular mechanisms that control how organisms develop. The laboratory uses experimental approaches to understand how genes and cellular processes coordinate biological development. Its official outreach page explicitly welcomes high-school students from local, national, and international schools and documents previous high-school interns participating in developmental biology research. This provides strong evidence of established high-school research involvement in an active Caltech laboratory. Interested students should review the laboratory's outreach information and inquire about available research projects, mentorship, and any applicable eligibility requirements.

name: Wang Research Lab
title: Biomaterials, Cancer Immunotherapy and Biomedical Engineering Research Prospect
description: The Wang Research Lab at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign conducts interdisciplinary biomedical engineering research involving biomaterials, cancer immunotherapy, and technologies for improving medical treatment. The laboratory's official outreach information documents high-school researchers participating in projects involving biomaterials and cancer immunotherapy. A high-school researcher associated with the laboratory also received recognition at a national biomedical engineering poster competition, demonstrating opportunities for students to communicate substantive research findings. This provides strong evidence of high-school involvement in active biomedical engineering research. Prospective students should inquire about current research opportunities, required preparation, and mentorship availability.

name: HIP-SAT — High School Research Internship Program
title: Paid Summer Research Internship for Homeschooled High School Students
university: Massachusetts Institute of Technology / Weill Cornell Medicine
description: HIP-SAT is a paid summer research internship program designed specifically for homeschooled high-school students, with research placements involving institutions such as the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Weill Cornell Medicine. The program provides approximately eight weeks of research experience under the mentorship of graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, or other scientific mentors. Participants contribute to active university research projects, develop scientific skills, and present their work at a concluding research symposium. For the 2026 program, published compensation was approximately $15 per hour for around 20 hours of work per week. The program provides a distinctive pathway into university research for students whose educational arrangements meet its homeschooling eligibility requirements. Applicants should consult the official website for current eligibility, locations, stipend information, deadlines, and participating laboratories.

name: Vanderbilt Research Experience for High School Students (REHSS)
title: Six-Week Faculty-Mentored Summer Research Internship
university: Vanderbilt University / Vanderbilt University Medical Center
description: The Research Experience for High School Students (REHSS) at Vanderbilt University provides a six-week summer research experience in active laboratories at Vanderbilt University or Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Participants conduct independent research projects under faculty and laboratory mentorship, gaining experience with scientific investigation, research techniques, data collection, and analysis. Research topics vary according to available university and medical-center laboratories. The documented program is restricted to students participating in the Interdisciplinary Science and Research pathway, so it is not a general open-enrollment summer internship for all high-school students. Eligible students should review the Vanderbilt Center for Science Outreach website for current program requirements, application procedures, research placements, and scheduling.

name: Aspirnaut Summer Research Internship
title: Residential Biomedical Science Summer Research Internship
description: The Aspirnaut Summer Research Internship at the University of Michigan's Life Sciences Institute is a six-week residential research program for eligible Michigan high-school students entering their senior year. Participants join active university research groups and conduct biomedical or life-sciences research under scientific mentorship. The experience introduces students to experimental research, laboratory methods, scientific problem-solving, and professional research environments. The program provides residential housing, meals, and a stipend, helping eligible participants engage in research without having to arrange independent accommodation. Students should consult the official Aspirnaut website for current Michigan residency requirements, grade eligibility, application deadlines, research areas, and compensation details.

name: Boyce Thompson Institute High School Research Experience
title: Paid Plant Biology and Computational Biology Research Internship
description: The Boyce Thompson Institute High School Research Experience provides paid research internships in plant biology, plant science, computational biology, and related biological disciplines at a research institute affiliated with Cornell University. Participants work with scientific mentors on active research projects and gain experience in experimental or computational methods depending on their laboratory placement. The program does not require previous laboratory research experience, making it accessible to motivated students who are new to scientific research. Published program information identifies a stipend of approximately $4,200 and requires participants to live within roughly one hour of Ithaca throughout the year. Interested students should review the official program website for current residency restrictions, grade eligibility, application deadlines, stipend amounts, and research opportunities.

name: Northwestern University Research Program for High Schoolers (NURPH)
title: Paid Materials Science and Engineering Summer Research Program
department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
description: The Northwestern University Research Program for High Schoolers (NURPH) is a seven-week paid summer research experience focused on materials science and engineering. The program is designed for eligible rising high-school juniors and seniors from the Chicago and Evanston area. Participants conduct original research under the mentorship of university researchers, gaining experience with scientific methods, laboratory techniques, materials characterization, and research communication. No previous research experience is required, allowing students to develop foundational skills while contributing to active university research. Students should consult the official program website for current geographic eligibility requirements, application deadlines, compensation, and research expectations.

name: Utah NeuroRobotics Lab — High School Research Program
title: NeuroRobotics, Exoskeletons and Biomedical Engineering Summer Research Prospect
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: The Utah NeuroRobotics Lab at the University of Utah offers a specialized summer research experience for a small number of high-school students interested in robotics, neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and assistive technologies. The laboratory's official high-school research page describes hosting approximately one or two high-school researchers annually for a two-month summer experience. Previous student projects have involved robotic exoskeletons, virtual-reality systems, and clinical diagnostic technologies, and some former high-school participants have contributed to first-author scientific publications. The program provides opportunities for substantial research involvement under laboratory mentorship, although available positions are highly limited. Published tuition begins at approximately $4,000, so applicants should verify current fees, eligibility requirements, deadlines, and project availability before applying.

name: Dolmetsch Lab
title: Neuroscience, Neurodevelopment and Cellular Research Prospect
description: The Dolmetsch Lab at Stanford University conducts neuroscience research investigating the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying nervous-system development and function. Its research involves neurodevelopment, cellular biology, and experimental approaches to understanding neurological processes. The laboratory's official recruitment page explicitly states that it accepts a small number of high-school volunteers each year. Interested students are instructed to email a one-page essay explaining their scientific interests and motivation for joining the research group. This provides a documented direct-inquiry pathway for high-school students seeking authentic university laboratory experience. Opportunities are limited and depend on the laboratory's current research needs and mentorship availability.

name: Feeley-Liu Lab
title: Stem Cell Biology and Molecular Biomedical Research Summer Internship
description: The Feeley-Liu Lab at the University of California, San Francisco provides opportunities for high-school students to participate in biomedical research involving stem cell biology, molecular biology, and experimental laboratory techniques. Its official recruitment page describes a summer research experience for high-school students, with opportunities to learn scientific methods, contribute to active research projects, and potentially participate in scientific presentations or publications depending on the nature of their work. The laboratory has published information inviting inquiries for summer 2027, providing a prospective application pathway. Interested students should review the official recruitment page and contact the laboratory regarding eligibility, scheduling, available projects, and mentorship capacity.

name: Molecular Plant-Microbe Interaction Research Group
title: Plant Biology, Plant Immunity and Molecular Research Prospect
description: The Molecular Plant-Microbe Interaction Research Group at the University of Michigan investigates the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing interactions between plants and microorganisms. Research topics include plant immunity, plant defense responses, molecular signaling, and biological processes that influence plant health. The research group's official website explicitly welcomes high-school students interested in research experience and directs prospective applicants to contact Dr. Ping He. This provides a documented pathway for motivated students to inquire about participation in university-level plant biology research. Students should review the laboratory's research interests and contact instructions to determine whether suitable projects and mentorship opportunities are available.

name: OBM Laboratory — High School Research Internship
title: Biomedical Engineering and Experimental Research Internship Prospect
description: The OBM Laboratory at the University of Missouri–St. Louis provides opportunities for high-school students to participate in authentic biomedical engineering research alongside university researchers. The laboratory's official recruitment page explicitly describes unpaid high-school research internships, establishing a direct pathway for students interested in gaining hands-on scientific experience. Participants may develop research skills, learn experimental techniques, and contribute to active laboratory projects under scientific mentorship. Interested students should review the laboratory's recruitment information and inquire about available projects, research expectations, scheduling, and eligibility requirements. The documented high-school internship opportunities are unpaid.

name: CUNY STEM Research Academy
title: Paid High School STEM Research and University Laboratory Internship Program
description: The CUNY STEM Research Academy provides New York City public high-school students with opportunities to explore scientific research and participate in mentored STEM experiences at City University of New York institutions. The program emphasizes authentic scientific investigation, research preparation, and exposure to university-level research environments. Eligible participants may be matched with summer research experiences and receive competitive stipends while contributing to projects under the guidance of faculty or research mentors. The program particularly targets students in grades 10 and 11, although exact eligibility requirements may vary by application cycle and participating campus. Interested students should consult the official CUNY website for current application procedures, school eligibility, participating institutions, deadlines, and stipend details.

name: Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience High School Internship
title: Paid Materials Science and Nanoscience Summer Research Internship
department: Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience
description: The Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln offers a paid summer research internship for high-school students interested in materials science, nanotechnology, physics, chemistry, and engineering. Participants engage in approximately eight weeks of mentored laboratory research and contribute to active scientific projects involving materials and nanoscale systems. The program provides opportunities to develop experimental techniques, understand scientific methodology, and communicate research findings through a final poster presentation. Published information for the 2026 program identified compensation of approximately $15 per hour. Applicants should consult the official program page for current eligibility requirements, research dates, compensation, application deadlines, and available placements.

name: Mohan Lab — High School Summer Internship
title: Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience and Computational Research Internship
description: The Mohan Lab at the University of Houston offers a summer research internship for eligible high-school students entering their senior year. The approximately eight-week program introduces participants to biomedical engineering research through projects that may involve neuroscience, experimental bench techniques, computational analysis, and biomedical data interpretation. Students work with laboratory researchers, develop scientific skills, and present findings from their research experiences. The laboratory also describes opportunities for some students to continue research involvement beyond the initial summer experience, depending on project needs and mentorship availability. Interested applicants should review the official high-school internship page for current eligibility requirements, application procedures, deadlines, and program expectations.

name: Georgetown Lombardi Cancer Center Summer Research Volunteer Program
title: Cancer Biology and Oncology Summer Research Volunteer Internship
description: The Georgetown Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center Summer Research Volunteer Program provides high-school students with opportunities to participate in cancer research under the mentorship of university scientists and laboratory research teams. The program offers approximately eight weeks of full-time research involvement, allowing participants to contribute to independent projects related to cancer biology, oncology, and biomedical science. Students gain exposure to experimental techniques, scientific investigation, research methods, and the professional environment of a comprehensive cancer research center. The program emphasizes substantive research participation rather than classroom-only instruction. Interested students should consult the official program page for current age and grade eligibility, volunteer requirements, application deadlines, and research-placement availability.

name: Duke University Neuroscience Experience (DUNE)
title: Paid High School Neuroscience Summer Research Internship
description: The Duke University Neuroscience Experience (DUNE) is a paid summer research program designed to provide eligible local high-school students with hands-on neuroscience research experience at Duke University. Participants spend approximately eight weeks working in university neuroscience research environments under individualized mentorship from researchers. The program introduces students to scientific investigation, experimental methods, research communication, and the interdisciplinary study of the brain and nervous system. Participants also receive professional development and exposure to scientific careers and university research culture. Interested applicants should review the official Duke Institute for Brain Sciences website for current geographic eligibility restrictions, application deadlines, compensation, and program requirements.

name: Mount Sinai Student Research Volunteers
title: High School Biomedical and Clinical Research Volunteer Program
university: Mount Sinai Health System / Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
description: Mount Sinai's Student Research Volunteer pathway provides eligible high-school students with opportunities to participate in basic-science and clinical research activities within the Mount Sinai Health System and its affiliated medical research environment. Research involvement may include computer-based scientific work, data analysis, and laboratory-based research depending on the student's age, preparation, and available research placements. The official program information identifies a minimum age of 15 for computer-based research and 16 for wet-laboratory research. Opportunities may be available throughout the year, subject to institutional requirements and research-team availability. Interested students should review the official student research volunteer information for current eligibility, application procedures, required approvals, and placement expectations.

name: Northwestern University Physics & Astronomy Faculty Research
title: Physics, Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Prospect
description: Northwestern University's Department of Physics and Astronomy provides opportunities for motivated high school students to explore participation in faculty-led research. Research areas across the department include astrophysics, cosmology, particle physics, condensed matter physics, computational physics, and experimental physics. The department's outreach information encourages interested high school students to contact faculty members about potential research involvement. Students should identify professors whose research matches their interests and inquire about available projects, supervision, and laboratory requirements. Placement depends on faculty availability and is not guaranteed.

name: Georgia Tech R.E.A.L. Experience
title: Engineering, Science and Technology Laboratory Research Experience
department: Center for Education Integrating Science, Mathematics, and Computing
description: Georgia Tech's R.E.A.L. Experience connects high school students with authentic research environments at the Georgia Institute of Technology. The program provides a five-week research experience in which students work alongside participating teachers and university researchers on STEM-related investigations. Students gain exposure to laboratory procedures, scientific inquiry, research methods, and the process of investigating real scientific and engineering questions. Participants must satisfy the program's age and eligibility requirements, including being at least 16 years old. Availability and research placements depend on the current program cycle.

name: McGovern Medical School High School Summer Research Program
title: Biomedical Science and Molecular Biology Summer Laboratory Research
department: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston offers a high school summer research program through its Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. Participants spend approximately four weeks gaining experience with laboratory research, experimental methods, and biomedical science under the guidance of faculty and student mentors. The program introduces students to the research environment of a major academic medical center and provides opportunities to develop laboratory skills and scientific understanding. The advertised 2027 program costs approximately $4,000, making it a tuition-based research experience rather than a paid internship. Students should review the official program page for current eligibility, dates, and application requirements.

name: Sarah Lawrence College Science Research: Methods and Ethics
title: Scientific Research Methods, Experimental Design and Research Ethics
description: Sarah Lawrence College offers a two-week precollege science research course focused on the methods and ethical considerations involved in conducting scientific investigations. Students explore research design, develop questions, collect and analyze data, and examine how scientific evidence is produced and interpreted. Faculty guide students through research-related activities while emphasizing responsible scientific practices and critical thinking. The program awards two college credits and provides an introduction to college-level scientific research. It is best categorized as a research-oriented academic course rather than a long-term independent laboratory internship.

name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
title: Biomedical Science, Molecular Biology and Laboratory Research Internship
description: Rockefeller University's Summer Science Research Program provides high school students with an intensive summer experience in biomedical and biological research. Participants work in research teams under scientific mentorship, developing and investigating research questions while gaining experience with laboratory methods and data analysis. The program introduces students to the research culture of Rockefeller University, an institution specializing in fundamental biomedical science. Applicants generally must be at least 16 years old and meet the program's high school grade-level requirements. This summer program is distinct from Rockefeller's academic-year LAB Jumpstart initiative, although the two programs are connected through the university's science outreach efforts.

name: Loyola Marymount University CURes — The Living City
title: Urban Ecology, Environmental Science and Applied Field Research
description: Loyola Marymount University's Center for Urban Resilience offers The Living City, a summer experience introducing high school students to urban ecology and environmental research. Participants investigate ecological questions within urban environments through field activities, scientific observation, and applied research projects. The experience emphasizes the relationships between cities, biodiversity, environmental sustainability, and ecosystem processes. Students gain exposure to ecological research methods and the challenges of studying natural systems in urban landscapes. This is a short precollege research experience rather than a conventional long-term university laboratory internship.

name: Case Western Reserve University Physiology & Biophysics Faculty Research
title: Physiology, Biophysics and Biomedical Research Prospect
description: Case Western Reserve University's Department of Physiology and Biophysics provides a pathway for high school students interested in participating in faculty-led biomedical research. The department's research opportunities page specifically directs high school students seeking part-time laboratory experience or summer internships to contact individual faculty members. Research across the department spans physiology, biophysics, cellular processes, molecular mechanisms, and biomedical science. Interested students should identify investigators whose work matches their interests and contact them directly regarding potential research positions. Participation depends on faculty availability, laboratory requirements, and available mentorship.

name: Salk Institute Heithoff-Brody High School Summer Scholars
title: Molecular Biology, Genetics and Biomedical Science Summer Research Internship
description: The Salk Institute's Heithoff-Brody High School Summer Scholars program provides eligible high school students with an eight-week paid research internship in active scientific laboratories. Participants work with Salk researchers and mentors while gaining experience with experimental methods, scientific investigation, and the daily practices of biomedical research. Research areas at the institute include molecular biology, genetics, neuroscience, cancer biology, developmental biology, and related biological sciences. Applicants generally must be at least 16 years old and satisfy the program's San Diego County eligibility requirements. The program offers substantial exposure to research at a major independent biological research institute.

name: University of Maryland Physics PROPEL
title: Physics Research, Scientific Computing and University Research Mentorship
description: The University of Maryland's Department of Physics has documented PROPEL, a research-focused initiative connecting high school students with university physics researchers. The initiative has provided opportunities for students to engage with scientific investigation, physics-related projects, and mentorship in an academic research environment. Activities may involve exposure to research methods, scientific computing, data analysis, and the broader process of conducting physics research. The available university information documents previous participation rather than confirming a currently open application cycle. Students should contact the department to determine whether the initiative remains active or whether comparable opportunities are available.

name: Columbia Lamont Next Generation of Hudson River Scientists and Educators
title: Hudson River Environmental Science, Ecology and Field Research
description: Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory has documented the Next Generation of Hudson River Scientists and Educators initiative, which engages students in environmental science and Hudson River research. Participating students investigate the river ecosystem through field-based scientific activities, environmental observations, data collection, and analysis. The initiative emphasizes understanding regional waterways and developing scientific skills through direct engagement with environmental research. Participation has involved students from schools in Rockland County, Westchester County, and northern New Jersey. This initiative is distinct from Lamont's Secondary School Field Research Program, and students should consult the official information to determine current participation pathways.

name: Genspace Biorocket Research Internship
title: Biotechnology, Genetic Engineering and Molecular Biology Research Internship
description: Genspace's Biorocket Research Internship provides New York City high school students with an extended biotechnology research experience in a community laboratory environment. Participants receive training in laboratory methods, genetic engineering, molecular biology, and experimental research while working with scientific mentors. The program runs for approximately six months and emphasizes hands-on scientific investigation, biotechnology skills, and the development of research experience. Eligible applicants generally must be at least 16 years old and attend a New York City public or charter high school. The program advertises a $2,000 stipend, making it a paid research opportunity rather than a tuition-based course.

name: Seattle Science Lab Secondary Research Opportunities Program
title: Scientific Research Mentorship and Independent STEM Capstone Project
description: Seattle Science Lab's Secondary Research Opportunities Program provides high school students with a structured research mentorship experience lasting approximately twelve weeks. Students work toward an individual research capstone that may involve experimental investigation, scientific literature analysis, computational work, or the development of a technology prototype. The program emphasizes research planning, scientific reasoning, data interpretation, and communication of research findings. Participants receive guidance throughout the research process while developing a project related to their interests. Students should consult the official program information for current eligibility, costs, scheduling, and mentorship arrangements.

name: Wistar Institute High School Fellowship in Biomedical Research
title: Biomedical Science, Molecular Biology and Experimental Laboratory Research
description: The Wistar Institute offers a High School Fellowship in Biomedical Research that introduces students to laboratory investigation at a major biomedical research institution. Participants spend approximately four weeks working in a training laboratory and gaining experience with scientific methods, experimental procedures, and biomedical research concepts. The program provides exposure to research areas associated with Wistar's work in cancer biology, immunology, molecular biology, and infectious disease. Students develop laboratory skills while receiving scientific guidance and learning how biomedical investigations are conducted. Applicants should consult the official program page for the upcoming application cycle, eligibility requirements, and available placements.

name: Temple University and Heights Philadelphia STEM Research Internship
title: Engineering, Applied Science and University Laboratory Summer Research
description: Temple University's College of Engineering collaborates with Heights Philadelphia to provide high school students with summer STEM research experiences. Participants spend approximately six weeks engaging in faculty-led engineering and applied science projects within a university research environment. Students receive mentorship, develop research skills, and gain experience with scientific investigation, laboratory procedures, and communicating technical findings. The program has included final presentations in which students share their research experiences and project outcomes. Access is organized through the Heights Philadelphia partnership rather than through an unrestricted nationwide application, so students should verify current eligibility and recruitment procedures.

name: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
title: Artificial Intelligence, Medical Imaging and Biomedical Data Science Research
department: Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging
description: Stanford University's Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging offers a summer research internship introducing high school students to artificial intelligence applications in medicine. Participants engage with research topics involving machine learning, medical imaging, healthcare data, and computational approaches to biomedical problems under scientific mentorship. The program emphasizes understanding how artificial intelligence can be developed and evaluated for medical research and clinical applications. Students gain exposure to research methodology, computational investigation, and communication of scientific findings. This summer internship is distinct from AIMI's academic-year continuation program, which is intended for selected previous summer participants.

name: Stanford Inspiring Future Scientists Program
title: Chemistry, Experimental Science and University Laboratory Research Exposure
description: Stanford University's Department of Chemistry offers the Inspiring Future Scientists program to introduce eligible high school students to chemistry research and the university laboratory environment. The program provides exposure to experimental chemistry, scientific methods, and the work conducted by academic researchers. Students participate in structured scientific activities and gain insight into the research process through interactions with university scientists and mentors. Admission is competitive and has included a recommendation requirement, with eligibility focused on qualifying local students. This opportunity is primarily a research-exposure and laboratory-learning experience rather than a guaranteed independent research placement.

name: University of Florida Gainesville Emerging Scientist Training
title: Chemistry, Molecular Imaging and Scientific Instrumentation Research Training
department: Center for Precollegiate Education and Training
description: The University of Florida's Gainesville Emerging Scientist Training program introduces local high school juniors and seniors to university laboratory science and research techniques. The short program provides approximately two days of scientific training involving molecular imaging, laboratory instrumentation, and data analysis. Participants learn about experimental methods and gain exposure to equipment and scientific practices used in academic research. The experience is designed to develop familiarity with research environments rather than provide a sustained independent research internship. Students should review the official program page for current eligibility, scheduling, and application requirements.

name: Meharry Medical College High School STEM Internship Program
title: Biomedical Science, Biological Research and Community Health Research Internship
department: Research and Innovation / Together for Change Great Health Study
description: Meharry Medical College offers a High School STEM Internship Program connected to its research and community health initiatives. The advertised program involves mentored scientific experiences across two eight-week summer sessions in 2026 and 2027, providing students with opportunities to learn about biomedical research and scientific investigation. Participants may gain exposure to biological research methods, data analysis, laboratory practices, and health-related scientific questions. The advertised cohort targets students entering their junior year in 2026, so the program should not be assumed to be accepting new applicants for a separate 2027 cohort. Interested students should review the official program information for eligibility, recruitment status, and future opportunities.

name: Hormel Institute High School Summer Research Scholars
title: Cancer Biology, Molecular Biology and Biomedical Science Summer Research
university: University of Minnesota — The Hormel Institute
description: The Hormel Institute at the University of Minnesota offers a High School Summer Research Scholars program that provides students with mentored biomedical research experience. Participants spend approximately eight weeks working about 25 hours per week in a scientific research environment, learning laboratory techniques and contributing to research activities. The institute conducts research in areas including cancer biology, molecular biology, cell biology, and related biomedical sciences. Students receive individualized research guidance and opportunities to communicate their work through presentations. The program advertises a $3,000 stipend, making it a paid summer research opportunity.

name: University of South Alabama Borchert Lab High School Summer Research
title: Genomics, Cancer Biology and Computational Biomedical Research Prospect
description: The Borchert Laboratory at the University of South Alabama has documented high school student participation in summer research involving genomics, cancer biology, and biomedical science. Students have worked alongside graduate student mentors on projects incorporating laboratory experimentation and computational analysis. The research environment provides exposure to molecular biology, gene regulation, oncology, bioinformatics, and scientific data interpretation. This listing is based on documented high school research participation rather than an advertised recurring internship application. Interested students should contact the laboratory or relevant university researchers to determine whether additional high school research opportunities are available.

name: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program
title: Genetics, Genomics and Biomedical Science Summer Research
description: The Jackson Laboratory's Summer Student Program provides a ten-week research experience for eligible undergraduate students and graduating high school seniors. Participants work on authentic genetics, genomics, and biomedical research projects under the mentorship of experienced scientists. Research may involve molecular biology, computational biology, disease genetics, cancer biology, or related experimental approaches. Students gain experience with research methods, scientific data analysis, and communicating their findings through presentations. The program has advertised compensation of approximately $7,000, although applicants should verify current financial support, eligibility, and program locations.

name: Rockefeller University Summer Neuroscience Program
title: Neuroscience, Experimental Design and Brain Research Experience
description: Rockefeller University's Summer Neuroscience Program introduces eligible New York City public high school students to neuroscience research through an intensive two-week experience. Participants explore neuroscience concepts, develop and conduct an original experiment, and learn about the scientific research process. The program incorporates journal clubs, laboratory visits, scientific discussions, and presentations of student findings. Applicants generally must be at least 16 years old and meet the program's school eligibility requirements. This is a short research-oriented educational program rather than a sustained summer laboratory internship.

name: Yale Pathways Research Internships
title: Faculty-Mentored Laboratory Research and Scientific Investigation
department: Yale Pathways to Science / Summer Research Internships
description: Yale Pathways Research Internships provide eligible high school students with approximately seven weeks of laboratory research at Yale University. Students work with graduate student, postdoctoral, or faculty mentors on authentic scientific projects while learning research techniques and developing analytical skills. The program has involved approximately 32 hours of research activities per week and an educational stipend of around $2,500. Participants gain experience with experimental investigation, research communication, and the university research environment. Access is restricted to eligible students within Yale Pathways rather than being available through an unrestricted nationwide application.

name: Harvard Undergraduate OpenBio Student Research Institute
title: Virtual Biomedical Science and Interdisciplinary Research Mentorship
description: The Harvard Undergraduate OpenBio Student Research Institute offers a virtual research mentorship experience organized by Harvard undergraduate students. Selected high school participants work with research mentors, including doctoral researchers, to explore scientific questions and develop research-related projects. Depending on mentor availability and project design, activities may involve literature-based investigation, data analysis, computational approaches, or original research development. The program emphasizes scientific reasoning, research communication, and exposure to academic research practices. Students should verify the current application cycle, program structure, eligibility, and whether particular projects involve original data collection.

name: Roswell Park High School SURE-CAN
title: Six-Week High School Cancer Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open Oct 1, 2026–Jan 1, 2027.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Six-week, full-time mentored cancer research with laboratory, epidemiology, or computational projects, lectures, and a final poster. Applicants must be current high school juniors (class of 2028), at least 15 by June 27, 2027, US citizens/permanent residents, and both reside and attend school in Erie, Niagara, Cattaraugus, or Chautauqua County, NY.

name: Roswell Park College SURE-CAN
title: Ten-Week Undergraduate Cancer Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open Oct 1, 2026–Jan 1, 2027.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Ten-week full-time mentored cancer research with wet-lab, clinical, epidemiological, or computational projects. Applicants must be US citizens/permanent residents and either college juniors or sophomores participating in SUNY C-STEP, LSAMP, or McNair. Selected interns receive a $6,000 subsistence allowance; lodging is not provided.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
title: Selective Residential Summer Research Program
university: Center for Excellence in Education / MIT / Stanford
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open; deadline Dec 11, 2026.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Cost-free six-week science and engineering research program with intensive coursework, mentored individual projects, and written and oral research presentations. Open to eligible high school juniors; sophomores and seniors are not eligible. 2027 programs take place at MIT and Stanford.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
title: Six-Week Faculty-Mentored Summer Research
applicationWindow: 2027 application expected Nov 15, 2026; consult official site for nomination and application deadlines.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Six-week research placement with Stony Brook faculty in science, mathematics, or engineering, ending with a research poster. Applicants must be high school juniors, US citizens/permanent residents, and at least 16 at program start; school nomination is required, with a maximum of three nominees per school.

name: Barrow Summer High School Internship Program
title: Five-Week Neuroscience and Laboratory Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications Jan 4–Feb 12, 2027.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Five-week part-time placement in a research laboratory or supporting department, with faculty mentorship, seminars, and a final symposium. High school students must be at least 16 by the internship start; specific laboratory placements are not guaranteed.

name: Chicago EYES on Cancer
title: Two-Year Cancer Research and Mentorship Program
applicationWindow: 2027 application opening not yet confirmed on official page; sign up for updates.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Two-year program with two eight-week summer research placements, monthly enrichment, and a $5,000 annual stipend. High school sophomores through seniors and college freshmen/sophomores may apply; high school applicants must reside in specified Chicago-area counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. Applicants must be at least 16 at program start.

name: UT Southwestern STARS Summer Research Program for Students
title: Eight-Week Biomedical Laboratory Research Internship
department: Science Teacher Access to Resources at Southwestern
applicationWindow: 2027 applications Nov 16, 2026–Jan 22, 2027.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Eight-week nonresidential, stipend-supported faculty laboratory research placement for high school juniors in North Texas. Applicants must be at least 16 by June 1 and eligible to work in the US. Intended for students without prior research experience; work is biomedical laboratory research, not clinical shadowing.

name: UChicago Advanced Research Internship
title: Undergraduate Cancer Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 summer dates Jun 6–Aug 13; current application opening not verified.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Ten-week full-time laboratory cancer research placement plus academic-year mentorship and enrichment, with a $5,000 stipend. Applicants must be college sophomores or juniors with a strong academic record and prior research experience; a minimum 3.0 GPA is required. Housing and transportation are not provided.

name: Non-Trivial Research Fellowship
title: Online Independent Research and Expert Mentorship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open; early-bird Nov 15, 2026; final Jan 4, 2027.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Free online program for ages 14–20 who have not started university, supporting independent research on important real-world problems. Participants progress through research foundations and a fellowship; selected Research Scholars may receive further expert mentorship and scholarship awards. Research Scholar status and awards are competitive, not guaranteed.

name: Stanford AIMI Student Research Internships
title: Ongoing Medical Imaging AI Research Placement
department: Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging
applicationWindow: Ongoing interest/application pathway described on Stanford AIMI student page; no fixed 2027 deadline verified.
ratingNote: Editorial estimate of research depth and selectivity; not an official institutional ranking.
summary: Limited unpaid research placements in medical-imaging artificial intelligence for high school and undergraduate students. Applicants should have significant Python or MATLAB experience, basic machine-learning knowledge, completed introductory calculus, and ability to commit at least one year. This is separate from AIMI’s summer program and alumni-only academic-year program.
