name: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
title: Faculty-Mentored Summer Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open December 7, 2026 and close February 12, 2027. The university will finalize 2027 mentor placements, dates, and tuition in November 2026.
ratingNote: Genuine faculty-mentored research with original projects and presentation opportunities. Application and tuition fees apply, although financial-need waivers are available.
summary: Eight-week full-time research experience at George Mason and collaborating institutions. Participants work on projects selected by faculty mentors and develop scientific communication skills. High school and undergraduate students may apply. Students generally must be at least 15 for computational or remote placements and 16 for wet-laboratory placements; confirm 2027 requirements. Recently published costs are a $25 application fee and $1,299 tuition for three college credits, with need-based waivers. Housing is not provided to minors.

name: Mount Sinai SPARKED Research Internship
title: Ten-Month Cancer Research and Bioinformatics Training
university: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
applicationWindow: The 2026 application cycle is closed. The official website asks students to check again in December 2026 for the 2027 cycle. No 2027 application deadline has been confirmed.
ratingNote: Sustained cancer research mentorship and scientific presentation. Eligibility is restricted to qualifying NYC public high school students.
summary: Ten-month research program combining preparation meetings, six weeks of summer wet-lab or computational cancer research, and continued part-time activities during the academic year. Applicants must be rising high school juniors or seniors at NYC public schools, reside in one of the five boroughs, meet academic requirements including an 80% science average, and commit to the entire program. A stipend is provided for completing the summer internship.

name: Yao Laboratory — Student Research Opportunities
title: CRISPR, Gene Therapy and Muscle Biology Research
department: College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
applicationWindow: The laboratory explicitly invites high school and undergraduate student inquiries. No fixed deadline is published. Preference is given to students who can commit at least three semesters and 12 hours weekly, especially first- or second-year undergraduates. Positions depend on available laboratory capacity.
ratingNote: Direct laboratory research pathway explicitly welcoming high school students. Significant preferred time commitment may limit accessibility.
summary: The Yao Lab investigates CRISPR-based genome engineering, gene therapies for muscular disorders, cell biology, and muscle-related traits in livestock. The laboratory invites high school and undergraduate students to inquire about joining research projects. Long-term involvement is preferred, and UGA students may pursue research credit or related fellowship opportunities.

name: UCSF SEP High School Intern Program (HIP)
title: Eight-Week Paid Biomedical Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open January 15, 2027 and close February 15, 2027 according to the official 2027 timeline. An older FAQ on the same webpage lists a different previous deadline.
ratingNote: Paid mentored research on original biomedical projects, with strict eligibility limited to San Francisco public and charter school students.
summary: Eight-week paid biomedical research internship pairing rising high school seniors with UCSF scientist mentors. Participants conduct original research, present findings, and receive college counseling. Students must attend a San Francisco Unified School District public high school or San Francisco public charter school; no exceptions are permitted. The 2027 program lists approximately 35 hours per week and $4,500 upon full completion.

name: Sonmezoglu Lab — High School Research Inquiry
title: Biomedical Sensors and Electrical Engineering Laboratory Research
department: Biomedical Engineering and Integrated Systems Research
applicationWindow: High school students are invited to email Professor Sonmezoglu about research opportunities. No fixed application deadline or guaranteed high school position is listed. Northeastern undergraduates may also inquire, with undergraduate researchers generally expected to commit for at least an academic year.
ratingNote: Explicit faculty research inquiry route in advanced biomedical engineering. Research placement depends on current project and mentoring availability.
summary: The Sonmezoglu Lab develops electronics, sensors, microfabricated systems, and wireless technologies for health monitoring and biomedical applications. High school students are explicitly encouraged to contact the laboratory about research involvement. Undergraduate students may also inquire about projects in biomedical devices and integrated systems.

name: Matthew Griffin Lab — Summer High School Research
title: Chemical Biology and Host–Microbe Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The lab's recruitment page was updated September 23, 2026. High school students may submit a CV, transcript, and approximately 100-word description of research interests by email. High school placements are generally summer-only. Undergraduate applicants have separate requirements and an expected long-term commitment.
ratingNote: Laboratory with explicit, recently updated high school research inquiry instructions and opportunities involving bioinformatics and synthetic biology.
summary: The Griffin Lab studies chemical biology, host-microbe interactions, microbial glycans, and immunity. High school students may inquire about summer research involving bioinformatics and synthetic biology while working with laboratory members. Undergraduates may apply for longer-term positions. Acceptance and project assignments depend on available opportunities.

name: Georgia Cancer Center Summer Research Experiences (GCC SRE)
title: Six-Week High School Cancer Research Internship
applicationWindow: 2027 applications opened October 15, 2026 and close January 15, 2027. The program runs June 2–July 14, 2027.
ratingNote: Six-week mentored cancer research program with confirmed 2027 application dates. Housing and stipends are not provided.
summary: Augusta University Georgia Cancer Center provides six weeks of mentored high school research in cancer immunology, molecular biology, clinical outcomes, bioinformatics, computational biology, and related fields. Applicants must be at least 16 to work on bench laboratory projects; younger high school students may apply for bioinformatics or community-based research projects. No housing or stipend is provided.

name: Salk Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (Salk SURF)
title: Nine-Week Paid Biomedical Research Fellowship
applicationWindow: The Summer 2027 application is currently open. An application deadline was not provided in the official information reviewed. Program dates are June 7–August 6, 2027.
ratingNote: Paid research experience with mentorship, travel, and needed housing support. Restricted to eligible undergraduate or transferring community college students.
summary: Nine-week Salk Institute fellowship combining a virtual training week with eight weeks of in-person biomedical research. Applicants must be at least 18, eligible to work in the United States, pursuing a STEM-related degree, and entering their junior or senior undergraduate year, or be community college students in their transfer year. Minimum GPA requirements are 3.0 overall and 2.5 in science. Participants receive an hourly wage, U.S. roundtrip travel, and housing as needed.

name: SIAM-Simons Undergraduate Summer Research Program
title: Eight-Week Applied Mathematics and Computational Science Research
university: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM)
applicationWindow: Applications for Summer 2027 are expected to open in late 2026. No exact opening date or application deadline has been published for undergraduate participants.
ratingNote: Intensive research with individual mentoring, stipends, travel and lodging support, and opportunities to present mathematical research.
summary: Eight-week research program in applied mathematics and computational science across five U.S. sites. Each site hosts one faculty mentor and two students. Participants receive weekly stipends, coverage of lodging, meals, and travel, and opportunities to present research. Applicants must remain undergraduates in September 2027, attend a U.S. college or university, and be U.S. citizens or permanent residents. The program aims to broaden participation in mathematical and computational sciences.

name: Ludwig Princeton Summer Internship
title: Nine-Week Cancer Biology Research Internship
applicationWindow: Summer 2027 applications are scheduled to open in November 2026. The official program page has not published an exact deadline.
ratingNote: Cancer biology research with stipend, housing, and exposure to translational medicine. Restricted to qualifying Princeton and Rutgers undergraduates.
summary: Nine-week cancer biology research internship at Princeton University or Rutgers Cancer Institute, featuring laboratory mentorship, lectures, and exposure to clinical research. Applicants must be rising sophomores or juniors enrolled full-time at Princeton or Rutgers. Participants receive a weekly stipend, dormitory housing, and up to $600 in transportation reimbursement with receipts.

name: Meza Research Group — High School and Undergraduate Research
title: Nanoarchitected Materials and Mechanical Engineering Research
description: The Meza Research Group studies the mechanics of nanoarchitected materials. The group reports current openings for motivated undergraduate researchers and limited research positions for exceptional high school students. Undergraduate applicants are asked to email Professor Meza with a two-page CV; high school students should contact the professor to discuss eligibility, project availability, and research expectations. No fixed application window is posted.

name: OHSU CORE Community Research Internship
title: Community-Engaged Public Health and Research Internship
description: The OHSU Community Outreach, Research and Engagement (CORE) Internship offers undergraduates experience with research and program evaluation for nonprofit, government, and academic community partners. Work may include health-related data collection, community assessments, evidence-based program evaluation, and assistance on investigator-led research projects. Applications are considered in academic-quarter cycles, depending on available projects. The OHSU-PSU School of Public Health has posted an undergraduate application page; confirm the current quarter’s acceptance status before applying.

name: Tim Duong Lab — High School and Undergraduate Research
title: Biomedical Imaging, MRI and Medical Data Research
description: The Duong laboratory reports hosting high school and undergraduate students from across the country for summer research, often continuing part-time during the school year. Some projects can be completed remotely. Its stated criteria include strong academic standing (top 10% of class) and willingness to commit through the summer, with limited stipends depending on funding and productivity. Interested students may contact Tim Duong or individual faculty members to discuss projects and availability; no fixed deadline is listed.

name: OHSU Gibbs Lab Fluorescence Molecular Imaging Internship
title: Ten-Week Molecular Imaging Research Internship
description: The Gibbs Laboratory Fluorescence Molecular Imaging Internship trains high school and college students in a ten-week summer research experience. Projects can involve fluorescence imaging, microscopy, spectroscopy, cell culture, organic synthesis, immunostaining, data analysis, and scientific troubleshooting. OHSU lists the 2027 application period as January 4 through March 15, 2027; students may contact gibbsinternship@ohsu.edu for program details.

name: SUNY Oneonta Biological Field Station Summer Internships
title: Paid Aquatic Ecology and Field Research Internships
description: SUNY Oneonta Biological Field Station provides summer research internships involving lake and watershed ecology, fisheries and vegetation surveys, laboratory analysis, data interpretation, research reports, and posters. High school roles last eight weeks and are open to New York State residents age 16 or older by June 20; one of the approximately one to three high school places is reserved for an Otsego County resident. Undergraduate positions typically last ten weeks. The posted completion stipends are $3,500 for high school interns and $5,000 for undergraduates, with possible undergraduate housing. Application materials are expected in January 2027.

name: Indiana Biosciences Research Institute Biology Research Intern (2027)
title: Paid Translational Biology Summer Research Internship
description: The Indiana Biosciences Research Institute seeks biology research interns for May 17 through August 6, 2027. Interns assist with laboratory experiments, sample preparation, assay development, data collection, interpretation, and research presentations for translational biomedical projects. The institute lists a stipend of $9,650 for 35 hours per week. Applicants must be currently enrolled in or recently graduated from an eligible undergraduate or graduate life-science degree pathway, with Indiana education eligibility specified on the posting. Apply by November 30, 2026; the earlier October 15 priority date has passed.

name: Mount Sinai Abilities Research Center Volunteer Internship
title: Neurorehabilitation, Robotics and Human Research Internship
university: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
description: The Abilities Research Center offers a volunteer research internship open to high school and undergraduate students. Participants may assist with neurorehabilitation studies, data collection, analysis, scientific writing, and, depending on qualifications, technologies such as exoskeletons, robotic rehabilitation devices, and virtual reality. Projects may be on-site or remote. Applicants should email a CV and one-page research statement describing their background and interests. The center does not publish a fixed application deadline.

name: Purdue NanoX Lab — High School Research Inquiry
title: Microelectronics, Semiconductor Devices and AI Hardware Research
description: The NanoX laboratory at Purdue explicitly welcomes high school students, including those outside the Greater Lafayette area, to email Professor Li about potential research opportunities. The group focuses on microelectronics, semiconductor memory technologies, circuits, and computing hardware. Purdue ECE undergraduates can also explore research through ECE 496 and SURF. High school participation is inquiry-based, subject to mentorship capacity, and not an advertised guaranteed internship.

name: Morehouse Materials/Optics Research and Engineering (MORE) Lab
title: Undergraduate Quantum Optics and Photonics Research
description: The MORE Lab welcomes undergraduate researchers in optics, photonics, quantum science, and advanced materials. Students may contribute to experimental and computational projects, scientific presentations, and research collaborations. The lab directs interested undergraduate applicants to contact Dr. Wesley Sims with their major, class year, résumé or CV, and a short statement of interests. The separately advertised MORE-QuEST high school program is research exposure, not this undergraduate lab assistant role.

name: Michigan Psychoneuroimmunology (PNI) Lab Research Assistant
title: Undergraduate Psychology, Immunology and Medicine Research
description: The Michigan Psychoneuroimmunology Lab is accepting undergraduate research assistant applications on a rolling basis. Applicants with interests in psychology and medicine, human research data collection, or wet laboratory work are particularly encouraged. Participation requires enrollment in PSYCH 326 for three to four credits; the lab is not accepting volunteers, summer-only undergraduate interns, or high school students. Apply by emailing the lab manager a CV, tailored cover letter, and three references.

name: NYSCF Summer Science Internship (JAX Collaboration)
title: Ten-Week Stem Cell Biomedical Research Internship
university: New York Stem Cell Foundation / The Jackson Laboratory
applicationWindow: January 4–March 15, 2027; 2027 internship June 7–August 13.
ratingNote: Ten-week independent laboratory research with $7,000 stipend and transit assistance.
summary: Ten-week in-person internship in New York City pairing undergraduates with NYSCF researchers studying stem cells, human disease, and biotechnology. Applicants must be NYC residents, at least 18, enrolled full-time in undergraduate study with at least one completed college year, and eligible to work in the US. The program is nonresidential and full-time.

name: Huyck Preserve Odum Internship
title: Residential Ecology Field Research Internship
university: Huyck Preserve and Biological Research Station
applicationWindow: 2027 applications open January 4, 2027; program June 27–August 7, 2027.
ratingNote: Original field research and presentation with housing and modest living expense stipend.
summary: Full-time residential field-station internship for undergraduates conducting independent ecological research under a Summer Research Fellow. Up to four students typically participate; housing and equipment are provided with a $400 living-expense stipend. Interns also gain environmental education experience through a high-school summer program.

name: Duke–Marshall STAR Program Partnership
title: West Virginia High School Clinical Research Program
university: Duke Clinical Research Institute / Marshall University
applicationWindow: October 19, 2026–January 15, 2027; in person June 28–July 30, 2027.
ratingNote: Small cohort and faculty mentorship with research-methods training and stipend.
summary: New 2027 five-week clinical research training partnership at Marshall Health Network sites in West Virginia. Restricted to rising 11th- and 12th-grade high school students in West Virginia, including homeschool students. Includes mentored research, research methods, medical writing, and possible clinical observation. Stipend offered.

name: Duke–Cook Children’s RISE–STAR Affiliate Program
title: Texas High School Pediatric Clinical Research Internship
university: Duke Clinical Research Institute / Cook Children’s Medical Center

department: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
description: The Child Lab recruits undergraduate assistants for a longitudinal study of social-emotional development from infancy through adolescence. Activities include participating in lab sessions, video coding and data management. Recruiting for Winter 2026 and Spring 2027, with reviews beginning in October 2026. Desirable GPA 3.5; two letters of recommendation and a two-semester, nine-hours-per-week commitment are required.

name: Rice SWEL Lab
title: Behavioral Health and Stigma Research Assistant
description: The Stigma, Weight, Eating & Lifestyle (SWEL) Lab led by Erin Standen is recruiting undergraduate research assistants to begin Spring 2027. Students interested in behavioral health and social stigma can apply through the linked RA form. The lab provides an email contact for questions; exact project assignments and acceptance depend on openings.

name: CSUF Behavioral Health Promotion Lab
title: Psychology Education and Behavioral Health Research
description: CSUF’s Behavioral Health Promotion Lab, led by Yuko Okado, is recruiting undergraduates to study psychology learning and student pathways. Spring 2027 assistants primarily support the Psychology Pathways Project. Most positions involve three units of PSYC 499; research credit is preferred, and paid or volunteer positions depend on funding and vacancies. Application details: Recruiting undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027, with a possible computer science undergraduate opening in Summer 2027. CSUF students apply through Titan Connection; preference for PSYC 499 credit and one-year commitment. Not accepting high school applicants.

name: Tulane Learning and Brain Development Lab
title: Infant Learning and Brain Development Research Assistant
description: The Learning and Brain Development Lab at Tulane studies learning and cognitive development in infancy and childhood. It is accepting Tulane undergraduate research assistant applications for Spring 2027. Interested students submit the official form and may contact lab manager Kayla Brown for questions. Application details: Spring 2027 applications for Tulane undergraduates are due October 28, 2026 at 8 PM Central. Apply using the form on the lab recruitment page.

name: UMD Psychotherapy and Trauma Research Lab
title: Trauma and Psychotherapy Research Assistant
description: Dr. Catherine Reich’s Psychotherapy and Trauma Research Lab offers Spring 2027 undergraduate directed research on studies related to trauma and psychotherapy. Assistants help run participants and perform assigned research tasks, with training provided. Students must attend weekly meetings and be comfortable with sensitive discussion topics. Application details: Spring 2027 directed research for course credit; applicants must be enrolled at the University of Minnesota Duluth and in good standing. Complete the lab application form. Prior research experience is helpful but not required.

name: UVA Emotion and Behavior Lab
title: Emotion and Social Behavior Undergraduate Research
description: The Emotion and Behavior Lab in the University of Virginia Department of Psychology is recruiting undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027. It prioritizes students who can participate for several years. Applicants use the lab’s posted form; the lab will follow up after the deadline. Application details: UVA undergraduate applications for Spring 2027 research assistants are due November 10, 2026. Applications after that date may be considered for the following cycle; first- and second-year students are preferred.

name: Texas A&M CONGAlab
title: Executive Function and Decision Neuroscience Research Assistant
department: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
description: The CONGAlab at Texas A&M studies executive function, reward-based decisions, effort, and motivation. Undergraduate researchers may administer cognitive experiments, perform questionnaire and brain-data analysis, escort participants to imaging sessions, review literature, or write scripts. The laboratory encourages applicants with strong organizational skills and ideally a 3.5 GPA. Application details: Spring 2027 undergraduate research assistant applications are open, with review during pre-registration. Typically requires 6–12 hours each week and enrollment through NRSC/PBSI 491.

name: UNC Wilmington DISCO Lab
title: Social Communication and Relationship Research Assistant
description: The DISCO Lab at UNC Wilmington recruits undergraduate assistants for social-psychology projects. Its Spring 2027 opening focuses on in-lab data collection for a study of relationship communication. No prior research is required, but attendance at weekly meetings and a longer commitment are important. Application details: Recruiting one undergraduate research assistant for Spring 2027. Must attend Monday 4–5 PM lab meetings and ideally commit for at least two semesters. Apply through the lab form; typical summer participation is not available.

name: University of Arizona SCAN Lab
title: Cognitive Assessment and Psychology Volunteer Research Assistant
description: The University of Arizona SCAN Lab offers student research assistant roles involving cognitive and psychological assessments and interactions with research participants. Interested undergraduates submit the lab inquiry form for interviews. Academic credit may be possible, and paid technician roles are advertised separately through the university. Application details: The laboratory interviews undergraduate research assistants each semester and during summer. Spring 2027 interviews were scheduled to begin in early October 2026; new applicants should check remaining availability. The general volunteer recruitment notice says volunteers are not being recruited separately at present.

name: Texas Tech PEANUTs Lab
title: Developmental Psychopathology and Mental Health Research Assistant
description: Dr. Charlie Rioux’s PEANUTs Lab at Texas Tech recruits undergraduates to support developmental psychopathology and mental health research through literature screening, annotated bibliographies, survey development, and data collection. Apply through the online form with cover letter, résumé, unofficial transcript, and writing sample. Application details: Accepting undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027; rolling review began October 5, 2026 and continues until places are filled. Two-semester commitment and HUSC 4000 enrollment for three credits (nine hours weekly) required.

name: University of Kansas BRAIN Lab
title: Autism and Neurodevelopmental Research Assistant
description: The BRAIN Lab, directed by Matt Mosconi at the University of Kansas, studies brain development, movement, cognition, and sensory processing in neurodevelopmental conditions. Its research includes eye movement, motion analysis and MRI techniques. Undergraduate students may apply for its Spring 2027 research assistant openings. Application details: The BRAIN Lab is accepting applications for undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027 through the application linked on its official University of Kansas website.

name: Temple Dynamical Systems Laboratory
title: Lithium-Ion Battery Safety and Modeling Research Assistant
description: Temple University’s Dynamical Systems Laboratory seeks undergraduate researchers for mathematical modeling and safety evaluation of lithium-ion batteries. Candidates should be comfortable with dynamics, controls, and analytical methods. The lab advertises multiple Fall 2027 positions and directs inquiries to Professor Damoon Soudbakhsh. Application details: Multiple undergraduate and graduate research assistant openings are advertised for Fall 2027. Applicants should have preparation in dynamics, control, and analytical modeling, and contact Professor Damoon Soudbakhsh.

name: Boston University Spatial Development and Learning Lab
title: Child Spatial Cognition and Development Research Assistant
department: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
description: The Spatial Development and Learning Lab (SDLL) is accepting research assistant applications for Spring 2027. Applicants should be able to work in person in Boston, including at the Museum of Science, commit at least eight hours weekly for two semesters, and be available for three to four weekend days per semester. Students may help run child development studies and recruit participants. Apply using the laboratory's online form; college-level applicants are sought, and high school eligibility is not advertised.

name: Florida State Hermiller Lab
title: Brain Stimulation, fMRI and Memory Research Assistant
description: The Hermiller Lab invites undergraduate applications for Spring 2027 entry on a rolling basis. Students may join through directed individual study or volunteering and assist with study development, participant scheduling, behavioral tasks, MRI or transcranial magnetic stimulation research, eye tracking, and data quality checks. Applicants able to commit more than two semesters and at least nine hours weekly are preferred. Apply through the interest form on the lab's recruitment page.

name: UT Austin MUNA Lab
title: Neuropsychology, Aging and MRI Research Assistant
description: The MUNA Lab is accepting undergraduate research assistant applications for Spring 2027, with its interest form due December 28, 2026. Researchers may assist with neuropsychological literature reviews, participant recruitment, cognitive testing, MRI-related data collection, analysis and entry. Students must commit at least eight hours weekly for two semesters. Submit the RA interest form and email a CV and unofficial transcript to the lab.

name: Harvard Bergelson Lab Undergraduate Research Assistants
title: Infant Language Acquisition and Developmental Psychology Research
description: The Bergelson Lab is seeking undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027. Research investigates infant word learning, language comprehension, and developmental communication, using studies with families and child-language datasets. Interested undergraduate students should email a CV or resume and an unofficial transcript to lab managers Sophie Schoenbohm and Michika Ito. The lab does not offer remote undergraduate positions and explicitly does not offer high school opportunities at this time.

name: UConn Mozeiko Aphasia Rehabilitation Lab
title: Aphasia Treatment and Speech-Language Rehabilitation Research
description: Jennifer Mozeiko's Aphasia Rehabilitation Lab announced two undergraduate research assistant openings for Spring 2027. The laboratory studies rehabilitation approaches for individuals with aphasia and commonly works with several undergraduate assistants per semester. Students should consult the lab join page and contact the research team for current application instructions and eligibility; specific positions are limited.

name: University of Montana Minds Lab
title: Child Cognition and Social Development Research Assistant
description: The Minds Lab, directed by Rachel Severson, invites undergraduate research assistant applications for future semesters, including Spring 2027 consideration. Student researchers assist with child-focused psychology studies and educational outreach at the Missoula Public Library Living Lab. Assistants generally work six to nine hours weekly for course credit, with a preferred GPA of 3.0 and two-semester commitment. Apply through the lab form with a CV and unofficial transcript.

name: Rutgers READ Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Psychology and Eating-Disorder Research Assistant
description: The READ Lab led by Dr. Reilly plans to recruit undergraduate student researchers and summer research students. Rutgers undergraduates can help with study protocols, recruitment, data management, scientific reading and outreach. Undergraduate volunteers must currently be enrolled at Rutgers, commit around eight hours each week, and participate for at least two semesters or six months. Apply using the form on the official lab recruitment page; prospective roles depend on capacity.

name: University at Buffalo Jiayu Peng Research Lab
title: Scientific AI and Computational Materials Research Assistant
department: Department of Materials Design and Innovation
description: The Peng Research Lab currently advertises openings for University at Buffalo undergraduate students through the university Undergraduate Research program. Researchers explore artificial intelligence methods for understanding and designing chemical and materials systems. Interested current UB students should review the lab's project and email Professor Jiayu Peng with a CV and transcript. The listed opportunity is for university undergraduates, not high school students.

name: USC Learning, Development, and Rehabilitation Laboratory
title: Infant Movement and Motor Development Research Assistant
department: Division of Biokinesiology and Physical Therapy
description: The Learning, Development, and Rehabilitation Laboratory led by Dr. Kretch welcomes undergraduate and Doctor of Physical Therapy student research assistant applications on a rolling basis. Research assistants may help with behavioral coding, data collection, and community outreach in studies of learning and motor development. Course credit is available for psychology and some other undergraduates. Apply through the form on the lab's recruitment page; undergraduate-only listing.

name: Texas A&M CARES Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Clinical Psychology, Anxiety and Behavioral Health Research
department: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
description: The CARES Lab studies anxiety, related mental health concerns, and contextual factors influencing emotional health. The lab explicitly states that it is not recruiting undergraduate assistants for Spring 2027, with recruitment expected to resume for Summer and Fall 2027. Interested college students can review the lab application form; applicants need a 3.5 cumulative GPA, psychology background, at least nine hours per week and a two-semester commitment. No current Spring opening should be assumed.

name: Washington University Laboratory for Child Brain Development
title: Child Development, EEG and fNIRS Research Assistant
description: The Laboratory for Child Brain Development is recruiting undergraduate research assistants for Spring 2027. Assistants support family research sessions, behavioral coding, questionnaire data entry and EEG or fNIRS collection. Applicants need experience interacting with children, availability for weekend sessions, and a two-semester, 10-hour-per-week commitment. Apply using the laboratory form.

name: UTA Undergraduate Research Assistant Program
title: Paid Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research
description: The Undergraduate Research Assistant Program (URAP) funds mentored research positions with UTA faculty. Students assist with genuine faculty projects and develop research skills through structured participation. Applications for Spring 2027 are due November 6, 2026; selection depends on project needs and faculty matching. UTA undergraduates should review the official application guidance for minimum enrollment and other requirements.

name: University of Tennessee AMP Lab
title: Affective Neuroscience and Psychophysiology Research Assistant
description: The AMP Lab studies emotional and motivational processes using behavioral and physiological methods. Undergraduate research assistants may contribute to data collection, participant research, and analysis. The lab is accepting undergraduate applications for Spring 2027 and directs interested UT Knoxville students to submit its official application. Available positions and specific duties vary by ongoing projects.

name: Teachers College Columbia SMILE Research Lab
title: Developmental Psychology and Social Learning Research Assistant
description: The SMILE Research Lab at Teachers College advertises research assistant recruitment for projects involving development, learning and social behavior. Interested students can apply through the lab's official recruitment page. The available information does not clearly establish whether current undergraduates at Columbia or other universities are eligible, so prospective applicants must confirm eligibility and available positions directly before applying.

name: Illinois Gies Business Research Lab
title: Paid Business Research and Data Analysis Assistant
description: The Gies Business Research Lab recruits undergraduate research assistants for faculty-led studies in business and related fields. Students may perform data cleaning, analysis, literature research and project support. Paid opportunities are advertised for the current recruitment cycle, with applications accepted until positions are filled. Specific assignments and eligibility depend on the posted role.

name: Case Western Reserve Atit Lab
title: Developmental Genetics and Biological Research Assistant
description: The Atit Lab at Case Western Reserve studies developmental biology and genetic mechanisms underlying tissue formation. The group accepts undergraduate research assistant applications for Spring 2027, with a posted December 1, 2026 deadline. Students interested in molecular and developmental biology can submit the lab application and ask about available research projects and mentorship.

name: Yale Rangaraju Lab
title: Neuroscience and Proteomics Research Assistant
description: The Rangaraju Lab studies molecular mechanisms regulating synapses and neuronal function, including proteomics-based approaches. The lab offers undergraduate research opportunities and requests that students seeking Spring 2027 placements apply by October 31, 2026. Prospective assistants should review the laboratory application instructions and confirm current project capacity.

name: Yale Computational Clinical Science Lab
title: Computational Psychiatry and Clinical Data Research
description: The Computational Clinical Science Lab studies mental health and clinical psychology using quantitative methods, computational modeling and data analysis. The lab provides an undergraduate research assistant application pathway and recruits students according to project capacity. Interested undergraduates should review the current recruitment instructions to determine whether Spring 2027 places are available.

name: Purdue Cognition and Learning Lab
title: Memory, Learning and Experimental Psychology Research Assistant
description: Purdue's Cognition and Learning Lab conducts experimental research on learning, memory and cognition. Undergraduate students may assist with behavioral studies, participant sessions, data processing and related research activities. The laboratory maintains an undergraduate application route and evaluates prospective assistants based on current research needs and available mentorship.

name: Iowa State Kristi Costabile Research Group
title: Social Cognition and Narrative Psychology Research
description: Professor Kristi Costabile's research group studies social cognition, autobiographical memory and narrative processes. Undergraduate students interested in assisting with research can contact the professor through the university's faculty research information. Research positions may involve reading scientific literature, running behavioral studies and handling experimental data; openings depend on current projects.

name: Tufts University Blackiston Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Developmental Biology and Biohybrid Robotics Research
description: The Blackiston Lab studies how cell populations organize into tissues and uses living materials for biosensors and biohybrid devices. Tufts Biology lists two undergraduate research positions, with rolling review. Biology 13 is a prerequisite. Applications are reviewed from the previous two semesters when openings become available. Apply using the Tufts Biology undergraduate research form, submitted to biologyundergradresearch@tufts.edu.

name: Tufts University Deyle Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Marine Ecosystem Modeling and Quantitative Ecology Research
description: The Deyle Lab uses computational methods and ecological time series to investigate fishery dynamics and coral reef restoration. Tufts lists one to three research positions beginning Fall 2026, with rolling recruitment. Biology 132/133 and Biology 51 are advantageous depending on the project. Students should consult the lab's Connect page and follow its application instructions.

name: Tufts University Dopman Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Evolutionary Genomics and Adaptation Research
description: The Dopman Lab examines genetic, ecological and physiological causes of phenotypic variation, adaptation and speciation. Tufts lists one or two undergraduate positions during fall, spring and summer sessions. Application review dates are November 15 for spring, March 15 for summer and August 10 for fall. No specific prerequisites are listed. Apply through the Biology Department's undergraduate research application.

name: Tufts University Freudenreich Lab Undergraduate Research
title: DNA Replication and Genome Instability Research
description: The Freudenreich Lab uses yeast genetics and molecular techniques to investigate repetitive DNA, chromosome fragility and DNA repair. Tufts lists one or two undergraduate positions for Fall 2026–Spring 2027. Applications are rolling, and Genetics (Biology 41) is required. Students typically commit 10–15 hours weekly and should apply at least four weeks before the intended semester through the Biology undergraduate research form.

name: Tufts University Hernandez Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Mitochondrial DNA and Protein Biochemistry Research
description: The Hernandez Lab studies enzymes and nucleic acid-binding proteins involved in mitochondrial DNA replication and expression. Research techniques include recombinant protein purification, biochemical assays and studies of protein–nucleic acid interactions. Tufts lists two undergraduate openings with rolling applications and no stated course prerequisites. Submit the departmental undergraduate research application for consideration.

name: Tufts University McVey Lab Undergraduate Research
title: DNA Damage Responses and Drosophila Genetics Research
description: The McVey Lab investigates cellular responses to DNA breaks and damaged bases using fruit fly genetics, with connections to cancer and aging. Tufts lists one available position for Spring 2027, with applications reviewed in early November. Deadlines are November 15 for spring and March 15 for summer. Biology 13 and Biology 15 are required. Apply through the Tufts Biology undergraduate research application.

name: Tufts University Mirkin Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Genome Instability and Repeat Expansion Research
description: The Mirkin Lab investigates genome instability caused by repetitive DNA sequences and transcription–replication conflicts in yeast and cultured human cells. Tufts lists one undergraduate opening with rolling applications. Biology 41, biosafety training and at least 15 hours of laboratory work weekly are required. Selected applicants may be invited for an in-person interview. Apply through the Biology Department.

name: Tufts University Orians Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Plant Physiology and Herbivore Ecology Research
description: The Orians Lab studies how growing conditions affect plant chemistry, resource allocation, defensive traits and herbivore interactions. Tufts lists one undergraduate research position, with rolling applications. A background in plant biology, chemistry and laboratory techniques is preferred. Recruitment typically occurs one semester before the student begins a project. Apply using the Tufts Biology undergraduate research form.

name: Tufts University Reed Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Conservation Ecology and Species Extinction Risk Research
description: The Reed Lab studies habitat change, extinction risk and bird conservation, including island bird populations and forestry-related ecological research. Tufts lists one or two undergraduate openings and accepts applications on a rolling basis. Ecological experience is preferred, with skills in R statistics and GIS considered advantageous. Students interested in long-term ecological research and graduate study are particularly encouraged to apply.

name: Tufts University Romero Lab Undergraduate Research
title: Wild Bird Stress Physiology and Animal Behavior Research
description: The Romero Lab studies physiological and behavioral responses to stress in wild vertebrates, especially birds. Undergraduate researchers may contribute to behavioral observation, physiological monitoring, hormone assays and experimental design. Tufts lists one opening and rolling applications. Previous or concurrent Group B coursework, or its equivalent, is required. When openings occur, the lab reviews recent applications and invites selected candidates to interview.

name: Fei Xia Research Lab
title: Neuroengineering and Bioelectronics Research
description: The Xia Lab explicitly welcomes high school, undergraduate, and masters students to inquire about research. High school applicants may ask about opportunities outside its OPALS pathway. The lab currently highlights experience in animal models, cell culture and optoelectronic instrumentation as especially relevant; such experience is not stated as a universal prerequisite. Email the PI or use the inquiry form; placement is not guaranteed.

name: FaST Lab Summer Research Internship
title: High School Summer Research Internship
description: The FaST Lab describes a summer research internship for high school students involving food science research. Students interested in applying should consult the lab's official internship information for current eligibility, project availability and application instructions. The next application cycle has not been confirmed.

name: Yale Forests Student Research
title: Forest Ecology and Environmental Research
description: Yale Forests provides educational and research opportunities connected to forest ecology, conservation and environmental science. Students may inquire about possible research involvement, field activities or mentorship. Specific high school placement availability, supervision and eligibility should be confirmed before treating an inquiry as an accepted research position.

name: Beaury Lab — New York Botanical Garden
title: Invasion Ecology and Conservation Research
description: The Beaury Lab studies plant invasions, ecological change and conservation. Students interested in contributing to research can investigate the group's current projects and inquire about mentorship or research-assistant possibilities. A currently open high school position has not been confirmed, so this should be treated as an outreach prospect rather than a guaranteed internship.

name: Monell Chemical Senses Research
title: Chemical Senses and Behavioral Research
description: Monell Chemical Senses Center conducts interdisciplinary research on taste, smell and related sensory processes. High school students interested in research should consult the center's official student opportunity pages and inquire about applicable programs. Participation requirements and current openings may differ by program.

name: Alley Pond Field Biology Internship
title: Environmental Field Biology Internship
description: Alley Pond Environmental Center offers a field-oriented educational internship involving local environmental science, ecology and conservation activities. The program lists a $250 participation fee, with financial assistance available. Applicants should confirm current dates, eligibility and whether their specific placement involves independent research or primarily environmental education.

name: UNC Fry Lab FRESH Outcomes
title: Environmental Health and Community Research
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
description: The Fry Lab's FRESH-related work connects environmental health research with community engagement and research training. Interested high school students should confirm whether the current project has a student participation pathway, applicable geographic restrictions and an open recruitment process. It should not be interpreted as an automatically available laboratory position.

name: Turnbaugh Lab Summer Research Pathway
title: Microbiome and Biomedical Science Research
description: The Turnbaugh Lab conducts microbiome research involving microorganisms and host biology. Students may explore the lab's research and relevant UCSF student research pathways. A currently open high school-specific placement has not been verified, and prospective applicants should not assume that the lab recruits high school students directly.

name: UCI Blum Center Summer Scholars
title: Public Health and Community Research Experience
description: The UCI Blum Center is associated with interdisciplinary education and community-focused initiatives. The current existence, high school eligibility and availability of a Summer Scholars research pathway have not been fully verified. This listing requires confirmation from an official current program announcement before publication as an available opportunity.

name: Tennessee Center for Environmental Biotechnology
title: Environmental Biotechnology Research
description: Environmental biotechnology research at the University of Tennessee may involve microorganisms, biological systems and environmental applications. A specific current high school research opportunity associated with this center has not been verified. Students should confirm that the relevant research group is active and accepts inquiries before pursuing this listing.

name: Jing Tang — Tang Group
title: Materials, Batteries and AI-Assisted Chemistry Research
description: Professor Jing Tang explicitly welcomes talented high school students and undergraduates from any discipline. Current research includes battery materials, electrochemistry, AI-guided materials discovery, mineral recovery and sustainability. High-school applicants should inquire directly about capacity; the page does not guarantee an opening.

name: Tufts Summer Research Experience
title: Six-Week University Research Experience
description: Tufts offers a six-week in-person pre-college summer research experience combining exposure to university research projects with foundational skills workshops, speakers, and field trips. The 2027 application is scheduled to open December 14, 2026. This is a tuition-based pre-college program; consult the program for fees and project selection.

name: University of Arizona Young Global Leaders Program
title: Public Health Research and Laboratory Summer Program
description: Summer public-health program for current high school students featuring team-based small-scale investigations, data analysis, laboratory activities and a final showcase. Summer 2027 applications are expected in February 2027. Published cost is $350 with scholarships available. Students from outside Tucson must arrange housing and be accompanied by a parent or guardian remaining in Tucson.

name: George Mason Schar Young Scholars Research Program
title: Faculty-Mentored Multidisciplinary Research
department: Schar School of Policy and Government
description: George Mason Schar School offers faculty-mentored research activities for students in grades 9–12 across areas such as data science, bioinformatics, public policy and astronomy. Its official page lists 2026 offerings and says applications generally open in early February, with possible fall options. Fees and 2027 topics should be confirmed before applying.

name: Shukla Lab — High School Research Pathways
title: Biology and Nanoscience Student Research
description: The Shukla Lab states that high-school students can participate through the NanoExplorers Summer Research Program or Summer Biology Research Workshop rather than direct unrestricted lab placement. Interested students should apply through the respective programs and verify next-cycle eligibility, dates and application availability.

name: Boston College Quantum Materials Laboratory
title: Quantum Materials and Devices Research Inquiry
description: Boston College Quantum Materials Laboratory welcomes motivated undergraduates and, in some cases, high school students for projects involving quantum materials and devices. The page describes volunteer research and mentored projects tailored to background and availability. Contact Professor Ma to ask whether an appropriate supervised position exists; high-school admission is not guaranteed.

name: Mount Sinai Orthopaedics Research Labs Internship
title: Orthopaedic Biomedical Research Internship
university: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
description: Mount Sinai Orthopaedics Research Labs describes a research internship application pathway for high-school, undergraduate and post-baccalaureate students. Applicants are told to email an appropriate lab PI or Dr. James Iatridis with interests, availability and CV. The displayed acceptance notice refers to 2023, so current placement availability has not been confirmed; treat as a documented inquiry pathway only.

name: Duncan Lab — UMB CURE Scholars Research
title: Biomedical Engineering Research for Baltimore High School Scholars
description: The Duncan Lab documents paid summer biomedical engineering research internships for Baltimore City high-school students already enrolled as UMB CURE Scholars. Interns work with a graduate or postdoctoral mentor on an independent project. This is a restricted partner-program pathway, not open cold-email recruitment for all high-school students.

name: Wiseman Lab — Scripps High School Research Pathway
title: Protein Homeostasis and Chemical Biology Research
description: The Wiseman Lab explicitly welcomes high-school and undergraduate interns, but instructs applicants to use the Scripps Research High School Internship Program or Summer Undergraduate Research Program, respectively. Placement with this specific lab is not guaranteed and the relevant program may impose eligibility restrictions.

name: Nicholas Lab — UCI High School Research Pathway
title: Neuroendocrine and Immunology Research
description: The Nicholas Lab indicates that high-school students can train through UCI structured programs including the Youth Science Fellowship Program and UCI x GATI, but it does not accept high-school interns outside those programs. The lab studies immune-system regulation of gonadotropin secretion. Current program eligibility and placement must be checked independently; the lab also lists commitment and GPA criteria that should be clarified with its PI.

name: Hartstone-Rose Research Lab
title: Functional Morphology and Paleontology Research
description: The Hartstone-Rose Lab documents working with high-school students on functional morphology projects and invites interested students to explore lab participation. The lab uses anatomical approaches including dissection and imaging. Current high-school capacity is not stated; ask Dr. Adam Hartstone-Rose before assuming an opening.

name: LSU LCMC Health Cancer Center Summer Research Internship
title: Cancer Biology Summer Research Internship
description: Eight-week hands-on cancer research internship for high-school juniors or seniors ages 16–18 at application. Participants must live in or near the New Orleans area during the program and attend all dates and mandatory orientation. The program ends with a poster or oral research presentation. Confirm next-cycle dates on the official page.

name: University of Utah Engineering High School Summer Research Internship
title: Engineering Laboratory Summer Research
department: John and Marcia Price College of Engineering
description: Competitive no-cost, unpaid summer internship placing eligible high-school students in university engineering labs with a faculty-assigned research project and final symposium. The current page states applicants graduating in 2028 may apply; housing is not supplied. Verify deadline and cohort requirements on the application page.

name: University of Delaware CIS High School Faculty Lab Research
title: Computer Science Faculty Research Inquiry
department: Department of Computer and Information Sciences
description: The University of Delaware Computer and Information Sciences department states that selected faculty labs occasionally host motivated local high-school juniors and seniors for summer research in areas including human-computer interaction, cybersecurity and biomedical data. Students are instructed to identify aligned faculty labs and email a resume and brief statement, ideally in January–March. No specific professor placement is guaranteed.

name: Nihal Dharmasiri — Plant Molecular Biology Lab
title: Plant Development and Molecular Biology Research
description: The Dharmasiri laboratory explicitly accepts inquiries from motivated high-school juniors and seniors for short-term summer research projects lasting approximately four to six weeks. The research concerns plant molecular biology and development. Contact the laboratory to determine whether a particular summer has capacity.

name: James D. Lewis — Plant and Forest Ecology Research
title: Forest Ecology and Environmental Change Research
description: Fordham faculty member James D. Lewis explicitly states that research opportunities exist for high-school, undergraduate and graduate students interested in plant or forest ecology. Research addresses invasive species, climate change, urbanization and plant responses to environmental conditions. Students should contact him about current project and mentoring capacity.

name: Stanger-Hall Lab — Firefly Biology Research
title: Firefly Ecology and Biology Summer Research
description: The Stanger-Hall Lab explicitly directs high-school students interested in a summer research experience to inquire about applying through UGA’s Young Dawgs program. The group researches fireflies and related biological questions. This is a program-dependent pathway, not confirmed unrestricted admission directly into the laboratory.

name: Jin He Nano-Bio Research Laboratory
title: Nanobiotechnology and Single-Molecule Research
description: The Jin He lab states it accepts one or two teacher-recommended high-school students for summer research and also participates in institutional summer research internships. Work includes molecular electronics, nanobiotechnology and single-molecule biophysics. Recommendation and capacity requirements apply; verify a current summer opening before outreach.

name: Hudson Lab — Developmental Neurobiology High School Internships
title: Developmental Neurobiology Research Internship
department: Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology
description: The Hudson Lab says it occasionally hosts high-school students for research internships and instructs interested students to contact the professor directly. Its research opportunities page focuses on developmental neurobiology and bench research. High-school placements are occasional, not guaranteed or necessarily currently open.

name: Creighton HS-MACA/CPHHE Summer Research Institute
title: Biomedical and Community Health Summer Research
department: Center for Promoting Health and Health Equity
description: Creighton’s HS-MACA/CPHHE Summer Research Institute introduces high-school and college students to biomedical and community-based research. Participants are paired with faculty on ongoing projects or community organizations for participatory research and conclude with oral or poster presentations. Confirm current selection criteria and next-cycle application dates.

name: CUNY Language Acquisition Research Center — Advanced High School Internship
title: Child Language and Psychology Research Internship
university: Hunter College, City University of New York
description: The CUNY Language Acquisition Research Center accepts internship inquiries and notes that successful interns have very occasionally included advanced high-school students. Candidates submit a cover letter, resume, transcript, instructor recommendation, and availability; selection can include a child-speech transcription exercise and evaluation of research material. Its page currently says internships and independent studies are available but no research assistant positions.

name: Robert Catena — M.O.M. Biomechanics Lab
title: Movement and Occupational Mechanics Research Internship
description: Dr. Robert Catena explicitly invites exceptional local high-school students to discuss an internship in the M.O.M. Lab. Interested students should email to arrange a meeting; opportunities are not guaranteed. The lab also hosts undergraduate projects relating to biomechanics and movement.

name: Loyola CHARM — High School Biomedical Research Volunteers
title: Molecular Biology and Healthy Aging Volunteer Research
university: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
department: Center for Healthy Aging Research and Medicine
description: Loyola CHARM explicitly welcomes volunteers from high-school level and above to inquire about joining a basic research team. Interested students are directed to contact the program about research-lab volunteer opportunities; the site does not promise immediate openings or a specific placement.

name: Shaghayegh Bagheri — Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Laboratory
title: Advanced Manufacturing and Materials Research Inquiry
description: The Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Laboratory at George Mason University explicitly welcomes middle- and high-school students to contact the group about research opportunities. Its stated interests include additive manufacturing, polymer chemistry, and engineering design and analysis. Students should inquire about available projects rather than assume a vacancy.

name: UMES Geoscience Bridge Program
title: Paid Geosciences Summer Research and College Experience
description: The University of Maryland Eastern Shore describes a six-week paid Geoscience Bridge Program for high-school students considering geosciences careers. The program combines courses, field trips, hands-on activities and a stipend, with housing, meals and travel support described on the institutional summer-program page. Current-cycle availability and detailed eligibility must be reconfirmed.

name: UCSC Health Equity in Youth Lab — Youth Advisory Board
title: Adolescent Health and Psychology Research Advisory Experience
description: The Health Equity in Youth Lab invites middle- and high-school students to apply for its Youth Advisory Board. Members attend monthly online meetings to discuss study findings and help shape future research questions. This is research participation and advisory training, not a conventional laboratory research-assistant internship.

name: Stanford Social Learning Lab — FAST Research Pathway
title: Developmental Psychology Research Through FAST
description: Dr. Hyowon Gweon’s Social Learning Lab studies how children learn from other people. The lab says it generally does not admit high-school research assistants except through the Stanford FAST program; only program-admitted students can participate, and direct volunteer internships are not supported. A position with this specific laboratory is not guaranteed.

name: Nayak Lab — UCSF High School Summer Research Pathways
title: Microbiome and Immunology Research Through UCSF Programs
description: The UCSF Nayak Lab directs high-school applicants to the UCSF Science and Health Education Partnership (SEP) for summer internships instead of offering unrestricted high-school placements. Its institutional page also discusses research volunteering through the San Francisco VA for people aged 16 or older, subject to separate eligibility and clearance rules. Students should apply through the relevant program and must not assume assignment to this lab.

name: Zhicheng Jin Lab — High School Research Recruitment
title: Biomaterials and Analytical Chemistry Research Internship
description: The Jin Lab recruitment notice, updated August 2026, explicitly seeks two high-school students. Applicants are instructed to email Dr. Zhicheng Jin with a CV and use a subject line giving their high school, name and intended internship period. The laboratory develops materials for applications in human health; confirm whether the advertised slots remain open.

name: Stanford Rehabilitation Research Intern Program
title: Neurorehabilitation and Clinical Research Internship
university: Stanford Medicine / VA Palo Alto Health Care System
description: Stanford Medicine describes a year-round onsite rehabilitation research internship involving neuropsychology, neuroimaging, clinical research and research data management. High-school students age 17 and older are explicitly encouraged to apply. No remote positions are offered; the program asks candidates to use its application route and designated contact email, not individual mentors.

name: James Kirby — Kirby Laboratory Research Volunteers
title: Biomedical Laboratory Volunteer Research Positions
university: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center / Harvard Medical School
description: The Kirby Laboratory at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center explicitly advertises volunteer research positions for high-school and undergraduate students. The laboratory has previously mentored numerous Massachusetts high-school researchers. Interested students are instructed to contact James Kirby or Dr. Yanqin Huang directly with a CV and brief statement of research interests. The laboratory's official positions page describes volunteer opportunities as immediately available, although applicants should confirm that openings remain.

name: CHROME Lab — High School Engineering Research
title: Human-Centered Engineering and Technology Research Internship
description: Saint Louis University's CHROME Lab accepts applications from high-school students in the St. Louis area for summer research experiences involving engineering, computer science and human-centered technology. Participants work alongside university researchers on ongoing projects, typically committing at least ten hours per week. Applicants must have parental permission and transportation to campus. The laboratory generally hosts approximately two or three high-school students each summer. Its published application timeline anticipates opening applications near the end of October, accepting submissions through March, conducting interviews in April and making decisions by mid-May.

name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Science Enrichment Program
title: Cancer Biology and Biomedical Research Enrichment Internship
description: Memorial Sloan Kettering's Science Enrichment Program is a ten-month research enrichment pathway for students attending designated New York City partner high schools. Participants receive instruction in cancer biology, laboratory skills and clinical research, followed by an intensive eight-week summer research internship with individual mentorship. Students must be nominated through a participating school; applications are not open to all NYC high-school students. The official partner-school list includes Brooklyn Latin School, the High School for Health Professions and Human Services, Lincoln High School and Uncommon Collegiate Charter High School. This program is separate from MSK's general Summer Student Program.

name: Gautam Dantas — Dantas Laboratory
title: Microbiology, Genomics and Biomedical Summer Research
description: The Dantas Laboratory at Washington University in St. Louis explicitly welcomes inquiries from high-school and undergraduate students interested in summer research internships. The laboratory investigates microbial communities, antibiotic resistance and related biomedical questions using experimental and computational approaches. Prospective researchers are strongly encouraged to seek independent funding or fellowship support and to contact the laboratory well ahead of summer fellowship deadlines. St. Louis-area high-school students may also investigate Washington University's Young Scientist Program. Current placements depend on laboratory availability and funding.

name: Samir Kendale — CERBERUS Clinical Research Project
title: Neuroanesthesia and Clinical Neuroscience Research
university: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center / Harvard Medical School
description: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center's Office of Student Engagement and Experience lists the CERBERUS clinical research project under Dr. Samir Kendale as an unpaid, in-person opportunity explicitly available to high-school students and students at higher educational levels. The study examines cerebral autoregulation during major non-cardiac surgery and its relationship to postoperative cognitive outcomes. Opportunities include clinical research, neurocognitive assessment, and potentially machine-learning analysis with experienced mentors. The posting describes flexible full-time or part-time arrangements. Applicants should email Dr. Kendale with their resume and statement of interest and copy the Office of Student Engagement and Experience.

name: Children's National — Colaco Scholar Program
title: Pediatric Laboratory Medicine and Clinical Research Internship
description: The Colaco Scholar Program at Children's National Hospital provides approximately eight weeks of laboratory medicine and clinical research exposure for one or two area high-school students. Participants work in the hospital's clinical laboratory, learn about medical laboratory testing, observe relevant medical specialties and contribute to research projects. Recruitment is highly restricted by donor requirements, with most participants coming from selected private high schools in Washington, D.C., or Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology in Virginia. The institution does not advertise an unrestricted national application route.

name: Boston Children's Hospital Anesthesiology Research Opportunities
title: Pediatric Biomedical and Translational Research Inquiry
university: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
department: Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine Research
description: Boston Children's Hospital's Anesthesiology, Critical Care and Pain Medicine research division explicitly states that high-school students aged sixteen or older may seek research opportunities, including students from outside the hospital. Interested students are instructed to contact the investigator whose research interests them. The department documents previous high-school participation in biomedical laboratory projects involving nanoparticle technologies, cell culture and experimental methods. The opportunities depend on the investigator's ability to supervise students and are distinct from guaranteed placement in the department's structured clinical research internship.

name: Scripps Research Translational Institute — Student Research Internship
title: Genomics and Digital Health Translational Research Internship
description: The Scripps Research Translational Institute offers a student research internship for highly motivated students interested in genomics, mobile health and translational biomedical research. High-school students must be at least sixteen years old before the internship begins. The unpaid internship requires school credit or a transcript notation, with an affiliated community college pathway potentially available to help arrange credit. The 2027 application is scheduled to open November 23, 2026, with a March 30, 2027 deadline. Interns are selected according to project fit and mentor availability. This is distinct from Scripps Research's REACH internship.

name: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee — ACS Project SEED
title: Paid Chemistry and Biochemistry Summer Research Internship
description: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee hosts an American Chemical Society Project SEED site providing paid, mentored summer chemistry research for eligible high-school students. Participants work alongside university faculty and graduate researchers on authentic scientific projects. The 2027 research areas include computational chemistry, drug discovery and biochemistry, environmental and water chemistry, and molecular biophysics. The university lists applications from February 8 through April 1, 2027, with the summer program running June 15 through August 6. Applicants must meet ACS Project SEED eligibility requirements, including its applicable financial eligibility criteria.

name: Melanie Morrison — UCSF Neuromodulation Imaging Lab
title: Neuroimaging and Brain Stimulation Research Pathway
description: The Neuromodulation Imaging Lab at UCSF, led by Dr. Melanie Morrison, explicitly welcomes high-school students through designated paid summer research programs. Research involves neuroimaging, brain stimulation and investigation of deep brain stimulation mechanisms and outcomes. The laboratory directs interested students toward structured programs including RISE, SEP, CURE and BAYS rather than guaranteeing independent laboratory placement. Students applying through an eligible program are encouraged to notify the lab of their interest. Program-specific eligibility restrictions and placement availability apply, and acceptance into a program does not guarantee assignment to this laboratory.

name: Veenema Lab — High School Behavioral Neuroscience Internship
title: Behavioral Neuroscience Summer Volunteer Research
description: The Veenema Lab explicitly welcomes talented high-school students interested in volunteering as summer research interns. Students may gain experience with behavioral neuroscience experiments and laboratory techniques. Applicants must be at least sixteen years old. The laboratory's outreach page still mentions commuting to Boston College, although its current website identifies Michigan State University, so prospective applicants must confirm the present internship location and availability before making arrangements.

name: Candace Fleischer — Fleischer Lab High School Research Pathway
title: Biomedical Engineering and Medical Imaging Research
description: The Fleischer Lab conducts biomedical imaging and neuroscience-related research and explicitly considers high-school students through established research-training programs. Its official recruitment page states that high-school students must already be enrolled in a formal program, such as Project ENGAGES, Winship Summer Scholars, or a qualifying school-credit internship. The laboratory does not advertise unrestricted high-school volunteer positions. Students should apply to an appropriate program and verify whether a placement in this particular laboratory is possible.

name: University of Hawaii Cancer Center — High School Research Mentorship
title: Cancer Research and Population Science Project Mentorship
description: The University of Hawaii Cancer Center permits high-school students with school research projects to inquire about faculty mentorship. Applicants are instructed to submit a resume and short proposal outlining the research question, objectives, and any preliminary work. Due to institutional policies involving minors, students younger than eighteen cannot be placed in laboratory settings. Possible alternatives include faculty guidance on research papers and population-science projects. Mentorship depends on faculty availability and is not guaranteed.

name: Graham Macleod — Macleod Neurophysiology Laboratory
title: Neurophysiology, Cell Biology and Biophysics Research Internship
description: The Macleod Lab at Tulane University explicitly advertises opportunities for high-school interns, undergraduate interns, research assistants, graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers. Its research concerns neurophysiology at the intersection of cellular biology, biophysics, and genetics. Students interested in experimental neuroscience can contact Dr. Graham Macleod directly about potential research involvement. The laboratory's recruitment page lists high-school interns among its open position categories, although specific project assignments and remaining vacancies should be confirmed.

name: CRoME Pharmacy Summer Research Scholars
title: Virtual Pharmacy and Health Research Summer Program
description: The University of Kentucky's Collaborative Research on Medication Use and Family Health Laboratory operates the CRoME Pharmacy Summer Research Scholars program, a six-week virtual research experience for high-school students. Participants learn how pharmacy research is designed, conducted, analyzed, and communicated while collaborating with peers and mentors on an independent research project. Graduates may be eligible for additional research activities, including internships, publications, and community outreach. The official page describes the program but does not confirm the next application deadline.

name: Anisha Gupta — Cancer Therapeutics Research Laboratory
title: Cancer Biology and Nucleic Acid Therapeutics Research
description: Professor Anisha Gupta's research laboratory at the University of Saint Joseph explicitly welcomes qualified high-school students, undergraduate students, and Pharm.D. students interested in cancer therapeutics, medicinal chemistry, and nucleic acid therapies. Research activities may include cell culture, molecular biology, experimental design, data analysis, scientific writing, and research presentations. Students are generally expected to contribute approximately four to eight hours weekly, attend laboratory meetings, and maintain organized research records. Previous research experience is not required. Interested students should contact Professor Gupta to discuss eligibility and available projects.

name: Huiqing Zhou — Zhou Laboratory High School Research
title: Molecular Biology and RNA Biochemistry Research Prospect
description: The Zhou Laboratory at Boston College conducts research involving RNA biology, biochemistry, and molecular chemical techniques. The laboratory's official news page documents high-school research assistants returning for summer research in June 2026, demonstrating that students at this educational level have participated in its projects. This is evidence of previous high-school mentorship rather than a currently advertised open position. Interested students may investigate the group's research and inquire about future opportunities, subject to laboratory capacity and supervision.

name: Georgia Tech College of Sciences Summer Research Academy
title: High School STEM Summer Laboratory Research
description: Georgia Tech's College of Sciences Summer Research Academy provides local high-school students with supervised volunteer summer research experiences at no cost. Applicants must be at least sixteen years old when the program begins. The program particularly encourages applications from Atlanta Public Schools students and students who have historically had limited access to STEM opportunities, although other eligible local students may apply. Participants gain laboratory research experience with mentorship from university researchers. Current program dates, placements, and application requirements should be checked before applying.

name: Pelham–Einstein Neuroscience Scholars Program
title: High School Neuroscience Summer Research Mentorship
description: The Pelham–Einstein Neuroscience Scholars Program is a summer research opportunity organized through neuroscientists and the Neuroscience Graduate Student Organization at Albert Einstein College of Medicine. High-school participants work on an original research project under the mentorship of graduate and postdoctoral researchers and attend enrichment activities focused on scientific literature and developing research questions. The institution identifies the program as a high-school research pathway, but current recruitment dates and geographic eligibility should be confirmed with the organizers.

name: Penn State College of Medicine High School Research Internships
title: Biomedical Research Internship and Laboratory Shadowing
university: Pennsylvania State University College of Medicine
description: Penn State College of Medicine maintains an institutional process allowing high-school students aged sixteen or older to seek research shadowing or extended research internships in faculty laboratories. Experiences may range from one or two days of observation to several weeks or months of supervised research. Students must first identify a prospective faculty supervisor using the institution's research directory before proceeding with the required application and safety procedures. A research placement is not automatically provided; approval depends on securing a willing mentor and satisfying institutional requirements for minors.

name: UCLA–LA Youth Research Initiative
title: University Laboratory Research Internship
