description: The UCLA–LA Youth Research Initiative provides local Los Angeles high-school students opportunities to participate in research at UCLA laboratories affiliated with the California NanoSystems Institute. Students selected through participating high-school teachers join a UCLA research laboratory for approximately five to six weeks during the summer. Each participant works closely with a graduate student mentor who develops a research schedule, provides training, and supervises laboratory activities. The application process normally involves teacher nominations in February, student applications during March or April, and interviews during May. Students must be nominated through participating local schools rather than applying independently.

name: Hamid Rabb — Rabb Kidney Research Laboratory
title: Kidney Disease, Immunology and Molecular Biology Research
university: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
description: The Rabb Kidney Research Laboratory at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine studies immunological and molecular mechanisms involved in acute kidney injury and kidney repair. Research includes T cell immunology, inflammatory responses, molecular biology, cell biology, and experimental approaches to understanding kidney damage. The laboratory explicitly invites high-school and undergraduate students interested in gaining research experience or exposure to a wet-lab environment to contact the group describing their interests and future plans. This is a documented high-school inquiry pathway, although current positions and mentorship capacity must be confirmed before participation.

name: Weissman Hood Institute High School Summer Research Internship
title: Biomedical Laboratory Summer Research Internship
description: The Weissman Hood Institute offers summer internships for eligible high-school and college students interested in biomedical research. Participants spend approximately eight weeks working in the laboratory of an institute scientist or in the Animal Resource Center, contributing to an active research project under the supervision of experienced researchers. Interns participate in journal clubs, scientific seminars, and laboratory activities before presenting their work at the end of the program. Applicants must have completed their junior or senior year of high school or be enrolled in college. The official page describes the June 15 through August 7, 2026 program; dates and application availability for 2027 have not yet been confirmed.

name: Harvard Chemistry High School Lab Pathways Research Program
title: Chemistry and Biological Laboratory Summer Research
department: Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology
description: Harvard University's Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology operates the High School Lab Pathways Summer Research Program in partnership with the Harvard Ed Portal. The documented program serves students from Brighton High School who are nominated by their teachers. Participants receive science-literacy and laboratory-skills instruction during the spring before undertaking approximately six weeks of mentored summer laboratory research. Students work with graduate student mentors, conduct experiments, read scientific literature, attend laboratory meetings, and gain exposure to research instrumentation. This is a restricted partner-school pathway rather than an open national application. Current cohort arrangements should be confirmed through Harvard.

name: Baruch College Now STEM Research Academy
title: Faculty-Mentored Summer Research and Research Methods Program
university: Baruch College, City University of New York
description: Baruch College's STEM Research Academy provides New York City public high-school students with a structured introduction to university research followed by potential faculty-mentored summer research. Approximately twenty-five students are selected for a spring college-credit research methods course covering research-question development, experimental design, literature searches, and scientific reading. Students who successfully complete the spring course with at least a C become eligible for a six-week summer research experience with CUNY faculty. Previous research disciplines have included biology, environmental science, sociology, and psychology. Selection considers academic records, Regents performance, and written application materials. The official page includes information from earlier cohorts; current application dates should be verified.

name: UC Davis EnvironMentors Research Program
title: Environmental Science and Ecology Research Mentorship
department: Environmental Science and Related Research Departments
description: UC Davis EnvironMentors connects Sacramento-area high-school students with university researchers for yearlong scientific research mentorship. Students work with undergraduate, graduate, postdoctoral, or faculty mentors to develop a research question, collect and analyze data, and communicate their findings. Research can involve ecology, environmental science, wildlife conservation, agriculture, environmental toxicology, or related scientific fields. The program generally runs from September through June and provides participants with opportunities to present their research at the UC Davis Science Fair, with selected projects advancing to an international science fair. Participation is free, prior research experience is not required, and students must meet the program's geographic and enrollment requirements.

name: Farmingdale State College SURI High School Scholars
title: Faculty-Mentored Summer Research Institute
department: Office of Undergraduate Research and Scholarship
description: Farmingdale State College's Summer Undergraduate Research Institute includes a High School Scholars pathway for eligible high-school juniors and seniors. Students join faculty-mentored research clusters that may involve laboratory experiments, data analysis, engineering prototypes, applied scientific investigations, or other scholarly projects. Research groups typically contain college students and a small number of high-school scholars, allowing collaborative research and mentorship. The college's 2027 program information states that high-school scholars are scheduled to join on July 5, 2027. Student application instructions and final project availability should be confirmed on the official program website.

name: Anne Arundel Community College High-RISE Research Experience
title: Paid High School Summer Scientific Research
department: School of Science, Technology and Education
description: Anne Arundel Community College offers High-RISE, a summer research program designed specifically for current and graduating high-school students. Participants work with college science faculty on research activities, develop experimental and analytical skills, and communicate their research findings. The program includes faculty mentorship and paid participation, with opportunities to present research results. For 2027, the college lists High-RISE from June 14 through June 25, with full-day activities Monday through Friday. Student applications are expected to open in early spring 2027. Specific eligibility requirements and project assignments should be checked when applications become available.

name: University of Rochester Laboratory for Laser Energetics Summer Research
title: Laser Physics, Plasma Science and Engineering Summer Research
description: The University of Rochester's Laboratory for Laser Energetics offers an eight-week summer research program for highly motivated high-school juniors from the Rochester, New York area. Selected students work on authentic research projects under the supervision of laboratory scientists or engineers. Projects are connected to the laboratory's research involving the OMEGA and OMEGA EP laser systems and may involve plasma physics, high-energy-density science, scientific instrumentation, modeling, and engineering. Participants receive a monetary stipend and present their research findings at a concluding laboratory symposium. The program is geographically restricted to eligible Rochester-area students, and applicants should verify the current application cycle.

name: Mount Sinai Krammer Lab — New York City Virus Hunters
title: Virology and Community-Based Infectious Disease Research
university: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai / BioBus
description: The Krammer Laboratory at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai collaborates with BioBus on New York City Virus Hunters, a community science initiative involving infectious disease research and student participation. The laboratory explicitly invites middle- and high-school classes to inquire about participating in research data collection and hands-on scientific activities. Individual students are also directed to contact BioBus for information about possible internships in future years. Interested students should contact the community science director to learn whether an internship or school-based research opportunity is available. This is a documented research engagement pathway rather than a confirmed currently open internship position.

name: James Gaynor — Ultrafast Spectroscopy Research Group
title: Physical Chemistry and Ultrafast Spectroscopy Research
description: The Gaynor Research Group at Northwestern University studies molecular processes using ultrafast spectroscopy and advanced experimental instrumentation. Research interests include multidimensional spectroscopy, femtosecond laser techniques, high-harmonic generation, and X-ray science. The laboratory's recruitment page explicitly invites interested high-school and undergraduate students to email Dr. James Gaynor describing their research interests and attaching a CV. Prior research experience is not required, although enthusiasm for designing, building, and operating spectroscopic instruments is emphasized. This is a direct laboratory inquiry pathway; actual availability depends on supervision and current projects.

name: Paul Chwatko — Chwatko Research Group
title: Chemical Engineering and Advanced Materials Research
description: The Chwatko Research Group at the University of Kentucky provides opportunities for students interested in chemical and materials engineering research. Its official recruitment page specifically welcomes high-school students from the Lexington, Kentucky area to email the principal investigator about potential research participation. Undergraduate students may also inquire directly about current opportunities. There is no centrally advertised high-school application cycle or guarantee of immediate placement. High-school applicants should contact the research group to discuss available projects, appropriate preparation, scheduling, and laboratory supervision.

name: Hinsby Cadillo-Quiroz — Cadillo Laboratory
title: Environmental Microbiology and Ecosystem Research
description: The Cadillo Laboratory at Arizona State University investigates environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, biogeochemistry, and microorganisms involved in ecosystem processes. Its official Join Us page includes specific instructions for undergraduate and high-school candidates. Interested students are instructed to email an introduction explaining their academic background, year in school, research interests, and reasons for wanting to participate, accompanied by a resume describing relevant coursework or research experience. Students must complete applicable laboratory safety training before beginning experimental work. High-school participation is explicitly contemplated, but specific placements depend on current projects and mentoring capacity.

name: Behnam Ghalei — RAMP Laboratory
title: Advanced Membranes and Chemical Engineering Research
department: Otto H. York Department of Chemical and Materials Engineering
description: The RAMP Laboratory at New Jersey Institute of Technology develops advanced materials and membrane technologies for chemical separations and related environmental applications. Its research includes polymer membranes, stimuli-responsive membranes, mineral recovery, and chemical engineering materials. The laboratory's official recruitment page explicitly states that it hosts high-school and community-college students as summer research interns. Students can gain exposure to membrane fabrication, material characterization, separation experiments, laboratory safety, and data analysis. The group identifies Dr. Behnam Ghalei as its contact. High-school applicants should inquire about summer eligibility and availability because the published application instructions are primarily directed toward graduate and undergraduate applicants.

name: Tao Gao — Sustainable Processing and Energy Resilience Laboratory
title: Battery Science and Electrochemical Engineering Research
department: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
description: Professor Tao Gao leads the Sustainable Processing and Energy Resilience Laboratory at North Carolina State University, studying battery systems, electrochemical separations, critical-material recovery, and sustainable industrial processes. The laboratory's recruitment page explicitly welcomes motivated high-school students, generally through summer research programs. Prospective students are instructed to contact Professor Gao through LinkedIn with information about their preferred timing and research interests. The laboratory does not advertise guaranteed direct high-school placements, and applicants should confirm whether a relevant program or individual research arrangement is available.

name: Upstate Freshwater Institute — High School Research Inquiry
title: Freshwater Ecology and Environmental Research Experience
description: The Upstate Freshwater Institute is an independent nonprofit environmental research organization that studies freshwater ecosystems, aquatic chemistry, and water quality. Its official student opportunities page explicitly encourages high-school students to contact institute staff about potential job-shadowing or research experiences. The organization operates an accredited environmental laboratory and conducts scientific work related to water resources. Its paid summer internship descriptions primarily concern college students and recent graduates, so high-school students should not assume eligibility for those positions. High-school research participation is inquiry-based and depends on available staff, supervision, and projects.

name: Leilani Gilpin — AIEA Laboratory
title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Research Internship
description: The AIEA Laboratory at the University of California, Santa Cruz conducts research on interpretable and explainable artificial intelligence, AI safety, neurosymbolic methods, and autonomous systems. Its official recruitment page explains that high-school students commonly join through UCSC's Science Internship Program or COSMOS. However, the laboratory also states that students outside these programs may be considered for structured summer volunteer opportunities involving independent projects or contributions to existing research. Interested students can join the prospective-intern mailing list or community channels to learn about availability. Independent volunteer placements are conditional rather than guaranteed, making this a useful but competitive research pathway.

name: Kavita Hegde — Ophthalmic Research Laboratory
title: Vision Science and Ophthalmic Research Internship
description: Coppin State University's Ophthalmic Research Laboratory offers a formal research internship pathway for high-school sophomores, juniors, seniors, high-school graduates, and college students. The laboratory is led by Dr. Kavita Hegde and provides opportunities to gain experience in ophthalmic and biomedical research. Its official website lists separate high-school and undergraduate application forms, making the application process more concrete than an informal faculty inquiry. The published schedule describes summer internships from June 15 through July 31 and academic-year internships from September 1 through May 15. Applications are requested by April 30 for summer participation and July 31 for academic-year participation. Applicants should confirm the applicable year and current capacity.

name: McCoy Lab — R.E.E.F. High School Research Mentorship
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Research Enrichment
description: The McCoy Laboratory at the University of Chicago offers R.E.E.F., or Readings in Ecological and Evolutionary Foundations, a research enrichment program designed for local Chicago-area high-school students. The program introduces participants to ecological and evolutionary research through weekly readings, guided discussion with graduate-student mentors, and participation in laboratory meetings. The documented 2026 session operated for approximately eight weeks, from June 8 through August 7, and concluded with student presentations. This is a scientific research-literacy and mentorship program rather than a conventional independent wet-laboratory research internship. Current application availability and the next program cycle require confirmation.

name: TGen Academic-Year Biomedical Research Internships
title: Translational Genomics and Biomedical Research Internship
description: The Translational Genomics Research Institute provides unpaid academic-year internships involving laboratory research, computational biology, bioinformatics, statistics, and other areas of translational bioscience. Internships are supervised by institute personnel and typically require ten to twenty hours weekly over at least one academic semester. The institution states that high-school participation is possible but extremely rare because students often cannot meet the weekday laboratory schedule. Applicants generally must be at least sixteen years old, satisfy applicable enrollment and immigration-status requirements, and contact the Education and Outreach office about potential placements. This is a limited inquiry-based pathway, not a guaranteed high-school research position.

name: Wen Song — Micro/Nanofluidics Research Laboratory
title: Microfluidics, Geochemistry and Energy Materials Recovery Research
description: Professor Wen Song's research group at the University of Texas at Austin investigates microscale fluid-solid interactions, microfluidics, geochemistry, and technologies for recovering materials and resources from subsurface environments. Research connects fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, reservoir engineering, and experimental approaches to sustainable resource recovery. The laboratory's official recruitment page explicitly welcomes high-school students who are curious about its research and encourages them to email a brief introduction explaining their interests and goals. Undergraduate students are also invited to inquire. This is a genuine direct-contact opportunity rather than a pathway restricted to an established summer program, although specific projects and mentorship availability must be confirmed with the laboratory.

name: Nicholas Hutzler — Hutzler Atomic Physics Laboratory
title: Atomic and Molecular Physics Summer Research
department: Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy
description: The Hutzler Laboratory at Caltech conducts experimental atomic and molecular physics research involving precision measurements, laser-based techniques, and fundamental physical phenomena. Its official community page documents a recurring partnership with Caltech's Summer Research Connection, administered through the Center for Teaching, Learning, and Outreach. Each summer, teams of high-school students and K-12 teachers have participated in research activities with the laboratory. The page documents past high-school research teams across multiple years and directs interested students to contact the Caltech outreach program, specifically Mitch Aiken, about participation. Students should apply or inquire through the relevant outreach program rather than assuming unrestricted admission directly into the laboratory. Availability for the next summer remains subject to confirmation.

name: Mechanics of Advanced Materials Laboratory — High School Explorers
title: Advanced Materials and Mechanical Engineering Research
description: The Mechanics of Advanced Materials Laboratory at the University of Texas at Dallas describes a High School Explorers research pathway for students in their junior or senior year. Interested high-school students may apply to volunteer in the laboratory after school or during summer vacation, contributing to investigations involving the mechanical behavior of advanced materials and new material compositions. The laboratory's outreach page explicitly describes student participation in research rather than general classroom enrichment. Students should contact the laboratory to confirm its current application procedure, project availability, age requirements, and supervision arrangements. The official page was indexed but could not be fully reopened during verification.

name: Wei Lin — Lin Research Group
title: Physics and Materials Research Through the UTRGV High Scholar Program
university: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
description: Professor Wei Lin's research group at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley explicitly welcomes high-school students to participate in summer research through the university's High Scholar program. The laboratory maintains active university research and offers opportunities for students to gain experience with scientific methods and faculty-supervised projects. Its official research-group page, updated in fall 2026, specifically identifies the High Scholar program as the route for high-school participation. Undergraduate students may separately contact the laboratory about research credit, volunteering, and supported research. High-school applicants should verify the current High Scholar application cycle, eligibility requirements, available projects, and whether placement with the Lin group is possible.

name: Yun Song — Song Laboratory at CHOP and Penn
title: Neural Development, Genetics and Brain Disease Research
university: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia / University of Pennsylvania
department: Center for Cellular and Molecular Therapeutics
description: The Song Laboratory at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and University of Pennsylvania investigates the cellular and molecular mechanisms governing neural circuit development, maintenance, and function. Its work includes neural development, neurogenetics, injury, neurodegeneration, and disease-related research using experimental model systems. The laboratory's official news page documents two students from Pennsylvania-area high schools beginning research internships in May and June 2026, providing recent evidence of direct high-school research involvement. The laboratory also states that it welcomes motivated prospective researchers and provides a contact email for Dr. Song. However, the recruitment instructions are not specifically written for high-school applicants, and the documented internships do not guarantee current openings. Students interested in neuroscience or molecular biology may inquire about possible summer opportunities while clearly identifying their educational level and research interests.

name: Morehouse Materials/Optics Research and Engineering Laboratory
title: Quantum Science, Optics and Photonics Summer Research Enrichment
description: Morehouse College's Materials/Optics Research and Engineering Laboratory, directed by Dr. Wesley Sims, describes a MORE-QuEST summer program for rising ninth- through twelfth-grade students interested in quantum science, optics, photonics, advanced materials, and computing technologies. The program is intended to introduce participants to foundational scientific ideas while developing research-related reasoning, problem-solving, and communication skills. Students must attend the full program duration. The laboratory's institutional page identifies a forthcoming application rather than confirming an active application cycle. Its separately advertised laboratory research-assistant positions are directed toward undergraduates, so high-school users should regard MORE-QuEST as a research-enrichment pathway rather than a guaranteed placement in an active research laboratory.

name: Wipawee Winuthayanon — Winuthayanon Laboratory
title: Reproductive Biology and Molecular Biomedical Research
department: Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Women's Health
description: The Winuthayanon Laboratory at the University of Missouri conducts biomedical research related to reproductive biology, reproductive physiology, and the molecular mechanisms regulating reproductive health. Its official laboratory membership page documents current high-school researchers from Rock Bridge High School in Columbia, Missouri. One joined during summer 2024 and continued into the 2025 academic year, while another joined during summer 2026. These records demonstrate recent and sustained high-school participation rather than merely one historical outreach event. However, the personnel page does not provide a formal open application or guarantee additional positions. Students interested in experimental reproductive biology may contact the laboratory about prospective research opportunities, with local access and mentorship capacity likely important considerations.

name: Xi Ling — Nanomaterials, Structures and Spectroscopy Group
title: Nanomaterials and Advanced Spectroscopy Research
description: Professor Xi Ling's research group at Boston University studies advanced materials and their physical and chemical behavior through spectroscopy, nanoscale characterization, and experimental materials research. The group's official news archive documents repeated participation by high-school researchers through Boston University's GROW and RISE summer programs, including students in 2024 and 2025. In 2025, the laboratory specifically reported that four high-school participants completed six-week summer research experiences under graduate-student mentorship. This provides evidence of recurring laboratory participation rather than a single isolated internship. High-school students should pursue the appropriate Boston University summer research application and understand that admission to a program does not guarantee assignment to the Ling Group. Independent direct high-school recruitment has not been confirmed.

name: University of Delaware Center for Composite Materials — Student Research Internships
title: Composite Materials and Manufacturing Engineering Research
description: The University of Delaware Center for Composite Materials offers research internships involving composite materials, advanced manufacturing, laboratory investigation, and engineering research. Its official internship page explicitly provides an application route for students who are not enrolled at the University of Delaware, including high-school students. Interested non-UD applicants are directed to email their resume to the center, including a short summary of their research experience, technical skills, and relevant coursework. Internships may involve mentorship from experienced researchers and university faculty, with opportunities to develop engineering skills and communicate research findings. The program describes flexible participation during academic semesters and summer or winter breaks. Specific high-school eligibility, available projects, compensation, and supervision requirements should be confirmed. The institutional page was indexed but could not be fully reopened during verification.

name: NYU Music and Audio Research Laboratory — High School Research Pathways
title: Music Technology, Audio Computing and Interdisciplinary Research
department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
description: The Music and Audio Research Laboratory at NYU Steinhardt conducts interdisciplinary research involving music, audio technology, computing, and related scientific and creative questions. Its official Join Us page explicitly welcomes middle- and high-school students to participate in initiatives through NYU programs including ARISE, SONYC K-12, and Music Technology Summer Intensives. These programs offer different forms of research exposure, training, and technical enrichment; not all constitute individual mentored laboratory research projects. Interested high-school students should review the requirements and application processes of the relevant program rather than assume the laboratory accepts unrestricted direct applications. Specific placement with MARL, research responsibilities, and next-cycle availability must be verified through the program.

name: Kaveh Yousefi — Flow Dynamics and Turbulence Laboratory
title: Fluid Mechanics, Computational Modeling and Machine Learning Summer Research
description: The Flow Dynamics and Turbulence Laboratory at the University of Texas at Dallas explicitly welcomes high-school students through its Summer STEM Scholars Program and STEM Bridge Program. Research involves fluid dynamics, wave modeling, computational methods, and machine learning. The laboratory states that it typically accepts one to three students through its own summer scholars pathway and four to five through STEM Bridge. Students work with university researchers and gain exposure to computational and experimental engineering. Interested high-school students may contact Professor Kaveh Yousefi directly at kyousefi@utdallas.edu regarding the Summer STEM Scholars Program. Admission is limited by available projects and supervision, and the next application dates should be confirmed.

name: UC Merced YuCCA Laboratory — High School Research
title: Edge Artificial Intelligence and Embedded Systems Research
description: Yu's Cognitive Computing and Automation Laboratory at UC Merced develops intelligent computing technologies with particular emphasis on edge artificial intelligence and embedded systems. Its official recruitment page explicitly addresses high-school students alongside undergraduate and master's students and invites motivated young researchers to inquire about participating. Research opportunities may provide faculty and graduate-student mentorship, technical skill development, and participation in active projects. The laboratory emphasizes that capacity is limited and that it cannot accommodate every applicant. Students should review the published requirements and use the laboratory's stated email-subject format when contacting the group. Current individual high-school openings and project assignments must be confirmed.

name: University of Maryland PRIME-R Robotics Research Program
title: Semester-Long Faculty-Mentored Robotics Research
description: The University of Maryland's Pre-College Research Internships and Mentored Experience in Robotics program, PRIME-R, places motivated high-school students into robotics laboratories affiliated with the Maryland Robotics Center. Students work alongside faculty members and graduate-student mentors on meaningful research projects over a semester, with an expected commitment of approximately five hours weekly. The program is open to current tenth-, eleventh-, and twelfth-grade students who are United States citizens. Applications require a transcript, resume, and recommendation letter, and prior robotics experience is not mandatory. The official application deadline is November 15, 2026. PRIME-R is an in-person commuter program without transportation or meals, and it does not provide academic credit.

name: Axel Krieger Research Group — AMIRo Laboratory
title: Medical Robotics and Image-Guided Intervention Summer Research
department: Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics
description: The Automation and Interventional Medicine Robotics Laboratory at Johns Hopkins University investigates medical robotics and technologies for robotic and image-guided interventions. Its official opportunities page states that the laboratory occasionally offers summer research positions for undergraduate students and advanced high-school students. Interested students are instructed to contact Professor Iulian Iordachita directly about possible summer research involvement. The laboratory does not promise a continuously available high-school opening, and participation depends on project needs, technical preparation, and available mentorship. Students should inquire about current opportunities rather than interpreting the page as a confirmed vacancy.

name: Gregory Fischer — Automation and Interventional Medicine Robotics Laboratory
title: Medical Robotics and Biomedical Engineering Summer Research
description: The Automation and Interventional Medicine Robotics Laboratory at Worcester Polytechnic Institute develops robotic technologies for medical applications and image-guided procedures. Its official positions page explicitly states that the group occasionally offers summer research positions to undergraduate students and advanced high-school students. Interested students are directed to contact Professor Gregory Fischer about potential research involvement. The laboratory's high-school positions are intermittent rather than guaranteed. Students should confirm whether a suitable summer project, available mentor, and institutional arrangements for minors exist before making plans. This is a separate institution and research group from the Johns Hopkins AMIRo laboratory.

name: Rutgers Institute for Translational Medicine and Sciences Summer Research Program
title: Translational Biomedical Research Summer Internship
department: Institute for Translational Medicine and Sciences
description: The Rutgers Institute for Translational Medicine and Sciences Summer Research Program provides high-school students, college students, and first-year medical students opportunities to contribute to translational biomedical research. Participants become part of research teams, participate in experimental planning and analysis, perform laboratory investigations where appropriate, and present scientific results. Applicants must be at least sixteen years old when the program begins. The official program page lists February 1 as the general application deadline, with January 1 specified for foreign nationals, and requires supporting application materials and recommendations. Students should verify the applicable summer cycle, project availability, and additional eligibility requirements before applying.

name: Shelly Peyton — Engineering the Cell Summer Research Program
title: Cancer Bioengineering, Biomaterials and Cellular Research
description: The Peyton Laboratory at Tufts University operates Engineering the Cell, a summer research program developed specifically for high-school students interested in science and engineering. Participants spend approximately six weeks in the laboratory working with Dr. Shelly Peyton and graduate researchers on scientific questions connected to cancer, brain research, soft materials, and biomaterials. The program provides direct exposure to experimental research and scientific methods. Participation is free, and selected students receive a small stipend. The 2026 application cycle is closed, with information for the following summer expected in early 2027. Applicants should confirm application dates, eligibility, and available placements before applying.

name: SickKids Summer Research Program — SSuRe
title: Pediatric Biomedical Research Summer Experience
description: The SickKids Summer Research Program provides research and professional development experiences for students working under the supervision of scientists at the SickKids Research Institute in Toronto. Summer researchers can attend seminars, scientific training activities, career events, and a concluding research symposium. High-school eligibility is specifically limited to students in their final year who will enroll in a university or college undergraduate program during the following fall. Younger high-school students are directed toward the separate Student Advancement Research internship program. Applicants must secure a qualifying research position and meet the institute's hiring and eligibility requirements. The available official page describes the 2026 application cycle; current openings and next-cycle dates require confirmation. This listing is distinct from SickKids StAR.

name: University of Pittsburgh Allegheny Observers
title: High School Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Group
description: Allegheny Observers is a high-school astronomy group based at the University of Pittsburgh's Allegheny Observatory. A September 2026 university report describes approximately sixty participating students from more than thirteen schools, coordinated through the observatory's outreach activities. Students engage with astronomy and astrophysics, scientific outreach, telescope-related activities, and research-oriented experiences, including a group trip to Green Bank Observatory. The program has received recognition for its scientific outreach. It should not be confused with a guaranteed individual university laboratory internship or a paid research position. Prospective participants should contact the observatory about current membership, research activities, geographic eligibility, and recruitment procedures.

name: University of Alberta EdTeKLA Research Group — High School Research Pathway
title: Educational Technology, Artificial Intelligence and Software Research
description: The University of Alberta EdTeKLA Research Group has documented high-school students participating in summer research and software-development activities through the university's Computing Science High School Internship Program and the Faculty of Science WISEST Summer Research Program. Research interests include educational technology, intelligent tutoring systems, computer-assisted learning, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction. The laboratory's available evidence comes from an archived former-members page rather than a current high-school recruitment announcement. Students should verify whether the group is still accepting placements through either program and apply through the appropriate university pathway rather than assuming direct lab admission. This is a historical participation pathway pending current-cycle confirmation.

name: Laboratory for Laser Energetics (LLE)
title: Summer High School Research Program
description: Paid, eight-week summer research placement for Rochester-area high-school students currently in their junior year. Accepted students are matched with an LLE scientist or engineer and work on projects connected to the OMEGA or OMEGA EP laser systems. Past topics include laser/plasma physics, materials science, diagnostics, optics, experimental data analysis, physical/computational chemistry, and modeling; students present their results at an LLE symposium. The official page says Summer 2026 applications are closed, and LLE announced in September 2026 that planning for the 2027 season had begun, but 2027 application dates are not yet posted. Local eligibility and the full eight-week commitment are important restrictions.

name: St. Bonaventure University Faculty Research Mentors
title: High School Student Research Program
description: A two-week, non-residential summer research experience for students completing their sophomore or junior year before Summer 2027. Students select and rank research interests from faculty project areas that include biochemistry, bioinformatics, biopsychology, computational chemistry, developmental biology, digital humanities, mathematics/computer-aided design, mechanical/electrical engineering, mental health in media, human-computer interaction, and molecular genetics. Participants work with a faculty mentor and present a project poster. For 2027, dates and the application deadline are still TBA; applicants should prepare a transcript and one-page personal statement and submit materials as directed on the program page. The stated program fee is $1,000 after acceptance; need-based scholarship support may be available. It is not residential, and a student needing on-campus housing must be accompanied by an adult.

name: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine & Imaging (AIMI)
title: AIMI Summer Research Internship
department: Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine & Imaging
description: Mentored high-school research internship focused on AI at the intersection of medicine and imaging. Students work with real-world health data and explore research questions involving the development and responsible translation of AI into healthcare. Stanford lists Summer 2027 applications as opening November 10, 2026, with a February 1, 2027 deadline. The official page does not yet specify the full 2027 schedule, compensation, or housing details, so applicants should verify these in the application materials. The program is a research experience rather than a general AI camp.

name: Duke Department of Cell Biology
title: Cell Biology Academy (CeBA)
department: Department of Cell Biology, Duke University School of Medicine
description: Paid summer cell-biology research opportunity for local Research Triangle-area high-school students. Interns conduct an independent project under a graduate-student or postdoctoral mentor and build experience in hypothesis formulation, practical bench skills, data analysis, and communicating results; the program also includes career seminars and journal clubs. The current program page says Summer 2027 applications will be accepted in January 2027. Current sophomores, juniors, and seniors may apply; participants must be local because transportation and lodging are not provided, and the page says students need an SSN or ITIN to receive the stipend. The page describes a six-week schedule for the prior cycle; 2027 dates and stipend amount should be reconfirmed when the new application opens.

name: University of Nebraska Medical Center SHARP
title: Summer High School Advanced Research Program (SHARP)
department: Division of Student Success; Pharmacology and Experimental Neuroscience; Biochemistry; Anesthesiology
description: Ten-week, bench-side research program in UNMC laboratories associated with pharmacology and experimental neuroscience, biochemistry, and anesthesiology (including the HSTAR pathway). Students receive biomedical research-methods training, work with a lab team, examine data, and prepare and present a research poster. The Summer 2027 application opens November 1, 2026 and is due February 1, 2027. Applicants must be at least 16, be a current high-school sophomore or junior, and be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; graduating seniors and international students are not considered. A 3.0 GPA, prior science coursework, and two strong recommendation letters are among the additional factors listed by UNMC.

name: RockEDU Science Outreach
title: Jumpstart: Spring-to-Summer Research Program
description: A combined after-school and summer program for New York City high-school juniors and seniors who are at least 16 at program start. The spring portion (February 25–June 10, 2027) meets Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:30–7:00 p.m. and builds molecular-biology laboratory skills; students then join the Summer Science Research Program for mentored, hands-on lab research from June 21–August 5, 2027, up to 35 hours per week. Applications for Jumpstart 2027 are open and all materials, including a recommendation letter, are due by 5:00 p.m. Eastern on January 4, 2027. Applicants must attend an NYC high school and commit to the entire spring-and-summer schedule. The page does not specify compensation or housing support.

name: Georgia Cancer Center (GCC)
title: Summer Research Experience (GCC SRE)
description: Six-week, individually mentored cancer-research experience at the Georgia Cancer Center, with projects spanning cell and molecular biology, cancer immunology, clinical outcomes, bioinformatics, population health, computational biology, and related areas. The 2027 program runs June 2–July 14; applications opened October 15, 2026 and are due January 15, 2027. Students must be at least 16 by the start date for bench-laboratory projects; younger high-school students may apply to non-bench projects such as bioinformatics, population health, clinical outcomes, or computational biology. Priority is given to students from Richmond, Columbia, and Aiken Counties, but the page does not make those counties an absolute eligibility requirement. Housing and stipends are not provided.

name: Simpson Querrey Lung Institute for Translational Science (SQLIFTS)
title: Kimberly Querrey Summer Research Program
department: Feinberg School of Medicine; Simpson Querrey Lung Institute for Translational Science
description: Paid six- to eight-week summer research program pairing participants with Northwestern faculty for basic or clinical projects related to lung disease. Interns work full-time (40 hours per week) and present their work at the Kimberly Querrey Summer Research Symposium. High-school applicants must be current juniors at application time and at least 16 years old by May 31 of the program year. The program welcomes applicants nationally, but students must arrange their own housing and transportation to Northwestern’s Chicago campus. The program page says the Summer 2027 application is expected to open in early January 2027; deadline and full 2027 details have not yet been posted.

name: Feeley-Liu Lab (Brian Feeley, MD)
title: Summer Research Program for High School Students
department: Sports Medicine and Shoulder Service; Department of Orthopaedic Surgery
description: A lab-run summer research program explicitly open to high-school, college, and medical students interested in sports medicine and translational stem-cell research. The lab studies muscle atrophy following rotator-cuff tears, muscle-stem-cell differentiation and regeneration, and low-cost motion analysis to improve lower-extremity movement and reduce injury or reinjury. Described student training includes histologic sample preparation and analysis, gene-expression work such as RT-PCR, protein-expression methods, and assessment of stem-cell function; some participants also gain clinical-research exposure and may shadow in the UCSF Sports Medicine Clinic. The lab page says applicants for Summer 2027 should contact the lab; it does not publish a deadline, stipend, or detailed grade/residency criteria. The contact link is email-protected on the public page, so no email is entered here rather than guessing.

name: BIO5 Institute / Keep Engaging Youth in Science (KEYS)
title: KEYS Research Internship
description: Free, seven-week summer research internship for high-school students from across Arizona. The 2027 program is scheduled for June 7–July 23, and applications open November 2, 2026; a closing date is not yet posted on the program homepage. Interns first complete a one-week introduction to bioscience and data-science techniques and science literacy, then join University of Arizona researchers on real projects across multiple disciplines. Placements have included research labs in Tucson and Phoenix as well as a virtual cohort, with mentoring from faculty, graduate/postdoctoral researchers, university students, and near-peer mentors. Students present their work at a research showcase. Housing arrangements for the 2027 cycle are not yet specified on the current page.

name: University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering
title: After-School Matters STEM Lab Internship
description: A STEM-focused opportunity associated with the University of Chicago and After School Matters. Verify the current program format, eligibility, and whether placements involve direct research before listing it as a research internship.

name: American Museum of Natural History (AMNH)
title: Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
description: A year-long research program for eligible New York City students in grades 10–11. Participants begin with a summer institute and then work in small teams with AMNH scientists on original research projects during the school year. Research areas vary annually and can include astrophysics, anthropology, conservation, genetics, genomics, and other natural sciences. Students develop research, data analysis, teamwork, and science communication skills and present their findings at a year-end symposium. Participants may receive a $2,500 stipend upon completing program requirements and may earn one CUNY Lehman College credit at no cost. Eligibility is restricted to students who live and attend school in NYC and meet additional academic and program-participation requirements. Check the official page for current application dates and eligibility details.

name: LSU College of Engineering
title: High School Summer Research (HSSR) Internship
description: A summer research opportunity connecting high-school students with engineering research at LSU. Students should consult the official program information for current eligibility, participating research areas, dates, and application requirements.

name: Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center
title: SURE-CAN
description: A research-focused educational opportunity associated with Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center. Verify current high-school eligibility, research placement structure, and application availability through the center's official education pages before applying.

name: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital
title: High School Research Immersion Program
description: A high-school research immersion opportunity connected to St. Jude's biomedical research environment. Check official program information for current availability, age and grade requirements, program format, and application details.

name: George Mason University
title: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
description: A summer research internship placing eligible high-school students with university researchers across STEM disciplines. Projects vary by faculty mentor and may involve laboratory experiments, computational research, data analysis, or engineering. Review the official ASSIP page for current eligibility, project listings, fees or stipends, and application deadlines.

name: UCSF Center for Science Education and Outreach
title: CURE Research Internship Program
department: Center for Science Education and Outreach
description: A research experience associated with UCSF's science education and outreach programs. Students should verify current eligibility, project placement, schedule, and application requirements through the official UCSF program pages.

name: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
title: Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
university: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: A summer internship pathway for high-school students interested in scientific and technical work at NIST. Potential research areas include physics, chemistry, engineering, materials science, and computing, depending on available projects. Confirm current program status, eligibility, location requirements, and application procedures through NIST's official student opportunities pages.

name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL)
title: Next Generation STEM Internship (NGSI)
description: A STEM internship opportunity associated with Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Research areas and eligibility can vary by program cycle and available placements. Confirm that the current NGSI pathway accepts high-school students and review its official eligibility and application requirements before listing it as an active research placement.

name: Moffitt Cancer Center Integrated Mathematical Oncology
title: High School Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology (HIP IMO)
description: A high-school research opportunity focused on mathematical and computational approaches to cancer. The Integrated Mathematical Oncology group studies how mathematical models can help explain tumor growth, treatment response, and interactions within the tumor environment. Verify the current internship cycle, eligibility, schedule, and application route through Moffitt's official pages.

name: Zuckerman Institute at Columbia University
title: Brain Research Apprenticeships in New York at Columbia (BRAINYAC)
department: Mortimer B. Zuckerman Mind Brain Behavior Institute
description: An intensive summer research internship placing high-school students in Columbia neuroscience laboratories for hands-on research with scientists. Eligibility is highly restricted: applicants must live in New York City and participate in an eligible partner program, such as S-PREP, BioBus, Lang Youth Medical, Columbia Secondary School, or Double Discovery Center. The 2027 application deadline is October 28, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.; students should check with their partner program about submitting an application. This is not an open application for all NYC high-school students.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine
title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
description: An eight-week biomedical research program in which high-school students conduct a medically oriented research project with Stanford faculty, postdoctoral fellows, students, and research staff. For Summer 2027, applicants must be high-school juniors or seniors, at least 16 by the program start, living in and attending high school in the United States, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Stanford states that selection will heavily favor Bay Area students. Consult the official page for the current application schedule and project details.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
title: Simons Summer Research Program
description: A six-week summer research program in which selected high-school students join Stony Brook faculty research groups, contribute to ongoing projects, pursue a research question, and present a poster. The 2027 program is scheduled for June 28–August 6. Applicants must be current high-school juniors, U.S. citizens or permanent residents, and at least 16 by the program start. School nomination is required, with a limit of three nominees per school; the published application guidance lists January 29, 2027, as the nomination deadline and February 5, 2027, as the student application deadline. Highly competitive.

name: Salk Institute for Biological Studies
title: Heithoff-Brody High School Summer Scholars Program
description: An eight-week paid summer internship in which high-school scholars work with Salk scientists on mentored research projects and present their findings at a research symposium. The 2027 program runs June 14–August 6, with applications scheduled to open December 1, 2026, and close February 15, 2027. Applicants must be at least 16 by June 14, live in San Diego County, and have completed their most recent high-school semester at a San Diego County high school. A minimum 2.75 GPA and completion of a high-school biology course are required; students under 18 need a school work permit upon hire.

name: CaliBaja Center for Resilient Materials and Systems
title: ENLACE Summer Research Program
department: CaliBaja Center for Resilient Materials and Systems
description: A summer research program connecting students with UC San Diego research laboratories in engineering, computer and data sciences, physical sciences, biological sciences, and earth sciences. The official 2027 page confirms that current high-school 11th graders are eligible to apply and notes scholarship support for the upcoming program. Students should review the official 2027 announcement for the application process, financial support conditions, and any additional eligibility restrictions before applying.

name: Houston Methodist Academic Institute
title: Summer High School Research Internship
description: A paid, full-time, ten-week summer internship introducing selected high-school juniors and seniors to translational research. Interns work with research mentors on projects, learn relevant laboratory techniques, and present their work at a research symposium. For Summer 2027, the program is scheduled for June 1–August 6; applications are scheduled to open December 4, 2026, and close January 29, 2027. Applicants must be at least 16 by June 1, have a minimum 3.5 GPA, submit a transcript and resume, answer essay questions, and provide two recommendations. Participants must arrange their own housing and transportation.

name: MIT PRIMES-USA
title: Program for Research in Mathematics, Engineering, and Science for High School Students — PRIMES-USA
description: A free, year-long research program for high-school sophomores and juniors residing in the United States outside Greater Boston. Participants work on original problems in mathematics or bioinformatics with academic mentors, primarily through remote collaboration. The program requires advanced mathematical preparation, independent study, and a substantial time commitment; admission is highly selective. The 2027 application deadline is November 2, 2026, with recommendation letters accepted through November 6. This is a genuine research program, distinct from MIT's math-enrichment offerings.

name: Department of the Navy Laboratories
title: Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
description: A competitive eight-week summer apprenticeship placing high-school students in Department of the Navy laboratories to participate in real science and engineering research with professional mentors. The program serves high-school sophomores, juniors, and seniors, with placements across multiple U.S. laboratories. The 2027 application cycle opened September 15, 2026, and the published application window runs through November 30, 2026. Students select preferred laboratories and apply through the central program portal; placement depends on the participating laboratory and its selection process.

name: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
title: Summer Internship Program (SIP) — Graduating High School Seniors
department: Office of Intramural Training and Education
description: The NIH Summer Internship Program offers mentored research placements in NIH laboratories and research groups. The high-school pathway is narrow: applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents and be graduating high-school seniors who will graduate before the internship starts. Applicants generally must be 18 by September 30, 2027; a graduating senior who is 17 on June 1 may qualify if their permanent home is within 40 miles of an NIH campus and they turn 18 by September 30. Check the official eligibility and application instructions carefully before applying, as this is not open to all high-school students.

name: Center for Excellence in Education (CEE)
title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
university: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Stanford University
description: A free, intensive six-week summer research program combining STEM coursework with a five-week mentored research internship and final oral and written research reports. For 2027, CEE is expanding RSI to both MIT and Stanford. Applicants typically apply during 11th grade and must have one year of high school remaining; seniors are not eligible, and applicants must be at least 16 by July 1, 2027. U.S. and permanent-resident applicants can apply, as can international students from participating countries. The 2027 application deadline is December 11, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

name: Stony Brook University Department of Biomedical Informatics
title: Computer Science and Informatics Research Experience (CSIRE)
description: A research-centered summer program in which high school students join active research groups and contribute to original projects in areas such as machine learning, biomedical informatics, medical imaging, natural language processing, data science, human-computer interaction, and computer systems. Students work with faculty and research mentors, develop research questions, conduct computational investigations, and present their findings at a final symposium. Applicants should already have strong programming skills and an understanding of computer science fundamentals. The 2026 cycle is closed; check the official website for the next application cycle, eligibility details, schedule, and program fee.

name: Center for Matter at Atomic Pressures (CMAP)
title: Research Experience for High School Students
description: A summer research experience hosted by the University of Rochester's Center for Matter at Atomic Pressures. The program introduces students to high-energy-density physics, planetary science, and Python through laboratory activities, demonstrations, and practical projects with university researchers. Students are nominated by their high school teachers, and schools across the Greater Rochester area are eligible to participate. This is a distinct opportunity from the university's Laboratory for Laser Energetics high school program. Check the official page for the next cycle's dates, nomination process, and eligibility requirements.

name: Barrow Neurological Institute
title: Summer High School Internship Program
description: A five-week summer internship for high school students aged 16 or older. Participants work part-time in a Barrow laboratory or supporting department under the mentorship of faculty, scientists, clinicians, or managers, with opportunities to participate in research and learn about scientific methods and technology. Applicants interested in laboratory research should review the institute's research groups and identify positions that align with their interests. The published 2027 timeline lists applications opening January 4 and closing February 12, with the internship running June 7 through July 8. Applicants should confirm the available research placements and application instructions on the official page.

name: CU Boulder Science Discovery
title: STEM Research Experience
description: A seven-week, nonresidential summer research program pairing high school students with researchers at CU Boulder or CU Anschutz Medical Campus. Students work on authentic research projects, review scientific literature, collect and analyze data, conduct experiments, and present their findings in a research poster. Past research areas have included aerospace engineering, astrophysics, bioengineering, biology, chemistry, ecology, neuroscience, and medicine. Students must be at least 16 years old by June 2, 2027. The 2027 program is scheduled for June 2 through July 30; applications are expected to open in mid-December 2026 and close March 16, 2027. Housing is not provided, and the program fee is still listed as to be determined.

name: Vanderbilt University Center for Science Outreach
title: Research Experience for High School Students (REHSS)
description: An intensive six-week scientific research internship for eligible students in Vanderbilt's Interdisciplinary Science and Research program. Rising high school seniors are immersed in a Vanderbilt University or Vanderbilt University Medical Center research laboratory and complete an independent project under the mentorship of a research faculty member. This is a targeted pathway rather than a program open to every high school student; prospective applicants should confirm that they are currently enrolled in the qualifying school-based program and check with the Center for Science Outreach for application details and the next cycle's timeline.

name: University of Delaware Department of Computer and Information Sciences
title: Computer and Information Sciences High School Faculty-Lab Research Opportunities
description: The department reports that selected faculty laboratories occasionally host motivated local high school juniors and seniors for summer research internships. Potential project areas include human-computer interaction, cybersecurity, and biomedical data analysis. This is not a single centralized internship with guaranteed placements; students should review the department's research areas and identify faculty whose work matches their interests and skills. The department recommends contacting faculty by email in late winter or early spring with a resume and a brief statement of interest. Availability depends on individual faculty and project capacity.

name: UCLA Brain Research Institute CELL Scholars
title: Cultivating Early Laboratory Learning (CELL Scholars)
description: A school-year research initiative connecting high school students with graduate-student mentors and research opportunities in UCLA bioscience laboratories. Participants develop hands-on laboratory or computational skills, receive career and college guidance, and present their work at a research poster symposium. The program is specifically available to students at University High School in Los Angeles, with scholarship-sponsored research opportunities also described for students from qualifying Title I high schools. Interested eligible students should contact the program directly to ask about openings in the next cycle; participation is not universally open to all high school students.

name: UCSF Science & Health Education Partnership
title: High School Intern Program
description: An eight-week paid summer internship in which high school students conduct original biomedical research under the guidance of a UCSF scientist mentor. The 2027 program is limited to current high school juniors enrolled in a San Francisco Unified School District high school or San Francisco public charter school. The published 2027 timeline lists applications opening January 15 and closing February 15, with the internship scheduled for June 7 through July 30. Students interested in applying should use the official program page to sign up for application notifications and confirm required materials. This is a distinct Science & Health Education Partnership opportunity, not the UCSF CURE internship.

name: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Chemistry and Biochemistry
title: American Chemical Society Project SEED Research Internship
description: A paid summer research internship for high school students interested in chemistry. Participants work on authentic research projects with faculty mentors and graduate students. The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee's 2027 project areas include computational research, biochemistry and drug discovery, environmental and water chemistry, and molecular biophysics or biochemistry. The local program lists dates of June 15 through August 6, 2027, with applications expected to be accepted from February 8 through April 1, 2027 through the national ACS Project SEED application system. Applicants should review national eligibility and financial-need requirements before applying.

name: UT Southwestern Medical Center Krishnan Lab
title: High School Research Opportunities through the Krishnan Lab
university: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
description: The Krishnan Lab's official Join Us page explicitly invites high school students to email about research opportunities. The lab also describes participation by a high school student in an eight-week summer research project through UT Southwestern's STARS program. Students interested in this pathway should read the lab's research description and contact the lab to ask whether a suitable project or mentor is available in the upcoming cycle. Past participation does not guarantee a current opening, and applicants should confirm age, school, safety, and scheduling requirements directly.
